Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "480px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "budget",
  sheets: [
    {
      id: "budget",
      name: "Budget",
      rowCount: 100,
      columns: [
        { key: "item", header: "Item", width: 200, type: "text" },
        { key: "cost", header: "Cost", width: 120, type: "number" },
      ],
    },
  ],
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, config: { ribbon: true } });
console.log(grid.getCommandState("undo").disabled); // true: no history yet
```

## Ribbon

The ribbon has four tabs with Excel's group names, labels and order:

| Tab | Groups and controls |
| --- | --- |
| Home | **Undo**. **Clipboard**: Paste split button. **Font**: font name and size boxes, grow and shrink, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, Borders, Fill Color and Font Color palettes. **Alignment**: top, middle, bottom, wrap, left, center, right, Merge & Center. **Number**: format box, currency, percent, comma, more and fewer decimals. **Cells**: Insert, Delete, Format. **Editing**: AutoSum, Clear, Sort & Filter, Find. |
| Insert | **Rows & Columns**: Insert (rows above or below, columns left or right), Delete (rows or columns). **Links**: link form. **Notes**: note form. |
| Data | **Sort & Filter**: Sort A to Z, Sort Z to A, Clear Filter. **Outline**: Group and Ungroup rows. **Show/Hide**: Hide Rows, Unhide Rows, Hide Columns, Unhide Columns. |
| View | **Window**: Freeze Panes, Freeze Top Row, Freeze First Column, Unfreeze Panes. **Zoom**: zoom out, current percent, zoom in. |

Every control reads the same `getCommandState` contract as host chrome. It disables while the grid is read-only.

### Narrow widths

As the grid narrows, the ribbon shrinks the way Excel does:

1. Large buttons become small ones.
2. Labels go.
3. Whole groups fold into one dropdown button that opens the group in a popup.

Groups fold in Excel order. On Home, Editing folds first, then Cells, Number, Alignment, Clipboard, Font and Undo.

Double-click a tab, or use the arrow at the right, to hide the panel and keep only the tab row. The grid takes the space back.

### Keyboard

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the tab row. The ribbon is first in the host, so keyboard users reach it before the grid. |
| Arrow keys | Move between tabs, and through menus and lists. |
| Enter | Picks a menu or list item. |
| Escape | Returns focus to the grid. |
| Ctrl/Cmd shortcuts | Still reach the grid, for example undo. Plain keys stay in the ribbon. |

### Loading

The ribbon loads with `import()` as its own chunk, only when a grid asks for it. A grid without the ribbon does not download it; that is about 25 KB less minified JavaScript.

- The grid reserves the ribbon's height while the chunk loads, so nothing moves when it arrives.
- A chunk that arrives after the chrome was rebuilt, or after the grid was destroyed, is dropped.
- If the chunk fails to load, the grid shows the flat toolbar. The load error is still reported as an unhandled promise rejection; the host cannot catch it.

### Ribbon outside the grid

The composable shell mounts the same ribbon. Pass `ribbon: true` to `createSpreadsheetShell`, or call [`createRibbon`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core-shell/create-ribbon/) to place it yourself:

```ts
import { createRibbon } from "@sheetwrite/core/shell";

const ribbonHost = document.createElement("div");
host.before(ribbonHost);
const ribbon = createRibbon(ribbonHost, grid, {
  focusGrid: () => host.focus(),
  onHeightChange: (height) => console.log(`ribbon is ${height}px tall`),
});

// During teardown; safe to call twice.
ribbon.destroy();
```

| `RibbonOptions` field | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `focusGrid` | Returns keyboard focus to the grid after a pick or Escape. By default the host gets focus. |
| `onHeightChange` | Called with the new height after the ribbon is minimized or expanded. |

The ribbon styles itself from the same `--sheetwrite-widget-*`, `--sheetwrite-toolbar-*` and `--sheetwrite-menu-*` properties as the toolbar, so light, dark and host themes apply.

## GridConfig (toolbar)

Each flag toggles one control. When `config` is present, every flag except `export` and `ribbon` defaults to `true`. `toolbar: false` suppresses the toolbar entirely.

```ts
createGrid(host, { workbook, config: {} });                 // toolbar with the default controls
createGrid(host, { workbook, config: { sort: false } });    // toolbar, no sort controls
createGrid(host, { workbook, config: { export: true } });   // toolbar with CSV and XLSX buttons
createGrid(host, { workbook, config: { toolbar: false } }); // no toolbar
createGrid(host, { workbook });                             // no toolbar (config omitted)
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `toolbar` | `boolean \| ToolbarItem[]` | `true`¹ | Master switch. `false` removes the toolbar. An item list replaces the default controls. |
| `undo` | `boolean` | `true` | Undo / redo buttons (also bound to Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z). |
| `bold` | `boolean` | `true` | Bold toggle. |
| `italic` | `boolean` | `true` | Italic toggle. |
| `align` | `boolean` | `true` | Left / center / right alignment. |
| `textColor` | `boolean` | `true` | Text color picker. |
| `fillColor` | `boolean` | `true` | Fill (background) color picker. |
| `border` | `boolean` | `true` | Border control. |
| `clearFormat` | `boolean` | `true` | Clear formatting. |
| `merge` | `boolean` | `true` | Merge / unmerge selection. |
| `sort` | `boolean` | `true` | Sort the selected column ascending / descending. |
| `export` | `boolean` | `false` | CSV / XLSX export buttons. |
| `ribbon` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the Excel-style ribbon instead of the flat toolbar. |

¹ "Default `true`" means: when you supply a `config` object at all. With no `config` there is no toolbar.

The underline and strikethrough toggles show when `bold` or `italic` is on.

### Toolbar actions

Every control acts on the current selection; see [Interaction → Selection model](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/#selection-model). A custom `toolbar: ToolbarItem[]` list names built-in actions, separators, or `onClick(grid)` callbacks:

```ts
createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  config: {
    toolbar: [
      { action: "undo" },
      { action: "redo" },
      { action: "separator" },
      { action: "bold" },
      { title: "Clear highlights", icon: "Clear", onClick: (grid) => grid.highlightCells(null) },
    ],
  },
});
```

Built-in action names: `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strikethrough`, `alignLeft`, `alignCenter`, `alignRight`, `alignTop`, `alignMiddle`, `alignBottom`, `wrap`, `textColor`, `fillColor`, `border`, `clearFormat`, `merge`, `unmerge`, `sortAsc`, `sortDesc`, `exportCsv`, `exportXlsx`, `undo`, `redo` and `separator`.

### Export buttons

- The export flag always enables CSV. The XLSX button requires an explicit optional installation and `import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register"` before use. The framework packages do not install an XLSX backend.
- Direct `grid.exportXlsx(...)` calls reject on failure.
- Built-in toolbar and context-menu actions show an alert and emit one `export-error` event for CSV or XLSX failures.
- `grid.actions.exportXlsx()` returns a promise that does not reject.
- Built-in buttons show a busy state and ignore repeated starts while their command is pending.

## Host-owned command state

Host chrome can use `grid.actions` without duplicating selection or history logic. Query one command with `grid.getCommandState(name)`, or subscribe to the complete snapshot through `command-state-change` (`onCommandStateChange` in React and Svelte, `@command-state-change` in Vue):

```ts
const update = (bold: GridCommandState, undo: GridCommandState) => {
  undoButton.disabled = undo.disabled;
  boldButton.disabled = bold.disabled;
  boldButton.setAttribute(
    "aria-pressed",
    bold.activity === "mixed" ? "mixed" : String(bold.activity === "active"),
  );
};

update(grid.getCommandState("bold"), grid.getCommandState("undo"));
const stop = grid.on("command-state-change", ({ states }) => {
  update(states.bold, states.undo);
});

boldButton.addEventListener("click", () => grid.actions.toggleBold());
undoButton.addEventListener("click", () => grid.actions.undo());

// Run during host teardown.
stop();
```

| `GridCommandState` field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `disabled` | Accounts for read-only mode, empty selections, and undo/redo history. |
| `activity` | `"inactive"`, `"active"` or `"mixed"` across the current selection, for formatting commands. |

The built-in toolbar uses the same contract, including native `disabled` and `aria-pressed="mixed"`.

## Feature flags

These `GridConfig` fields enable behavior outside the toolbar row:

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `find` | `boolean` | `true` | Built-in **Ctrl+F** search box, next/previous controls, and live match count. See [Search](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/search/). |
| `contextMenu` | `boolean \| ContextMenuItems` | `true` | Built-in right-click menu, disabled menu, static readonly rows, or a context-aware row factory. See [Context menu](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/context-menu/). |
| `icons` | `Partial<Record<ToolbarActionName, ToolbarIcon>>` | `undefined` | Built-in toolbar icon overrides. Strings render as text; a DOM `Node` or `() => Node` supports SVG/HTML without `innerHTML`. |
| `tabs` | `boolean` | `true` | Bottom sheet-tab bar for multi-sheet workbooks. |
| `keyboard` | `boolean \| KeyboardOptions \| function` | `true` | Built-in key bindings. See [Interaction → Keyboard navigation](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/#keyboard-navigation). |

Undo, redo and find are keyboard-driven and work without the toolbar: **Ctrl+Z** undoes the last edit, **Ctrl+Shift+Z** redoes it, and **Ctrl+F** opens the find widget (unless `find: false`).

## Edge cases and limits

- The per-control flags apply to the flat toolbar only, not to the ribbon.
- A custom `toolbar: [...]` item list still renders the flat toolbar, even with `ribbon: true`.
- `toolbar: false` removes both the toolbar and the ribbon.
- Command-state aggregation is bounded. Very large selections conservatively report `mixed` instead of forcing an unbounded cell walk.
- `grid.setConfig(config)` reconfigures the built-in chrome without replacing the grid or clearing selection and history.

- [Context menu](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/context-menu/)
- [Search](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/search/)
- [Grid methods](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/grid-methods/)
- [Styling → Widget and context-menu styling](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/styles/#widget-and-context-menu-styling)
- Generated [`GridConfig`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid-config/), [`GridActions`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid-actions/), [`GridCommandState`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid-command-state/) and [`createRibbon`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core-shell/create-ribbon/) contracts

### Selection and keyboard

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/

The grid selects cells with the mouse, the keyboard, or code, and runs Sheets-style keyboard shortcuts when it has focus.

```ts
grid.on("selection", (e) => console.log(e.selection));
grid.setSelection({ kind: "cell", addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 } });
console.log(grid.getSelection()); // { kind: "cell", addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 } }
```

| 10 | 30 |
| --- | --- |
| 20 | 40 |

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type ColumnarData, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sheet1",
  sheets: [{
    id: "sheet1",
    name: "Sheet1",
    rowCount: 2,
    columns: [
      { key: "a", header: "A", type: "number", width: 120 },
      { key: "b", header: "B", type: "number", width: 120 },
    ],
  }],
};
const data: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2,
  columns: { a: new Float64Array([10, 20]), b: new Float64Array([30, 40]) },
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, data });
grid.on("selection", (e) => console.log(e.selection));
grid.setSelection({ kind: "cell", addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 } });
console.log(grid.getSelection()); // { kind: "cell", addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 } }

// Later, clear the selection:
grid.setSelection(null);
```

The `selection` listener runs for each change. `getSelection()` returns the current selection, or `null` when nothing is selected. Call `grid.setSelection(null)` to clear it.

The grid makes its host element focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so that it receives keyboard events.

[Try it live → Spreadsheet showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/spreadsheet/)

## Selection model

A `Selection` is one of five shapes:

```ts
type Selection =
  | { kind: "cell"; addr: CellAddress }
  | { kind: "range"; range: Range }
  | { kind: "row"; sheet: SheetId; row: number }
  | { kind: "column"; sheet: SheetId; col: number }
  | { kind: "multi"; ranges: Range[] };
```

How the primary mouse button makes a selection:

| Gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Click a cell | Select that cell. |
| Drag across cells | Extend to a **range**. |
| Shift-click | Extend the range from the current anchor. |
| Ctrl/Cmd-click | Add a region. This makes a **multi** selection. |
| Click a column letter (top header) | Select that **column** (Shift extends; Ctrl/Cmd adds). |

Row and full-column selections are part of the model. The top header selects columns. **Row selection is programmatic only**: there is no row-header click gesture. Set it with `setSelection({ kind: "row", sheet, row })`.

For touch gestures, see [Touch](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/touch/).

## Keyboard navigation

When the grid has focus and is not editing:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Move the focus one cell. |
| Ctrl/Cmd + Arrow | Jump to the first/last row or column. |
| Page Up / Page Down | Move by a viewport of rows. |
| Home / End | Move to the first / last column of the row. |
| Ctrl/Cmd + Home / End | Move to the sheet's first / last cell. |
| Shift + any of the above | Extend the selection instead of moving. |
| Enter or F2 | Edit the focused cell (F2 selects the existing text). |
| Delete / Backspace | Clear the selected cells. |
| A printable character | Start editing, replacing the cell's content. |
| Ctrl/Cmd + C / X / V | Copy / cut / paste. |
| Ctrl/Cmd + Z | Undo the last edit. |
| Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Z (or Ctrl/Cmd + Y) | Redo. |
| Ctrl/Cmd + F | Open the find bar (when `config.find` is not `false`). |

The keys inside the inline editor are on [Editing and clipboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/#inline-editing).

## Rebind an action

Use `config.keyboard.bindings` to replace the keys for one action. Omitted actions keep their defaults. Use `null` to remove an action's keys, or an array for multiple bindings. These bindings apply when the grid has focus and is not editing.

```ts
grid.setConfig({
  keyboard: {
    bindings: {
      copy: "Mod+Shift+C",
      find: { key: "f", mod: true },
      replace: null,
    },
  },
  contextMenu: [
    { action: "copy", label: "Copy value", shortcut: "copy" },
  ],
});
```

The Copy label is `⌘⇧C` on macOS and `Ctrl+Shift+C` elsewhere. Its original Mod+C binding no longer runs Copy. Menu actions use their bound shortcut by default; `shortcut: "copy"` lets a custom item use the same label. Built-in toolbar titles and `grid.getShortcutLabel("copy")` use the same keymap.

### Write a key combination

Write a key combination as a string or as an object:

- A string lists modifiers and then one key: `"Mod+Shift+K"`, `"Ctrl+Alt+Delete"`. The modifiers are `Mod`, `Ctrl`, `Meta`, `Alt` and `Shift`, in any order.
- An object names the key and its modifiers: `{ key: "k", mod: true, shift: true }`. Use the object form for a key without modifiers, for example `{ key: "F2" }`.

`Mod` shows as Command on macOS and as Control on other systems. It accepts either key, so the same shortcut works with a Mac keyboard and a PC keyboard. `Ctrl` and `Meta` are always exactly the Control and Command (or Windows) keys, so `"Ctrl+J"` is Control+J on a Mac too. Shift and Alt must match exactly.

Name the key as printed without Shift: `"Mod+Shift+1"` and `"Mod+Shift+/"` run when the user presses Shift with the 1 or / key, although the browser reports `!` and `?` for those presses. Letters and digits keep their meaning on other keyboard layouts.

## Add a shortcut for your own command

Give a context-menu item a `shortcut` and an `onClick`. The grid then runs `onClick` when the grid has focus and the user presses that combination, with the focused cell as the cell argument. A combination with `Mod`, `Ctrl` or `Meta` also works while the inline editor is open. A hidden or disabled item does not run.

```ts
grid.setConfig({
  contextMenu: [
    {
      id: "open-record",
      label: "Open record",
      shortcut: "Mod+Shift+O",
      onClick: (_grid, cell) => {
        if (cell) console.log("open record for row", cell.row);
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

Pressing Mod+Shift+O logs the focused cell's row.

## Options

| `config.keyboard` value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `true` (default) | The stock bindings in the table above. |
| `{ bindings }` | Replace the keys of the named actions. Omitted actions keep their defaults; `null` removes an action's keys. |
| `false` | Turn off all built-in keys. The host handles every key. |
| `(e, grid) => boolean` | Intercept each keydown before the defaults. Return `true` to consume the key, or `false` to let the built-in handler continue. |

The actions you can rebind are `copy`, `cut`, `paste`, `pasteValues`, `undo`, `redo`, `find`, `replace` and `clearContents`. See [KeyboardOptions](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/keyboard-options/) and [KeyShortcut](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/key-shortcut/).

## Edge cases and limits

- Only the pointer that began a drag can change it. Switching sheets, changing sheet structure or the sorted/filtered view, or losing pointer capture ends the gesture. A later pointer release cannot apply it to a different sheet or view.
- If two commands use the same combination, `createGrid` and `setConfig` throw a `SheetwriteError` with code `shortcut-conflict`, and `setConfig` keeps the previous configuration.
- A malformed combination throws code `invalid-shortcut`.
- `readOnly: true` keeps navigation and selection, but turns off the keys that change cells.

## See also

- [Editing and clipboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/)
- [Resize, merge and fill](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/resize-merge-and-fill/)
- [Status bar](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/status-bar/): totals for the selected cells
- [Context menu](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/context-menu/)
- [`Grid` API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/)

### Editing and clipboard

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/

Users edit cells in place, copy and paste with Excel and Google Sheets, and undo or redo each change.

```ts
grid.on("edit-commit", (e) => console.log("committed", e));
grid.beginEdit(0, 0, "42"); // open the editor on A1 with the text "42"
// The user presses Enter: A1 becomes 42 and the selection moves to A2.
// Later, after the commit:
grid.undo(); // A1 is 10 again
grid.redo(); // A1 is 42 again
```

| 42 | 30 |
| --- | --- |
| 20 | 40 |

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type ColumnarData, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sheet1",
  sheets: [{
    id: "sheet1",
    name: "Sheet1",
    rowCount: 2,
    columns: [
      { key: "a", header: "A", type: "number", width: 120 },
      { key: "b", header: "B", type: "number", width: 120 },
    ],
  }],
};
const data: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2,
  columns: { a: new Float64Array([10, 20]), b: new Float64Array([30, 40]) },
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, data });
grid.on("edit-commit", (e) => console.log("committed", e));
grid.beginEdit(0, 0, "42");
// The user presses Enter: the grid commits A1 and moves down.
// Run these later, after the user commits:
// grid.undo(); // A1 has its old value again
// grid.redo(); // A1 has the committed edit again
```

`beginEdit(row, col, initial?, selectAll?)` opens the editor at a view cell. Enter commits the edit and emits `edit-commit`. `undo()` and `redo()` step through the history.

[Try it live → Spreadsheet showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/spreadsheet/)

## Inline editing

Editing happens in a single real `<textarea>` on top of the active cell. The grid never recycles it across cells, so **IME composition and focus survive scrolling**. Composing CJK text or other input methods is safe. Begin editing by double-clicking, pressing Enter or F2, or just typing.

Commit and navigation keys:

| Key | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Enter | Commit, move **down**. |
| Tab | Commit, move **right**. |
| Shift + Tab | Commit, move **left**. |
| Shift + Enter | Insert a newline (does not commit). |
| Escape | Cancel the edit. |
| Blur (click away) | Commit in place. |

While the IME is composing, keystrokes belong to the composition. The grid does not treat them as navigation. Editing emits `edit-begin` and `edit-commit` events.

### Event order

`beginEdit` closes the previous editor and selects the requested cell. It emits `selection` when that changes the selection, then emits `edit-begin` before it opens the editor. A synchronous handler can replace or cancel the request without the old editor reopening.

Successful completion emits `change`, then `edit-commit`, then the navigation's `selection` event. Rejected completion does not emit `edit-commit` or navigate. Event addresses remain view coordinates.

To supply your own editor, see [Host-supplied editors](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/custom-editors/).

## Clipboard interoperability

Copy and cut always produce injection-hardened TSV. Where the browser exposes `ClipboardItem`, they also write sanitized `text/html` and Sheetwrite's private `application/x-sheetwrite+json` payload. The private payload keeps formula source and cell styles for same-app round trips. The HTML contains only escaped table markup, plain cell text, safe `data-sheetwrite-formula` attributes, and a bounded style subset. No pasted HTML goes into the document.

Paste prefers the private Sheetwrite payload, then sanitized HTML tables, then plain TSV:

- HTML parsing uses an inert `DOMParser` document. It accepts only cell text, safe formula attributes, and supported inline styles.
- External formulas that contain control characters become text.
- TSV handles quoted, multi-line fields, the same as Excel and Google Sheets.
- External text that begins with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab, or CR gets a single-quote prefix, so it cannot become an executable formula.

`paste()` keeps supported formula and style data. `pasteValues()` writes resolved literals and drops formulas and styles on purpose. Cut clears its source only after the system clipboard accepts the payload.

### Report the clipboard outcome

`grid.actions.copy/cut/paste/pasteValues` return `Promise<ClipboardOutcome>` and never reject:

```ts
const outcome = await grid.actions.paste();
if (outcome === "blocked") console.warn("Allow clipboard access to paste.");
```

| Outcome | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"done"` | The action completed. |
| `"unsupported"` | The Clipboard API, or the method it needs, is missing. Examples: a non-secure context, or Firefox `readText`. |
| `"blocked"` | The browser rejected the request, usually because of a permissions policy or missing user activation. |
| `"empty"` | There is nothing to act on: no focused selection, an empty clipboard, or paste on a read-only grid. |

Custom UI can show the outcome without tripping global error monitoring.

## Undo and redo

`grid.undo()` and `grid.redo()` (and Ctrl/Cmd + Z, Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Z) step through the recorded transactions. Remote operations from a `SyncCoordinator` do not create undo entries.

History keeps at most 200 entries and 256 MiB of retained range snapshots, about twenty million-cell clears. When it passes either limit, it drops its oldest entries. The newest entry always stays undoable. The 256 MiB limit counts the snapshot bytes that the engine reports. It is not a limit on total process memory: it excludes cloned formula ASTs and JavaScript patch and redo payloads, which only the 200-entry limit bounds.

### Undo a large clear

Undo of a large clear restores every old cell. The grid restores the saved range directly from its packed engine snapshot. When the restore is larger than one transaction allows, the Grid sends one compressed `restoreBlock` operation. If that still needs more than one server version, it uses an atomic batch, which needs `PersistenceAdapter.commitBatch`. See [Large undo and atomic batches](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/#large-undo-and-atomic-batches).

If the restore is above the batch ceilings, cannot be split, or needs a `commitBatch` that the adapter does not have, `grid.undo()` changes nothing. The Grid emits `mutation-rejected` with a `resource-limit` issue and removes that entry from the history, so older edits can still be undone. Show the reason to the user:

```ts
grid.on("mutation-rejected", ({ issues }) => {
  for (const issue of issues) {
    if (issue.kind === "resource-limit") {
      console.warn(`Not undone: ${issue.resource} ${issue.actual} is above ${issue.max}.`);
    }
  }
});
```

## Options

| Option or method | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `readOnly: true` | Turns off every mutating interaction: editing, clearing, fill, paste, and restyling. Navigation and selection still work. |
| `config.keyboard.bindings` | Rebinds `copy`, `cut`, `paste`, `pasteValues`, `undo` and `redo`. See [Rebind an action](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/#rebind-an-action). |
| `grid.beginEdit(row, col, initial?, selectAll?)` | Opens the editor at a view cell, optionally with seed text or with all text selected. |
| `grid.actions.paste()` / `pasteValues()` | Paste with formulas and styles, or values only. |
| `grid.undo()` / `grid.redo()` | Step back or forward one transaction. |

## Edge cases and limits

- Stock, validation, and custom editors keep the underlying document cell while sorting or filtering changes its visible position. Completion writes that same cell, not the row that now occupies the old position.
- If the edited cell leaves the view, or the sheet structure changes, the grid cancels the editor.
- Paste does nothing when `readOnly` is on; it resolves `"empty"`.
- An undo that is too large to send changes nothing and leaves the history; see [Undo a large clear](#undo-a-large-clear).

## See also

- [Selection and keyboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/)
- [Validation, protection and notes](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/validation-protection-and-notes/): rules that every edit and paste passes through
- [Collaboration](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/)
- [`GridActions` API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid-actions/)

### Custom editors

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/custom-editors/

Set `Column.editor` to a key in `GridOptions.editors`, and Sheetwrite mounts your editor over the active cell.

```ts
const grid = createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  data,
  presentation: "data-grid",
  editors: { status: statusEditor },
});
```

| Ada | Active |
| --- | --- |

Editor example (requires host, workbook and data)

This editor example needs an initialized host, a workbook and data. For the result above, use a text column for the name and a text column with `editor: "status"` for the status, with one row containing `"Ada"` and `"Prospect"`.

```ts
const statusEditor: CellEditor = {
  mount(host, context) {
    const select = document.createElement("select");
    select.setAttribute("aria-label", context.label);
    for (const value of ["Prospect", "Active", "Paused"]) {
      select.add(new Option(value, value));
    }
    select.value = context.text;
    host.appendChild(select);
    select.focus();

    return {
      update(next) {
        select.setAttribute("aria-label", next.label);
        select.value = next.text;
      },
      reposition(rect) {
        select.style.width = `${rect.width}px`;
        select.style.height = `${rect.height}px`;
      },
      commit() {
        return select.value;
      },
      cancel() {},
      destroy() {
        select.remove();
      },
    };
  },
};

const grid = createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  data,
  presentation: "data-grid",
  editors: { status: statusEditor },
});
```

When the user edits a cell in a column with `editor: "status"`, a select list opens over the cell. Picking "Active" and pressing Enter commits `"Active"` and moves down.

## Editor contract

One retained wrapper and one `CellEditorInstance` exist per active edit:

| Hook / value | Guarantee |
| --- | --- |
| `mount(host, context)` | Runs once. The host is positioned over the active cell. |
| `context.address` / `viewAddress` | Canonical data-row and current displayed-row snapshots. They are readonly; mutating a JavaScript object received by the editor cannot retarget the edit. |
| `context.value` / `text` / `initialInput` | Resolved scalar, formatted text, and optional typed character. |
| `context.label` | Accessible name derived from the semantic or positional header plus the row number. |
| `context.signal` | Aborted before the editor's `cancel()` or `destroy()` hook on cancel, commit, reset, or unmount. |
| `context.commit()` / `cancel()` | Optional editor-driven completion using the canonical path. A non-string commit from untyped JavaScript cancels safely. |
| `update(context)` | External value, theme, zoom, view permutation, or geometry-sensitive state changed without replacing ownership. |
| `reposition(rect)` | The active cell moved or resized. |
| `commit()` | May return input synchronously or asynchronously; duplicate completion is ignored. |
| `cancel()` | Notification before a host-requested cancellation; the signal is already aborted. |
| `destroy()` | Runs exactly once; late async work must observe the aborted signal. A thrown hook error is reported without interrupting Sheetwrite's DOM, listener, or store cleanup. |

The returned value is parsed with the column's normal type. It commits through the same document transaction as stock editing. That preserves protection, validation, mutation policy, undo/redo, change events, and edit-commit events.

Keys inside the editor:

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Enter | Commit and move down. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Commit and move horizontally. |
| Escape | Cancel. |

Focus returns to the grid after commit or cancel.

## Asynchronous editors

For remote choices, use the editor-owned `AbortSignal`. Never let a late request write into a destroyed editor:

```ts
const assigneeAutocomplete: CellEditor = {
  mount(host, context) {
    const input = document.createElement("input");
    const list = document.createElement("datalist");
    list.id = `assignees-${context.address.row}-${context.address.col}`;
    input.setAttribute("list", list.id);
    input.setAttribute("role", "combobox");
    input.setAttribute("aria-label", context.label);
    input.value = context.initialInput ?? context.text;
    host.append(input, list);
    input.focus();

    void fetch(`/api/people?q=${encodeURIComponent(input.value)}`, {
      signal: context.signal,
    })
      .then((response) => response.json() as Promise<Array<{ id: string; name: string }>>)
      .then((people) => {
        if (context.signal.aborted) return;
        list.replaceChildren(
          ...people.map((person) => {
            const option = document.createElement("option");
            option.value = person.name;
            option.dataset.id = person.id;
            return option;
          }),
        );
      })
      .catch((error: unknown) => {
        if (!(error instanceof DOMException && error.name === "AbortError")) throw error;
      });

    return {
      update(next) {
        input.setAttribute("aria-label", next.label);
      },
      reposition(rect) {
        input.style.width = `${rect.width}px`;
      },
      async commit() {
        await Promise.resolve();
        return input.value;
      },
      cancel() {},
      destroy() {
        input.remove();
        list.remove();
      },
    };
  },
};
```

An asynchronous commit stays bound to the data row captured at `mount`. This holds even when sorting or `clearView()` moves that row before the promise settles.

## Framework adapters

`editors` is construction-bound, so React, Vue and Svelte resets safely abort and destroy an active editor before they publish the new grid generation. All adapters accept the same registry:

```tsx
<SheetwriteGrid
  ref={gridRef}
  workbook={workbook}
  data={data}
  presentation="data-grid"
  editors={{ status: statusEditor, assignee: assigneeAutocomplete }}
  onCommandStateChange={({ states }) => setCommandStates(states)}
/>
```

```vue
<SheetwriteGrid
  ref="gridComponent"
  :workbook="workbook"
  :data="data"
  presentation="data-grid"
  :editors="{ status: statusEditor, assignee: assigneeAutocomplete }"
  @command-state-change="({ states }) => commandStates = states"
/>
```

```svelte
<SheetwriteGrid
  bind:grid
  {workbook}
  {data}
  presentation="data-grid"
  editors={{ status: statusEditor, assignee: assigneeAutocomplete }}
  onCommandStateChange={(event: GridEvents["command-state-change"]) => commandStates = event.states}
/>
```

## Edge cases and limits

- A custom editor takes precedence over the built-in validation-list editor.
- If the `Column.editor` key is not in `editors`, Sheetwrite falls back to validation editing or its stock text/date editor.
- If a filter removes the row from the view while an async commit is pending, Sheetwrite cancels and aborts the edit. It does not retarget another row.
- A rejected promise, `undefined`, or a non-string value from untyped JavaScript cancels without a mutation.

- [Grid options and presentation](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/options-and-presentation/)
- [Interaction → Inline editing](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/#inline-editing)
- Generated [`CellEditor`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/cell-editor/), [`CellEditorContext`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/cell-editor-context/) and [`CellEditorInstance`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/cell-editor-instance/) contracts

### Resize, merge and fill

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/resize-merge-and-fill/

Users drag header boundaries to resize, merge a range into one cell, and drag the fill handle to repeat cells; code can do the first two through the `Grid`.

```ts
grid.setColumnWidth(0, 160); // one undoable size change
grid.setSelection({
  kind: "range",
  range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 0, col: 1 } },
});
grid.actions.merge(); // A1:B1 is now one cell that shows A1's value
```

10
2040

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type ColumnarData, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sheet1",
  sheets: [{
    id: "sheet1",
    name: "Sheet1",
    rowCount: 4,
    columns: [
      { key: "a", header: "A", type: "number", width: 120 },
      { key: "b", header: "B", type: "number", width: 120 },
    ],
  }],
};
const data: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 4,
  columns: { a: new Float64Array([10, 20, 0, 0]), b: new Float64Array([30, 40, 0, 0]) },
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, data });
grid.setColumnWidth(0, 160);
grid.setSelection({
  kind: "range",
  range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 0, col: 1 } },
});
grid.actions.merge();
// Later, make A1 and B1 separate again:
// grid.actions.unmerge();
```

Column A is 160 px wide. After `merge()`, A1's value spans both columns and B1 is hidden. Call `grid.actions.unmerge()` to separate them again.

[Try it live → Spreadsheet showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/spreadsheet/)

## Resizing

Drag a column-header boundary or a row-header boundary to preview its size. The preview changes geometry only: the document and undo history stay the same until release. Release submits one undoable size change. Cancellation, capture loss, or a rejected change restores the document's size. Turning read-only on ends an active resize without committing.

## Merged cells

Merging combines the selected range into one cell. The top-left value shows, and the covered cells are hidden. A per-sheet merge registry tracks them. Unmerge reverses it.

## Drag-to-fill

A small fill handle sits at the bottom-right corner of the selection. Drag it **down, up, left, or right** to fill the source block across the new region. The dominant axis wins. The grid tiles (repeats) the source to cover the target.

For example, after unmerging, select A1:B2 from Full setup and drag the fill handle down through row 4. The source repeats; it does not become a numeric series:

| 10 | 30 |
| --- | --- |
| 20 | 40 |
| 10 | 30 |
| 20 | 40 |

When the filled cells contain formulas, the grid rewrites references as it copies them: **relative** A1 parts shift by the fill offset, and **absolute** parts (prefixed with `$`) stay fixed.

| Source formula | Fill direction | Filled formula |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `=A1 + $B$1` | One column right | `=B1 + $B$1` |

See [Formulas → Point mode and reference rewriting](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/authoring-and-references/#point-mode-and-reference-rewriting).

## Options

| API | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `grid.setColumnWidth(col, width)` | Set one column's width with an undoable `setColumn` patch. |
| `grid.setRowHeight(row, height)` | Set one row's persistent display height through document history. |
| `grid.actions.merge()` / `grid.actions.unmerge()` | Merge or unmerge the selection. |
| `grid.actions.mergeAndCenter()` | Merge the selection and center its text, as one undoable step. |
| `readOnly: true` | Turns off drag-to-fill and resizing, including double-click autofit. Turning it on ends an active resize without committing. |

## Edge cases and limits

- Merges are **not drawn while a sort or filter view is active**, because the display order no longer maps cleanly to the merged region. Clear the view to see them again. See [Data operations](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/data-operations/#display-views).
- Drag-to-fill is unavailable while a sort or filter view is active (the handle is hidden). When `readOnly` is on, the handle still shows, but a fill changes nothing.
- A resize preview does not change the document. Only the release commits.

## See also

- [Selection and keyboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/)
- [Touch](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/touch/): resize and fill on a touch screen
- [Editing and clipboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/#undo-and-redo)
- [`Grid` API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/)

### Context menu

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/context-menu/

`GridConfig.contextMenu` turns the built-in right-click menu on or off, or replaces its rows with a static list or a context-aware factory.

```ts
declare const config: GridConfig;
grid.setConfig(config);
// Right-click a cell, then choose Inspect cell to log its stored value.
```

| Ada |
| --- |

Copy valueCtrl+C

Inspect cell
Download CSV

Result: right-clicking Ada opens these three menu rows, with a separator after Copy value. The cell value is unchanged. Static preview; the copy shortcut is shown for Windows/Linux.

Configuration example (requires an initialized grid)

This configuration excerpt needs an initialized grid. For the result above, use a sheet with `"Ada"` in A1, then pass `config` to `createGrid` or call `grid.setConfig(config)`.

```ts
const config = {
  contextMenu: (context) => [
    { id: "copy", action: "copy", label: "Copy value", shortcut: "copy" },
    { action: "separator" },
    {
      id: "inspect",
      label: "Inspect cell",
      visible: context.cell !== null,
      disabled: ({ cell }) => cell === null,
      onClick(grid, cell) {
        if (cell !== null) console.log(grid.store.getCell(cell));
      },
    },
    { action: "exportCsv", label: "Download CSV" },
  ],
} satisfies GridConfig;
```

A right-click on a cell shows three rows: **Copy value**, **Inspect cell** and **Download CSV**. When the pointer resolves no cell, **Inspect cell** is hidden.

## How the bundled menu works

On a right-click, Sheetwrite prevents the browser menu, hit-tests the pointer, and selects the resolved cell. Then it evaluates each item's `visible` and `disabled` policy.

## Menu items

`ContextMenuItems` is either a `readonly ContextMenuItem[]` or a factory evaluated for each `ContextMenuContext`.

| `contextMenu` value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `true` (default) | The default menu. |
| `false` | No bundled menu. |
| `readonly ContextMenuItem[]` | Static readonly rows. |
| `(context) => ContextMenuItem[]` | Rows built for each right-click context. |

| Item field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Stable row id. |
| `action` | A built-in action name (below). |
| `label` | Visible text. |
| `shortcut` | Shortcut hint. |
| `visible` / `disabled` | A boolean, or a predicate that receives the lean `ContextMenuContext`. |
| `onClick(grid, cell)` | Host callback. It overrides `action`. |

The lean `ContextMenuContext` carries only `cell`, `clientX`, and `clientY`.

The built-in action names are:

| Clipboard/content | Rows | Columns | View/export |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cut`, `copy`, `paste`, `clearContents` | `insertRowAbove`, `insertRowBelow`, `deleteRow`, `hideRow`, `showAllRows`, `autoFitRow` | `insertColumnLeft`, `insertColumnRight`, `deleteColumn`, `hideColumn`, `showAllColumns`, `autoFitColumn` | `clearFilter`, `merge`, `unmerge`, `exportCsv`, `exportXlsx` |

The default menu contains copy, cut, paste, clear contents, row insert/delete/hide/show/auto-fit, column insert/delete/hide/show/auto-fit, clear column filter, merge, and unmerge actions, with separators between groups. `exportCsv` and `exportXlsx` are not in the default menu, but you can use them in a custom list. XLSX still requires `@sheetwrite/xlsx/register`.

## Host-owned menu

For fully host-owned UI, set `contextMenu: false` and bind the DOM `contextmenu` event on the host. `grid.getCellAtPoint(event.clientX, event.clientY)` resolves the pointer without exposing renderer internals. The host then owns `preventDefault`, selection, positioning, dismissal, and calls to `grid.actions`. Sheetwrite does not prescribe the host's event lifecycle:

```ts
host.addEventListener("contextmenu", (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const cell = grid.getCellAtPoint(event.clientX, event.clientY);
  if (cell !== null) grid.setSelection({ kind: "cell", addr: cell });
  host.dispatchEvent(
    new CustomEvent("sheetwrite:context-menu", {
      detail: { cell, x: event.clientX, y: event.clientY, actions: grid.actions },
    }),
  );
});
```

## Temporary highlights

`grid.highlightCells(ranges, color?)` draws an overlay, not a document edit. Pass `null` to clear all temporary highlights. `color` overrides the theme highlight color; a range can also carry its own `color`.

```ts
const sheet = grid.getActiveSheet();
grid.highlightCells(
  [{ sheet, start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 2, col: 1 } }],
  "#ffe08a",
);
// later
grid.highlightCells(null);
```

- Undo does not clear a highlight.
- Choose a distinct overlay color, so users can tell it from selection and cell formatting.
- Use `grid.styleRange` when a fill must be saved and undoable.

The Vanilla workbench offers **Clear highlight** in its context menu. Right-click the highlighted cell to toggle it off, or right-click another cell and choose **Clear highlight**. Both actions write to the host event log.

## Edge cases and limits

- Hidden separators are normalized.
- Disabled rows cannot invoke actions.
- Built-in export actions show an alert and emit one `export-error` event on failure.

## See also

- [Toolbar and ribbon → Feature flags](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/toolbar-and-ribbon/#feature-flags)
- [Styling → Widget and context-menu styling](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/styles/#widget-and-context-menu-styling) for the bundled menu CSS hooks
- Generated [`ContextMenuContext`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/context-menu-context/), [`ContextMenuItems`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/context-menu-items/), [`ContextMenuItem`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/context-menu-item/), and [`Grid.getCellAtPoint`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-get-cell-at-point) contracts

### Search

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/search/

`grid.search(query, opts?)` scans cells, highlights every match, scrolls the first match into view, and emits a [`search`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/events/#grid-events) event.

```ts
const result = grid.search("error");
console.log(`${result.matches.length} match(es)`); // "2 match(es)"
```

error
1 of 2
↑ Previous
↓ Next
✕ Close

Replace with
Replace
All

| Log | Message | Source | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Job 1 | error | Import | Invalid file |
| Job 2 | OK | Import | Complete |
| Job 3 | OK | Export | Complete |
| Job 4 | OK | Import | Complete |
| Job 5 | OK | Export | Complete |
| Job 6 | Failed | Export | error |

Result: B2 is the active match and D7 is also highlighted; values are unchanged. The static controls show the equivalent Ctrl+F view after entering “error”; calling `grid.search` alone does not open the widget.

Usage example (requires an initialized grid)

This API excerpt needs an initialized grid. Populate its first seven rows with the log cells above, using plain `"error"` in B2 and D7. The final call clears the search highlights, not the values.

```ts
const result = grid.search("error");
console.log(`${result.matches.length} match(es)`);
grid.findNext();    // advance the active match and scroll to it
grid.clearSearch(); // remove the highlights when done
```

If cells B2 and D7 contain "error", the log shows `2 match(es)`. `result.matches` is `[B2, D7]` as zero-based addresses, and `result.active` is `0`.

`findNext()` and `findPrev()` move the active match. `clearSearch()` clears the highlights. The built-in **Ctrl+F** find widget, gated by `config.find` (on by default), drives this same API.

## Options and result

```ts
interface SearchOptions {
  matchCase?: boolean; // case-sensitive match (default false)
  wholeCell?: boolean; // match the whole cell, not a substring (default false)
  sheet?: SheetId;     // restrict to one sheet (default: the active sheet)
  columns?: number[];  // restrict to these column indices (default: all)
}

interface SearchResult {
  query: string;
  matches: CellAddress[]; // matching cells, in row-major order
  active: number;         // index of the active match, or -1 when there are none
}
```

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `search(query, opts?)` | Find matching cells; highlights them, emits `search`, returns a `SearchResult`. |
| `findNext()` / `findPrev()` | Step the active match forward / backward and scroll it into view. |
| `clearSearch()` | Drop the current search and clear its highlights. |
| `replaceCurrent(replacement)` / `replaceAll(replacement)` | Replace literal text/number matches through undoable transactions. |

## Edge cases and limits

- An active search picks up matches that a value edit adds or removes, without scrolling.
- On sheets with formulas or references, an active search rescans after each edit, including edits to off-screen inputs or other sheets. This keeps matches whose computed text changes.
- `highlightCells(ranges, color?)` highlights arbitrary ranges independently of search. Pass `null` to clear; `color` overrides the theme highlight color. See [Temporary highlights](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/context-menu/#temporary-highlights).
- Set `config.find: false` to turn off the Ctrl+F widget. The methods still work.

## See also

- [Toolbar and ribbon → Feature flags](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/toolbar-and-ribbon/#feature-flags)
- [Grid methods](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/grid-methods/#selection-editing-and-search)
- [Events](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/events/)
- Generated [`SearchOptions`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/search-options/), [`SearchResult`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/search-result/) and [`ReplaceResult`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/replace-result/) contracts

### Status bar

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/status-bar/

The status bar shows Excel's Average, Count and Sum for the selected cells, next to the size of the selection.

```ts
import type { createSpreadsheetShell } from "@sheetwrite/core/shell";
declare const shell: ReturnType<typeof createSpreadsheetShell>;

shell.grid.setSelection({
  kind: "range",
  range: { sheet: "sales", start: { row: 0, col: 1 }, end: { row: 2, col: 1 } },
});
```

| Notebook | 12 |
| --- | ---: |
| Pen | 4 |
| Folder | 8 |

Sales
Average: 8 · Count: 3 · Sum: 24 · 3 × 1 cells

Result: selecting the amounts in B1:B3 shows the selection totals and size in the shell's bottom status bar.

Full setup

```ts
import { initSheetwrite, type ColumnarData, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import { createSpreadsheetShell } from "@sheetwrite/core/shell";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";
import "@sheetwrite/core/shell.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#app");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #app host");
host.style.height = "480px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sales",
  sheets: [
    {
      id: "sales",
      name: "Sales",
      rowCount: 3,
      columns: [
        { key: "product", header: "Product", width: 180, type: "text" },
        { key: "amount", header: "Amount", width: 100, type: "number" },
      ],
    },
  ],
};
const data: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 3,
  columns: {
    product: ["Notebook", "Pen", "Folder"],
    amount: new Float64Array([12, 4, 8]),
  },
};

await initSheetwrite();
const shell = createSpreadsheetShell(host, { grid: { workbook, data } });

// Select B1:B3, the three amounts.
shell.grid.setSelection({
  kind: "range",
  range: { sheet: "sales", start: { row: 0, col: 1 }, end: { row: 2, col: 1 } },
});
```

The status line at the bottom of the shell reads `Average: 8 · Count: 3 · Sum: 24 · 3 × 1 cells`.

## Turn it on

`createSpreadsheetShell` always adds the status bar to its bottom row, next to the sheet tabs. There is no flag to turn it on.

To use it with a grid that you created yourself, for example the `Grid` from a framework adapter, mount the piece into your own element:

```ts
import { createSelectionStatus } from "@sheetwrite/core/shell";

const statusHost = document.createElement("div");
host.after(statusHost);

const status = createSelectionStatus(statusHost, grid);
// Later, when the grid goes away:
status.destroy();
```

`createSelectionStatus(host, grid)` appends an `<output role="status">` with the class `sheetwrite-shell-status` to `host` and returns a `ShellPiece`: `element` is the `<output>`, and `destroy()` removes it and stops its listeners. Import `@sheetwrite/core/shell.css` for the shell styles.

## What it shows

| Part | When it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Average | Two or more selected cells hold values, and at least one of them is a number. |
| Count | Two or more selected cells hold values. Text and errors count. |
| Sum | Two or more selected cells hold values, and at least one of them is a number. |
| Selection size | A range shows `rows × columns cells`, a row shows `Row n`, a column shows `Column n`, and a multi selection shows `n ranges`. A single cell shows nothing. |

The parts are joined with ` · `. When there is nothing to show, the `<output>` is hidden, and so is its host when the status bar is the host's only child.

The status bar updates on each `selection` and `change` event. It is a polite live region, so screen readers announce changes without interrupting the user.

## Read the totals yourself

`grid.summarizeSelection(signal?)` returns the totals that the status bar uses. Use it to build your own status bar, or to show Min and Max.

```ts
let pending: AbortController | null = null;

grid.on("selection", async () => {
  pending?.abort();
  const controller = new AbortController();
  pending = controller;
  try {
    const summary = await grid.summarizeSelection(controller.signal);
    if (summary === null || summary.numericCount === 0) return;
    console.log(`Min: ${summary.min} · Max: ${summary.max}`);
  } catch (error) {
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) throw error;
  }
});
```

With B1:B3 from the first example selected, this logs `Min: 4 · Max: 12`.

## Options

`createSelectionStatus` and `createSpreadsheetShell` have no status bar options. These are the fields of the `SelectionSummary` that `summarizeSelection` resolves:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `number` | Cells that hold any value, including text and errors. |
| `numericCount` | `number` | Cells that hold a number. Dates are numbers too. |
| `sum` | `number` | Sum of the numeric cells. |
| `average` | `number \| null` | Mean of the numeric cells; `null` when there are none. |
| `min` | `number \| null` | Smallest number; `null` when there are none. |
| `max` | `number \| null` | Largest number; `null` when there are none. |

`summarizeSelection` resolves `null` when nothing is selected.

## Edge cases and limits

- The totals cover only the cells the user can see. Rows that a filter hides are left out.
- Overlapping ranges in a multi selection count once per range, as in Excel.
- Whole-row selections stop at the last column; there are no cells past it.
- Large selections are read in chunks of 65,536 cells, with a pause between frames, so the page stays responsive. In one measurement, 4 million cells took about 160 ms in total and at most 10 ms per chunk.
- Abort the `signal` to stop early. The promise then rejects with the signal's reason. The status bar aborts an unfinished summary when the selection or the data changes.
- The totals use the selection and the active sheet as they were when the call started.

## See also

- [Selection and keyboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/)
- [`createSelectionStatus` API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core-shell/create-selection-status/)
- [`createSpreadsheetShell` API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core-shell/create-spreadsheet-shell/)
- [`Grid.summarizeSelection` API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-summarize-selection)

### Touch

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/touch/

The grid reads all input through Pointer Events, so mouse, touch, and pen share one code path, and a plain drag on touch scrolls the page natively.

```ts
grid.on("selection", (e) => console.log("tap selected", e.selection));
grid.on("edit-begin", (e) => console.log("double-tap edits", e));
// On a touch screen, tap A1 to select it; double-tap to edit.
```

| 10 | 30 |
| --- | --- |
| 20 | 40 |

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type ColumnarData, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sheet1",
  sheets: [{
    id: "sheet1",
    name: "Sheet1",
    rowCount: 2,
    columns: [
      { key: "a", header: "A", type: "number", width: 120 },
      { key: "b", header: "B", type: "number", width: 120 },
    ],
  }],
};
const data: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2,
  columns: { a: new Float64Array([10, 20]), b: new Float64Array([30, 40]) },
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, data });
grid.on("selection", (e) => console.log("tap selected", e.selection));
grid.on("edit-begin", (e) => console.log("double-tap edits", e));
```

On a touch screen, a tap on a cell logs `tap selected`. A double-tap on a cell logs `double-tap edits`. A drag across plain cells logs nothing, because it scrolls.

## Touch gestures

For `pointerType: "touch"` the policy is:

| Gesture | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Tap on a cell | Select the cell (same as a click). |
| Tap on a column header | Select the column. |
| Drag starting on a plain cell | **Native scroll**. The grid neither captures the pointer nor calls `preventDefault`. |
| Drag starting on the fill handle | Drag-to-fill (pointer captured). |
| Drag starting on a row/column resize boundary | Resize (pointer captured). |
| Drag starting on the border of a multi-cell selection (±6px band) | Extend the selection (pointer captured). |
| Double-tap on a cell | Begin editing (the browser's synthesized `dblclick`). |

## Mouse and pen

Mouse and pen behave classically: any drag from a cell extends the selection, and hovering a resize boundary shows the resize cursor.

## Options

Touch has no options of its own. The gestures above follow the same settings as the mouse: for example, `readOnly: true` turns off drag-to-fill, and an active sort or filter view hides the fill handle.

## Edge cases and limits

- A `pointercancel` (for example, when the browser reclaims the gesture) abandons the drag without committing.
- The scroller sets `touch-action: pan-x pan-y`. This keeps native panning, but disables double-tap zoom so that captured drags keep receiving `pointermove`.
- Long-press to open the context menu on touch is deferred. When it is added, it must cancel on move to respect the native-scroll rule.

## See also

- [Selection and keyboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/#selection-model)
- [Resize, merge and fill](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/resize-merge-and-fill/)
- [Accessibility](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/accessibility/)

### Grid methods

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/grid-methods/

`createGrid` returns an imperative `Grid` handle. Use it to read and change the document, the selection, the view and the layout.

```ts
const sheet = grid.getActiveSheet();
grid.setSelection({ kind: "cell", addr: { sheet, row: 0, col: 1 } });
grid.sortBy(1, false);  // display-only sort, largest first
grid.setFrozen(1);      // pin the first view row
grid.setZoom(1.25);
console.log(grid.getZoom()); // 1.25
const off = grid.on("selection", ({ selection }) => console.log(selection));
// later
off();
```

| Desk | 300 |
| --- | --- |
| Chair | 120 |
| Lamp | 40 |

Usage example (requires an initialized grid)

This API excerpt needs an initialized grid with a text item column and a numeric cost column. Use these data rows in order: Lamp / 40, Desk / 300, Chair / 120. There is no header row in the cell data.

```ts
const sheet = grid.getActiveSheet();
grid.setSelection({ kind: "cell", addr: { sheet, row: 0, col: 1 } });
grid.sortBy(1, false);  // display-only sort, largest first
grid.setFrozen(1);      // pin the first view row
grid.setZoom(1.25);
console.log(grid.getZoom()); // 1.25
const off = grid.on("selection", ({ selection }) => console.log(selection));
// later
off();
```

The grid shows column B sorted from largest to smallest, the first row stays in place while the body scrolls, and content is drawn at 125%.

Each name in the tables links to its entry in the [`Grid` API reference](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/). These are the signatures of the methods on this page:

```ts
interface Grid {
  readonly store: Store;
  readonly actions: GridActions;
  setActiveSheet(id: SheetId): void;
  scrollToCell(addr: CellAddress): void;
  getSelection(): Selection | null;
  setSelection(sel: Selection | null): void;
  setTheme(theme: Partial<Theme>): void;
  defineCellRenderer(name: string, renderer: CellRenderer): void;
  aggregate(col: number, op: AggregateOp): number;
  sortBy(col: number, ascending?: boolean): void;
  sortByMulti(keys: readonly SortKey[]): void;
  filterBy(col: number, needle: string): void;
  setColumnFilter(col: number, filter: ColumnFilter | null): void;
  getColumnFilters(): ReadonlyMap<number, ColumnFilter>;
  distinctValues(col: number, limit?: number): CellScalar[];
  hideRows(rows: readonly number[]): void;
  showRows(rows?: readonly number[]): void;
  hiddenRows(): readonly number[];
  hideColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void;
  showColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void;
  hiddenColumns(): readonly number[];
  groupRows(start: number, end: number): void;
  ungroupRows(start: number, end: number): void;
  setGroupCollapsed(start: number, collapsed: boolean): void;
  rowGroups(): readonly RowGroup[];
  clearView(): void;
  undo(): void;
  redo(): void;
  exportCsv(filename: string): void;
  exportXlsx(filename: string): Promise<void>;
  search(query: string, opts?: SearchOptions): SearchResult;
  findNext(): SearchResult;
  findPrev(): SearchResult;
  clearSearch(): void;
  replaceCurrent(replacement: string): SearchResult;
  replaceAll(replacement: string): ReplaceResult;
  insertRows(at: number, count?: number): void;
  removeRows(at: number, count?: number): void;
  insertColumns(at: number, count?: number): void;
  removeColumns(at: number, count?: number): void;
  highlightCells(ranges: readonly HighlightRange[] | null, color?: string): void;
  styleRange(range: Range, style: Partial<CellStyle> | null): void;
  setValidationRule(rule: DataValidationRule): ApplyTransactionResult;
  removeValidationRule(id: string): ApplyTransactionResult;
  setProtectedRange(range: ProtectedRange): ApplyTransactionResult;
  removeProtectedRange(id: string): ApplyTransactionResult;
  setProtectionResolver(resolver?: ProtectionResolver, mode?: MutationPolicyMode): void;
  setNote(addr: CellAddress, text: string | null): ApplyTransactionResult;
  getNote(addr: CellAddress): string | null;
  beginEdit(row: number, col: number, initial?: string, selectAll?: boolean): void;
  dataEdge(row: number, col: number, dRow: number, dCol: number): number | null;
  setRowHeight(row: number, height: number): void;
  setColumnWidth(col: number, width: number): void;
  autoFitRows(range?: Range): void;
  autoFitColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void;
  setFrozen(rows: number, cols?: number): void;
  setZoom(zoom: number): void;
  getZoom(): number;
  on<E extends keyof GridEvents>(evt: E, fn: (e: GridEvents[E]) => void): () => void;
  refresh(): void;
  destroy(): void;
  // Also covered under "Other methods" below:
  applyTransaction(transaction: GridTransaction): ApplyTransactionResult;
  exportSnapshot(): WorkbookSnapshot;
  applyRemoteOperations(operations: readonly DocumentOp[], options?: RemoteOperationOptions): ApplyTransactionResult;
  getCommandState(command: GridCommandName): GridCommandState;
  getFocusCellStyle(): CellStyle;
  getCellAtPoint(clientX: number, clientY: number): CellAddress | null;
  setConfig(config: GridConfig | undefined): void;
  setReadOnly(readOnly: boolean): void;
}
```

## Document and sheets

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`store`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-store) | The underlying [`Store`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/runtime-ownership/#the-store-contract): apply transactions, read cells, subscribe. |
| [`actions`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-actions) | Imperative action surface (`toggleBold()`, `merge()`, `undo()`, `exportCsv()`, …) the toolbar and context menu bind to. Use it to wire custom controls. |
| [`setActiveSheet(id)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-set-active-sheet) | Switch the visible sheet. |
| [`undo()`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-undo) / [`redo()`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-redo) | Undo or redo the last recorded cell edit (also bound to Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z). |
| [`insertRows(at, count?)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-insert-rows) / `removeRows(at, count?)` / `insertColumns(at, count?)` / `removeColumns(at, count?)` | Structural edits through undoable patches. |
| [`styleRange(range, style)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-style-range) | Merge or clear (`null`) store-backed cell styles across a range. |
| [`setValidationRule(rule)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-set-validation-rule) / `removeValidationRule(id)` | Add, replace, or remove a serializable range validation rule. List and checkbox rules get accessible editors. |
| [`setProtectedRange(range)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-set-protected-range) / `removeProtectedRange(id)` / `setProtectionResolver(resolver?, mode?)` | Define protected-range metadata and host-owned local permission policy. This is not server authorization. |
| [`setNote(addr, text)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-set-note) / `getNote(addr)` | Set, clear (`null`), or read a serializable plain-text cell note. |
| [`exportCsv(filename)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-export-csv) / `exportXlsx(filename)` | Download the active data; `exportXlsx` returns a promise. See [Data operations](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#errors-and-built-in-actions). |

## Selection, editing and search

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`getSelection()`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-get-selection) / `setSelection(sel)` | Read or set the current [`Selection`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/#selection-model) (`null` clears it). |
| [`scrollToCell(addr)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-scroll-to-cell) | Scroll a cell into view. |
| [`beginEdit(row, col, initial?, selectAll?)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-begin-edit) | Open the inline editor at a view cell. |
| [`dataEdge(row, col, dRow, dCol)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-data-edge) | Ctrl+Arrow-style data-run jump target, or `null`; vertical movement is view-aware under sort/filter. |
| [`search(query, opts?)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-search) | Find matching cells; highlights them, emits `search`, returns a [`SearchResult`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/search/#options-and-result). |
| [`findNext()`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-find-next) / `findPrev()` | Step the active match forward / backward and scroll it into view. |
| [`clearSearch()`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-clear-search) | Drop the current search and clear its highlights. |
| [`replaceCurrent(replacement)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-replace-current) / `replaceAll(replacement)` | Replace literal text/number matches through undoable transactions. |
| [`highlightCells(ranges, color?)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-highlight-cells) | Highlight arbitrary ranges (`null` clears); `color` overrides the theme highlight. |

## Views: sort, filter, hide and group

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |

| [`sortBy(col, ascending?)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-sort-by) / `sortByMulti(keys)` | Non-mutating display sorts; see [Data operations](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/data-operations/#display-views). |
| [`filterBy(col, needle)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-filter-by) / `setColumnFilter(col, filter)` / `getColumnFilters()` | Column filters that compose with sort, hidden rows, and row groups. `setColumnFilter(col, null)` removes one. |
| [`distinctValues(col, limit?)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-distinct-values) | First-seen distinct values for building filter menus. |

| [`hideColumns(cols?)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-hide-columns) / `showColumns(cols?)` / `hiddenColumns()` | Bulk-safe persisted column visibility; omitted arguments target the focused column for hide and every column for show. |
| [`groupRows(start, end)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-group-rows) / `ungroupRows(start, end)` / `setGroupCollapsed(start, collapsed)` / `rowGroups()` | Inclusive data-row groups with collapse state. |
| [`clearView()`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-clear-view) | Clears sort/filter state; hidden rows and row groups remain. |

| [`getCommandState(name)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-get-command-state) | Undo/redo availability and formatting active/mixed/disabled state. See [Host-owned command state](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/toolbar-and-ribbon/#host-owned-command-state). |
| [`getFocusCellStyle()`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-get-focus-cell-style) | Effective style of the focus cell: its own style over its column's `cellStyle`. |
| [`getCellAtPoint(clientX, clientY)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-get-cell-at-point) | Resolve viewport coordinates to an active-sheet cell for [host-owned menus](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/context-menu/#host-owned-menu). |
| [`setConfig(config)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-set-config) / [`setReadOnly(readOnly)`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#grid-set-read-only) | Reconfigure built-in chrome, or change editability, without replacing the grid. |

## Edge cases and limits

- Undo history keeps at most 200 entries. It also drops its oldest entries once retained range snapshots pass 256 MiB, about twenty million-cell clears. The newest entry always stays undoable.
- The 256 MiB policy counts engine-reported snapshot bytes, not total process memory. Cloned formula ASTs and JavaScript patch/redo payloads are bounded only by the 200-entry limit.
- Undo of a large clear restores the saved range directly from a packed engine snapshot.
- Display sorts and filters do not change the document. `clearView()` keeps hidden rows and row groups.

### Formatting

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/
