- [Fonts and alignment](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/fonts-and-alignment/): Set the font family, size, emphasis, horizontal and vertical alignment, and text wrap of cells.
- [Number formats](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/number-formats/): Show numbers and dates with Excel-style format codes and an explicit locale.
- [Conditional formats](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/conditional-formats/): Style cells from their values with ordered comparison, text, blank and formula rules.

### Styles and themes

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/styles/

Sheetwrite paints cells on a canvas, so it has two style layers: the **`Theme`** (colors, fonts, and geometry for the renderer) and **`CellStyle`** (formatting for one cell or one column). A small stylesheet styles the host container and declares CSS custom properties.

```ts
grid.setTheme({ headerBg: "#e8eef7", headerFg: "#1f3a5f" });
grid.applyTransaction({
  patches: [{
    op: "set",
    addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 },
    value: { kind: "literal", value: "Total" },
    style: {
      bold: true,
      backgroundColor: "#eef1f5",
      border: { bottom: { color: "#111111", width: 2, style: "solid" } },
    },
  }],
});
```

| **Total** | |
| --- | ---: |
| | |
| | |
| | |
| | |

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sheet1",
  sheets: [
    {
      id: "sheet1",
      name: "Sheet1",
      rowCount: 5,
      columns: [
        { key: "item", header: "Item", width: 160, type: "text", headerStyle: { bold: true } },
        { key: "qty", header: "Qty", width: 100, type: "number", cellStyle: { align: "right" } },
      ],
    },
  ],
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  theme: { headerBg: "#e8eef7", headerFg: "#1f3a5f" },
});

grid.applyTransaction({
  patches: [
    {
      op: "set",
      addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 },
      value: { kind: "literal", value: "Total" },
      style: {
        bold: true,
        backgroundColor: "#eef1f5",
        border: { bottom: { color: "#111111", width: 2, style: "solid" } },
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

The header row paints with the theme's `headerBg` and `headerFg`, and the "Item" header is bold. Cell A1 shows a bold "Total" on a light fill with a thick bottom border. The "Qty" column is right-aligned.

## Theme

The `Theme` controls the canvas paint. Pass a `Partial<Theme>` as the `theme` option, or call `grid.setTheme(partial)` at runtime. Sheetwrite merges either one over the defaults.

```ts
interface Theme {
  font: string;
  bg: string;
  fg: string;
  gridLine: string;
  headerBg: string;
  headerFg: string;
  selection: string;
  selectionBorder: string;
  rowHeight: number;
  headerHeight: number;
  rowHeaderWidth: number; // 0 hides the left row-number gutter
  searchMatch: string;       // fill behind a search match
  searchActiveMatch: string; // fill/outline for the active (current) match
  highlight: string;         // fill for cells highlighted via Grid.highlightCells
}
```

`DEFAULT_THEME` (exported from `@sheetwrite/core`):

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `font` | `"13px system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif"` |
| `bg` | `"#ffffff"` |
| `fg` | `"#111111"` |
| `gridLine` | `"#eeeeee"` |
| `headerBg` | `"#f4ede1"` |
| `headerFg` | `"#6b4a1f"` |
| `selection` | `"#2563eb22"` |
| `selectionBorder` | `"#2563eb"` |
| `rowHeight` | `28` |
| `headerHeight` | `32` |
| `rowHeaderWidth` | `48` |
| `searchMatch` | `"#ffd54f80"` |
| `searchActiveMatch` | `"#f59e0b"` |
| `highlight` | `"#a7f3d080"` |

The shipped `styles.css` declares different values for the search and highlight CSS custom properties (`#fff47580`, `#fbbc04`, `#e8f0fe99`). On a host that imports the stylesheet, those values win over `DEFAULT_THEME`, because of the [resolution order](#resolution-order).

Override the search-match colors at runtime with `setTheme`:

```ts
grid.setTheme({ searchMatch: "#fff47580", searchActiveMatch: "#fbbc04" });
```

### Resolution order

Sheetwrite computes the effective theme once at construction, and again on `setTheme`:

```text
DEFAULT_THEME  <  --sheetwrite-* CSS custom properties (resolveThemeFromCss)  <  opts.theme / setTheme
```

`resolveThemeFromCss(host)` reads CSS custom properties from the host's computed style into a partial theme. `opts.theme` wins last.

| Method | Semantics |
| --- | --- |
| `grid.setTheme(partial)` | **Imperative patch.** Merges into the accumulated base theme and repaints. Use it for incremental changes. |
| `grid.replaceTheme(partial \| undefined)` | **Option-level replacement.** Runs the construction-time resolution again with the new value. `undefined` restores the CSS-variable and default resolution. The framework adapters call it for their `theme` prop, so **the prop is authoritative**: when you remove the prop (or drop a field), the defaults come back; no stale merged values stay. |
| `grid.getEffectiveTheme()` | Returns the effective (post-zoom) theme that paints now. |
| `grid.getTheme()` | Returns a copy of the base theme, before zoom scaling. |

After `setTheme` or `replaceTheme` changes the base theme, the Grid emits `theme-change` with a copy of the new theme. Use it to keep host controls in step with the canvas. The built-in toolbar uses it: its text and fill color swatches show the theme's `fg` and `bg` until the user picks a color.

```ts
const swatch = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#fill-swatch")!;
swatch.style.background = grid.getTheme().bg;
grid.on("theme-change", ({ theme }) => {
  swatch.style.background = theme.bg;
});
```

Tailwind uses the same seam. Set `--sheetwrite-*` custom properties on the host with arbitrary-property utilities (for example `class="[--sheetwrite-bg:#0b0b0c] [--sheetwrite-fg:#e7e7e7]"`) or with a `@layer` rule. Construction and `replaceTheme(undefined)` both read them from the computed style.

```ts
const DARK: Partial<Theme> = {
  bg: "#0b0b0c",
  fg: "#e7e7e7",
  gridLine: "#26262a",
  headerBg: "#1a160f",
  headerFg: "#e8c98a",
  selection: "#e8c98a22",
  selectionBorder: "#e8c98a",
};

grid.setTheme(DARK);
```

## CSS custom properties and the stylesheet

Import the stylesheet once. It styles the host container (the grid adds the `.sheetwrite` class to your host element) and declares the `--sheetwrite-*` defaults. It also ships a dark variant under `[data-theme="dark"]` or a `.dark` ancestor class (the Tailwind convention).

```ts
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";
```

`resolveThemeFromCss` maps these custom properties onto `Theme` fields:

| CSS custom property | Theme field |
| --- | --- |
| `--sheetwrite-bg` | `bg` |
| `--sheetwrite-fg` | `fg` |
| `--sheetwrite-grid-line` | `gridLine` |
| `--sheetwrite-header-bg` | `headerBg` |
| `--sheetwrite-header-fg` | `headerFg` |
| `--sheetwrite-selection` | `selection` |
| `--sheetwrite-selection-border` | `selectionBorder` |
| `--sheetwrite-row-height` | `rowHeight` (parsed as a number) |
| `--sheetwrite-search-match` | `searchMatch` |
| `--sheetwrite-search-active` | `searchActiveMatch` |
| `--sheetwrite-highlight` | `highlight` |
| `--sheetwrite-font` | `font` (a `/ line-height` segment is removed for the canvas) |

`headerHeight` and `rowHeaderWidth` have no CSS variable. Set them with the `theme` option. An explicit `--sheetwrite-*` value on the `.sheetwrite` element itself wins over both dark selectors (the same element wins over an ancestor).

### Widget and context-menu styling

The stylesheet also exposes widget variables, in addition to the canvas theme mapping:

| CSS custom property | Widget use | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--sheetwrite-widget-border` | Borders and separators for toolbar, find and menu chrome | `--sheetwrite-grid-line` |
| `--sheetwrite-menu-hover` | Context-menu item hover background | `--sheetwrite-grid-line` |
| `--sheetwrite-menu-disabled-opacity` | Disabled context-menu row opacity | `0.5` |

The bundled menu uses these public classes:

| Class | Element |
| --- | --- |
| `.sheetwrite-context-menu` | Container |
| `.sheetwrite-context-menu-item` | Row |
| `.sheetwrite-context-menu-item-disabled` | Disabled state |
| `.sheetwrite-context-menu-shortcut` | Shortcut hint |
| `.sheetwrite-context-menu-sep` | Separator |

Scope overrides below the grid host. Do not replace positioning, visibility, or disabled behavior:

```css
.sheetwrite {
  --sheetwrite-widget-border: #334155;
  --sheetwrite-menu-hover: #1e293b;
  --sheetwrite-menu-disabled-opacity: 0.45;
}

.sheetwrite .sheetwrite-context-menu-item {
  font-weight: 500;
}
```

The recommended runtime-theming pattern changes both layers together. Toggle `data-theme` on a wrapper so the CSS-variable chrome around the grid changes, and call `setTheme` so the canvas repaints.

```ts
darkBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
  grid.setTheme(DARK);
  stage.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
});
```

## CellStyle

`CellStyle` formats individual cells. It appears in three places:

| Place | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `style` on a `set` patch | Formatting for that one cell. |
| `Column.cellStyle` | A column-wide default that the renderer paints under every body cell of the column. |
| `Column.headerStyle` | The style of that column's header cell. |

`Column.cellStyle` is a default, not a lock. A per-cell `set` style overrides the column default for that cell. A cell paints with its column's `cellStyle` until its own patch supplies styling.

```ts
interface CellStyle {
  bold?: boolean;
  italic?: boolean;
  underline?: boolean;
  strikethrough?: boolean;
  fontSize?: number;
  fontFamily?: string;       // e.g. "Calibri"; the theme font is the fallback
  color?: string;            // hex text color, e.g. "#111111"
  backgroundColor?: string;  // hex fill, e.g. "#ffffff"
  align?: "left" | "center" | "right";
  verticalAlign?: "top" | "middle" | "bottom"; // omitted = centered
  numberFormat?: string;     // overrides the column's numberFormat
  wrap?: boolean;
  border?: CellBorders;
}
```

The font, alignment and wrap fields are on [Fonts and alignment](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/fonts-and-alignment/). `numberFormat` is on [Number formats](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/number-formats/).

Apply a style to a cell with a transaction. A `set` replaces the value and the style, so pass the current value back when you only change the style:

```ts
grid.store.applyTransaction({
  patches: [
    {
      op: "set",
      addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 },
      value: { kind: "literal", value: "Total" },
      style: { bold: true, align: "center", backgroundColor: "#eef1f5" },
    },
  ],
});
```

### Borders

Borders are per side. `CellBorders.all` applies to each side that has no border of its own:

```ts
interface CellBorders {
  all?: CellBorder;
  top?: CellBorder;
  right?: CellBorder;
  bottom?: CellBorder;
  left?: CellBorder;
}

interface CellBorder {
  color?: string;                          // hex, e.g. "#111111"
  width?: number;
  style?: "solid" | "dashed" | "dotted";
}
```

```ts
const style: CellStyle = {
  border: {
    all: { color: "#cccccc", width: 1, style: "solid" },
    bottom: { color: "#111111", width: 2, style: "solid" },
  },
};
```

## Edge cases and limits

- On a host that imports `styles.css`, the stylesheet's search and highlight colors win over `DEFAULT_THEME`.
- `headerHeight` and `rowHeaderWidth` have no CSS variable.
- A `set` patch replaces the value and the style. Pass the current value back to change only the style.

### Fonts and alignment

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/fonts-and-alignment/

`CellStyle` sets a cell's font, its alignment, and its text wrap, and the `grid.actions` commands apply the same fields to the selection.

```ts
grid.styleRange(
  { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 0, col: 0 } },
  { fontFamily: "Georgia", fontSize: 16, bold: true, wrap: true, verticalAlign: "top" },
);
grid.setSelection({
  kind: "range",
  range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 1, col: 0 }, end: { row: 3, col: 1 } },
});
grid.actions.setFontFamily("Calibri");
grid.actions.stepFontSize(1);
grid.actions.setVerticalAlign("bottom");
```

| **Quarterly sales for the north and east regions** | 0 |
| --- | ---: |
| North | 120 |
| East | 95 |
| West | 80 |

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type ColumnarData, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sheet1",
  sheets: [
    {
      id: "sheet1",
      name: "Sheet1",
      rowCount: 4,
      columns: [
        { key: "region", header: "Region", width: 180, type: "text" },
        { key: "sales", header: "Sales", width: 100, type: "number" },
      ],
    },
  ],
};
const data: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 4,
  columns: {
    region: ["Quarterly sales for the north and east regions", "North", "East", "West"],
    sales: new Float64Array([0, 120, 95, 80]),
  },
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, data });

// Style one range directly.
grid.styleRange(
  { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 0, col: 0 } },
  { fontFamily: "Georgia", fontSize: 16, bold: true, wrap: true, verticalAlign: "top" },
);

// Or select cells and run the same commands as the toolbar and ribbon.
grid.setSelection({
  kind: "range",
  range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 1, col: 0 }, end: { row: 3, col: 1 } },
});
grid.actions.setFontFamily("Calibri");
grid.actions.stepFontSize(1);
grid.actions.setVerticalAlign("bottom");

console.log(grid.store.getCell({ sheet: "sheet1", row: 1, col: 0 }).style.fontSize);
// 14.666666666666666 (11 pt: the theme's 13px rounds to 10 pt, and the next standard size is 11 pt)
```

A1 shows a bold, 16 px Georgia title that wraps and starts at the top of the cell. A2:B4 paint in Calibri at 11 pt, at the bottom of their rows.

## Font and alignment fields

These `CellStyle` fields control text. All of them are optional.

| Field | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fontFamily` | `string` | One font family, for example `"Calibri"`. The theme font is the fallback. |
| `fontSize` | `number` | Font size in CSS pixels. |
| `bold` | `boolean` | Bold text. |
| `italic` | `boolean` | Italic text. |
| `underline` | `boolean` | Underlined text. |
| `strikethrough` | `boolean` | Struck-through text. |
| `color` | `string` | Hex text color, for example `"#111111"`. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` | Horizontal alignment. |
| `verticalAlign` | `"top" \| "middle" \| "bottom"` | Vertical alignment. Omitted means centered. |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | Wrap text onto more lines inside the cell. |

Paint, column auto-fit, snapshots, the clipboard and hyperlink styles all honor `fontFamily`, `verticalAlign` and `numberFormat`.

### Font family names

`fontFamily` names one family. Sheetwrite draws it before the theme font's families, so a font that the browser does not have falls back to the theme font.

A valid name has 1 to 128 characters: letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `_` and `-`. It starts with a letter or a digit and does not end in a space. `isCellFontFamily(value)` from `@sheetwrite/core` applies this rule. The same rule guards snapshots, hyperlinks, the clipboard and XLSX import.

```ts
import { isCellFontFamily } from "@sheetwrite/core";

isCellFontFamily("Segoe UI"); // true
isCellFontFamily("Arial, sans-serif"); // false: a comma is not allowed
```

## Grid actions

`grid.actions` holds the commands behind the toolbar and the ribbon. Each command applies to every cell of the current selection. It does nothing when the grid is read-only or the selection is empty.

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `setFontFamily(family: string \| null)` | Sets the font family. `null` returns the cells to the column or theme font. |
| `setFontSize(size: number \| null)` | Sets the font size in CSS pixels. `null` returns the cells to the default. |
| `stepFontSize(direction: 1 \| -1)` | Steps the focus cell's font size to the next larger (`1`) or smaller (`-1`) standard size, and applies it to the selection. |
| `setVerticalAlign(align: CellVerticalAlign)` | Sets `verticalAlign` to `"top"`, `"middle"` or `"bottom"`. |
| `toggleWrap()` | Sets `wrap` to the opposite of the focus cell's `wrap`. |
| `setAlign(align)` | Sets the horizontal alignment. |
| `toggleBold()`, `toggleItalic()`, `toggleUnderline()`, `toggleStrikethrough()` | Turn the field on or off, from the focus cell's current value. |

`stepFontSize` uses Excel's standard sizes, in points: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 36, 48, 72.

- The start size is the focus cell's `fontSize`. If the cell has none, it is the pixel size in the theme `font` (13 px when the theme font has no pixel size).
- Sheetwrite converts pixels to points at 96/72 pixels per point and rounds to the nearest half point.
- Above 72 pt, a step up goes to the next multiple of 10 points. Below 8 pt, a step down removes 1 point and stops at 1 pt.

The ribbon's font list calls `setFontFamily` (an empty name sends `null`). Its size box calls `setFontSize` with the points converted to pixels. Increase Font Size and Decrease Font Size call `stepFontSize(1)` and `stepFontSize(-1)`. Top Align, Middle Align and Bottom Align call `setVerticalAlign`, and Wrap Text calls `toggleWrap`.

```ts
grid.actions.stepFontSize(-1);
grid.actions.toggleWrap();
grid.actions.setFontSize(null); // back to the default size
```

## Vertical alignment in XLSX and LibreOffice

*Updated in 0.6.0.* An XLSX cell with no vertical alignment is bottom-aligned in Excel, but an unset Sheetwrite cell paints centered. Import and export now convert between the two defaults, so imported files look as they do in Excel. LibreOffice reads and writes the same XLSX attributes, and the LibreOffice round trip has no vertical-alignment differences.

Visible change: imported cells with no vertical alignment now sit at the bottom, as in Excel.

Import (cell styles):

| XLSX `<alignment vertical>` | Sheetwrite `verticalAlign` |
| --- | --- |
| No `<alignment>`, or no `vertical` attribute | `"bottom"` |
| `bottom` | `"bottom"` |
| `top` | `"top"` |
| `center` | Unset (the grid default, centered) |
| `center`, in a column whose default is `"bottom"` | `"middle"` (an explicit value overrides the column default) |

A workbook with no styles part imports every cell as `"bottom"`.

Export (cell styles):

| Sheetwrite `verticalAlign` | XLSX `<alignment vertical>` |
| --- | --- |
| Unset | `center` |
| `"middle"` | `center` |
| `"top"` | `top` |
| `"bottom"` | No `vertical` attribute (the XLSX default) |

Export also writes the workbook's normal cell style with `vertical="center"`, so unstyled cells stay centered.

Conditional-format styles are differential: they change only the fields they set. For them, import maps `center` to `"middle"`, `top` and `bottom` to the same names, and a missing attribute to unset. Export writes only a value that the style sets (`"middle"` as `center`).

Fonts on import: only fonts other than the workbook default become a cell `fontFamily`.

## Edge cases and limits

- `wrap` applies to text, not to numbers. A number that does not fit its cell paints as `#` characters.
- A wrapped block that is taller than its cell starts at the top of the cell.
- Text that does not wrap can spill past its cell: left-aligned text to the right, right-aligned text to the left, and centered text to both sides. Numbers never spill.
- Native boolean values are centered unless `CellStyle.align` overrides it.
- A font that the browser does not have falls back to the theme font.

## See also

- [Styles and themes](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/styles/#cellstyle) for the full `CellStyle` and borders.
- [Number formats](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/number-formats/)
- [Configuration](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/options-and-presentation/) for the toolbar.
- [XLSX export](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/)
- [`GridActions`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid-actions/), [`CellStyle`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/cell-style/) and [`isCellFontFamily`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/is-cell-font-family/) API reference.

### Number formats

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/number-formats/

A column or a cell can carry an Excel-style `numberFormat` code, and a column can carry a BCP 47 `numberLocale`, so numbers and dates paint the same way on every host.

```ts
import type { Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";

const columns: Workbook["sheets"][number]["columns"] = [
  { key: "amount", header: "Amount", width: 140, type: "number", numberFormat: "#,##0.00", numberLocale: "de-DE" },
  { key: "day", header: "Day", width: 120, type: "date", numberFormat: "yyyy-mm-dd" },
  { key: "share", header: "Share", width: 100, type: "number" },
];
grid.styleRange(
  { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 2 }, end: { row: 1, col: 2 } },
  { numberFormat: "0.0%" },
);
```

| 1.234,50 | 2024-02-29 | 12.5% |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 99,00 | 2024-03-01 | 50.0% |

The inputs are amounts `1234.5` and `99`, UTC date serials `45351` and `45352`, and shares `0.125` and `0.5`. `formatNumber` returns the same text the grid paints.

Full setup

```ts
import {
  createGrid,
  formatNumber,
  initSheetwrite,
  type ColumnarData,
  type Workbook,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sheet1",
  sheets: [
    {
      id: "sheet1",
      name: "Sheet1",
      rowCount: 2,
      columns: [
        {
          key: "amount",
          header: "Amount",
          width: 140,
          type: "number",
          numberFormat: "#,##0.00",
          numberLocale: "de-DE",
        },
        { key: "day", header: "Day", width: 120, type: "date", numberFormat: "yyyy-mm-dd" },
        { key: "share", header: "Share", width: 100, type: "number" },
      ],
    },
  ],
};
const data: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2,
  columns: {
    amount: new Float64Array([1234.5, 99]),
    day: new Float64Array([45351, 45352]),
    share: new Float64Array([0.125, 0.5]),
  },
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, data });

// A cell style overrides the column format.
grid.styleRange(
  { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 2 }, end: { row: 1, col: 2 } },
  { numberFormat: "0.0%" },
);

console.log(formatNumber(1234.5, "#,##0.00", "de-DE")); // "1.234,50"
console.log(formatNumber(45351, "yyyy-mm-dd")); // "2024-02-29"
console.log(formatNumber(0.125, "0.0%")); // "12.5%"
```

## Column and cell formats

| Place | Field | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Column` | `numberFormat` | Format code for every cell of a numeric or date column. |
| `Column` | `numberLocale` | BCP 47 locale for separators, for example `"de-DE"`. |
| `CellStyle` | `numberFormat` | Format code for one cell. It overrides the column's format. |

The canvas renderer, auto-fit measurement and the exported formatter use the same UTC serial value and the same locale.

A cell style overrides the column format. To set a format on a range, use `styleRange`:

```ts
grid.styleRange(
  { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 2 }, end: { row: 9, col: 2 } },
  { numberFormat: "0.0%" },
);
```

The code `General` takes a cell out of its column's format.

XLSX import keeps each cell's own format, so a column that mixes formats round-trips cell by cell.

The grid actions `setNumberFormat(code: string | null)` and `stepDecimals(direction: 1 | -1)` change the format of the selection. `setNumberFormat(null)` returns the cells to the column's format. `stepDecimals` shows one more (`1`) or one fewer (`-1`) decimal place than the focus cell does.

## Format codes

`formatNumber(value, code?, locale?)` is exported from `@sheetwrite/core`. It is a cached renderer for the supported Excel-style families:

These examples use `"en-US"`, the formatter's default locale. Set `numberLocale` on a column or pass a locale as the third argument to change separators.

| Code | Example output |
| --- | --- |
| _(none)_ or `General` | `1234.5` → 1,234.5 (locale default) |
| `0` | `1234.5` → 1235 |
| `0.00` | `1234.5` → 1234.50 |
| `#,##0.00` | `1234.5` → 1,234.50 |
| `0%` | `0.5` → 50% |
| `$#,##0.00` | `1234.5` → $1,234.50 |
| `0.00E+00` | `12345` → 1.23E+04 |
| `yyyy-mm-dd` | serial `45351` → 2024-02-29 |
| `mmm d, yyyy h:mm:ss AM/PM` | UTC serial `45477.62924768519` (2024-07-04 15:06:07 UTC) → Jul 4, 2024 3:06:07 PM |
| `0.00;[Red](0.00);"none";"value: "@` | Positive `2.5` → 2.50; negative `-2.5` → (2.50); zero `0` → none; text `"draft"` → value: draft |

### Numeric codes

Numeric formats support fixed decimals, optional grouping, percent scaling, scientific exponents with an explicit width, quoted and escaped literals, and currency prefixes and suffixes.

Up to four semicolon sections select the positive, negative, zero and text output. Sheetwrite accepts color directives such as `[Red]` as formatting metadata, but they do not change the canvas text color.

### Date and time codes

Date and time formats support numeric and named month and day fields, 12-hour and 24-hour time, minutes, seconds, and AM/PM. Neighboring time tokens decide whether `m` means month or minute.

UTC fields make date rendering the same in every host timezone. Locale-specific separators come from `numberLocale`, not from the browser's locale.

## Edge cases and limits

- Fractions, elapsed-time bracket tokens and fractional seconds are not supported.
- Formula errors are explicit values such as `#DIV/0!` and `#CYCLE!`. They are not non-finite numbers that the formatter hides. See [Formulas](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/authoring-and-references/#scalars-coercion-and-errors).
- Native boolean values use the normal cell style model and render as uppercase `TRUE` or `FALSE`. They are centered unless `CellStyle.align` overrides it.

- [Styles and themes](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/styles/#cellstyle)
- [Fonts and alignment](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/fonts-and-alignment/)
- [Conditional formats](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/conditional-formats/)
- [`formatNumber`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/format-number/) API reference.
- [Live formatting showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/formatting/) — try the number-format controls; column G shows seven mixed formats.

### Conditional formats

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/conditional-formats/

A conditional format is an ordered rule on a sheet: when a cell in the rule's range matches the predicate, the rule's `CellStyle` paints over the cell's own style.

```ts
const scores = { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 1 }, end: { row: 3, col: 1 } };
grid.setConditionalFormats([
  {
    range: scores, when: { kind: "lessThan", value: 50 },
    style: { color: "#b91c1c", bold: true }, stopIfTrue: true,
  },
  { range: scores, when: { kind: "formula", source: "=B1>=90" }, style: { backgroundColor: "#dcfce7" } },
  { range: scores, when: { kind: "equal", value: null }, style: { backgroundColor: "#fef3c7" } },
  {
    range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 3, col: 0 } },
    when: { kind: "contains", text: "late" }, style: { italic: true },
  },
]);
```

| Ana | 92 |
| --- | ---: |
| *Ben (late)* | **48** |
| Chen | 75 |
| Dee | |

Full setup

```ts
import {
  createGrid,
  initSheetwrite,
  type ColumnarData,
  type ConditionalFormatRule,
  type Workbook,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

const scores = { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 1 }, end: { row: 3, col: 1 } };
const rules: ConditionalFormatRule[] = [
  // First rule wins, and a match stops the later rules for that cell.
  {
    range: scores,
    when: { kind: "lessThan", value: 50 },
    style: { color: "#b91c1c", bold: true },
    stopIfTrue: true,
  },
  // Relative references move with each cell of the range: B1, B2, B3, B4.
  { range: scores, when: { kind: "formula", source: "=B1>=90" }, style: { backgroundColor: "#dcfce7" } },
  { range: scores, when: { kind: "equal", value: null }, style: { backgroundColor: "#fef3c7" } },
  {
    range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 3, col: 0 } },
    when: { kind: "contains", text: "late" },
    style: { italic: true },
  },
];

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "sheet1",
  sheets: [
    {
      id: "sheet1",
      name: "Sheet1",
      rowCount: 4,
      columns: [
        { key: "name", header: "Name", width: 160, type: "text" },
        { key: "score", header: "Score", width: 100, type: "number" },
      ],
      conditionalFormats: rules,
    },
  ],
};
const data: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 4,
  columns: {
    name: ["Ana", "Ben (late)", "Chen", "Dee"],
    score: [92, 48, 75, null],
  },
};

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, data });

const view = grid.store.getVisibleWindow("sheet1", { start: 0, end: 4 }, [1]);
console.log(view.styles[view.styleIds[0]!]?.backgroundColor); // "#dcfce7" (92 >= 90)
console.log(view.styles[view.styleIds[1]!]?.color); // "#b91c1c" (48 < 50)
```

The score 92 paints on a green fill, 48 paints in bold red, 75 has no rule style, and the blank score paints on a yellow fill. "Ben (late)" is italic.

To replace the rules of the active sheet at runtime, call `grid.setConditionalFormats(rules)`. It commits one `setSheetMeta` operation with the new list:

```ts
grid.setConditionalFormats([
  {
    range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 1 }, end: { row: 99, col: 1 } },
    when: { kind: "greaterThan", value: 100 },
    style: { backgroundColor: "#dbeafe" },
  },
]);
```

## Rule fields

`ConditionalFormatRule`:

| Field | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `range` | `Range` | The cells the rule checks. It must be on the sheet that holds the rule and inside the sheet's rows and columns. |
| `when` | `ConditionalFormatPredicate` | The condition. |
| `style` | `CellStyle` | The style that paints when the condition matches. |
| `stopIfTrue` | `boolean` | When the rule matches a cell, later rules are not checked for that cell. |

Rules live in `Sheet.conditionalFormats` (and `SheetSnapshot.conditionalFormats`). A `setSheetMeta` operation with `patch.conditionalFormats` replaces the list.

## Predicates

`ConditionalFormatPredicate`:

| `kind` | Fields | Matches when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"greaterThan"` | `value: number` | The cell holds a number greater than `value`. |
| `"lessThan"` | `value: number` | The cell holds a number less than `value`. A blank cell does not match. |
| `"equal"` | `value: number \| string \| null` | The cell holds the same number, or exactly the same text (case-sensitive). `value: null` matches blank cells. |
| `"contains"` | `text: string`, `matchCase?: boolean` | The cell holds text that contains `text`. The match ignores case unless `matchCase` is `true`. An empty `text` matches nothing. |
| `"formula"` | `source: string` | The formula is true for the cell. `source` starts with `=`. |

A formula predicate is anchored at the top-left cell of the rule's range. Relative A1 references move with each target cell; `$`-absolute parts stay fixed. Formula rules are calculated again when the cells they depend on change.

## Order and precedence

Sheetwrite checks rules in array order.

- When more than one rule matches a cell, their styles merge. For a field that two rules both set, the earlier rule wins.
- A matching rule with `stopIfTrue: true` keeps every later rule out of that cell's match set.

For example, if rule 1 sets `{ color: "#111111", bold: true }` and rule 2 sets `{ color: "#222222", italic: true }`, and both match, the cell paints `#111111`, bold and italic. With `stopIfTrue` on rule 1, the cell paints `#111111` and bold only.

## XLSX import and export

Export writes each rule as a native conditional-format record with a differential style (`dxf`). The array position sets the rule priority, and `stopIfTrue` writes `stopIfTrue="1"`.

| Sheetwrite predicate | XLSX rule |
| --- | --- |
| `greaterThan`, `lessThan`, `equal` | `cellIs` with the same operator |
| `equal` with `value: null` | `containsBlanks` |
| `contains` | `containsText` |
| `contains` with `matchCase: true` | `expression`: `ISNUMBER(FIND("text", anchor))` |
| `formula` | `expression` (without the leading `=`) |

Import reads the same rule types back, in priority order. An `expression` rule of the form `ISNUMBER(FIND("text", …))` imports as a case-sensitive `contains`.

Vertical alignment in a differential style maps as described in [Fonts and alignment](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/fonts-and-alignment/#vertical-alignment-in-xlsx-and-libreoffice).

## Edge cases and limits

- One sheet holds at most 32 rules (`MAX_CONDITIONAL_FORMAT_RULES`, the size of the renderer's `u32` match mask). Snapshot validation reports more as a `resource-limit` error at `sheets[n].conditionalFormats`.
- One formula predicate holds at most 8,192 characters (`MAX_CONDITIONAL_FORMAT_FORMULA_LENGTH`).
- The store rejects a rule list in which a range is on another sheet or outside the sheet, a formula does not start with `=`, or `stopIfTrue` is not a boolean.
- XLSX import drops these rules, each with a `format-loss` warning: color scales, data bars, icon sets, extended conditional formatting, rules with an invalid priority or differential style, formulas longer than 8,192 characters, formulas with external references, and rules past the 32-rule limit. For color scales, data bars, icon sets and other unsupported rule types, the warning names the rule type. Unrepresentable differential styles do not enter the live model or the renderer.
- A rule that export cannot encode stays in Sheetwrite metadata, with a `format-loss` warning.
- LibreOffice does not write `stopIfTrue`. A file saved by LibreOffice loses it; this is a recorded LibreOffice difference.

## See also

- [Styles and themes](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/styles/#cellstyle) for `CellStyle`.
- [XLSX export](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#workbook-interchange)
- [Compatibility results](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/compatibility-results/) for the checked conditional-format evidence.
- [`ConditionalFormatRule`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/conditional-format-rule/), [`ConditionalFormatPredicate`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/conditional-format-predicate/) and [`MAX_CONDITIONAL_FORMAT_RULES`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/max-conditional-format-rules/) API reference.

### Data operations

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/data-operations/

```ts
grid.sortBy(1, false);
const total = grid.aggregate(1, "sum");
console.log(total); // 195 for Ada: 120 and Lin: 75
```

| Ada | 120 |
| --- | --- |
| Lin | 75 |

[Try it live: sort and filter orders](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/data-tools/).

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (!host) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";
const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "s",
  sheets: [{ id: "s", name: "Sales", rowCount: 2, columns: [
    { key: "customer", header: "Customer", width: 140, type: "text" },
    { key: "total", header: "Total", width: 100, type: "number" },
  ] }],
};
await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  data: { rowCount: 2, columns: {
    customer: ["Lin", "Ada"], total: new Float64Array([75, 120]),
  } },
});
grid.sortBy(1, false);
console.log(grid.aggregate(1, "sum")); // 195
```

Sheetwrite can sort, filter, hide, group, aggregate, import, and export the active
sheet without rewriting the stored row data. Sorts and filters are display views:
the store keeps a row-order permutation/subset and the renderer reads through it.

## Display views

The simple shorthands are still available:

```ts
grid.sortBy(4);            // sort by column 4, ascending
grid.sortBy(4, false);     // descending
grid.filterBy(3, "Tokyo"); // keep rows whose column-3 text contains "Tokyo"
grid.clearView();          // clear sort/filter state only
```

For custom UI, use the composable primitives. All active column filters are ANDed
together, hidden rows and collapsed groups are subtracted, and the remaining rows
are sorted by the active multi-key sort.

```ts
grid.sortByMulti([
  { col: 4, ascending: false }, // primary key
  { col: 0, ascending: true },  // tie-breaker
]);

grid.setColumnFilter(3, { kind: "contains", text: "Tokyo" });
grid.setColumnFilter(2, { kind: "values", values: ["Retail", "Partner"] });
grid.setColumnFilter(5, { kind: "compare", op: "gte", value: 1000 });

const cities = grid.distinctValues(3, 100); // data source for a filter menu

grid.hideRows([1, 7, 9]);
grid.groupRows(10, 25);
grid.setGroupCollapsed(10, true);
```

| Method | Signature | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sortBy` | `sortBy(col: number, ascending = true): void` | Reorder displayed rows by one column. |
| `sortByMulti` | `sortByMulti(keys: readonly SortKey[]): void` | Stable multi-key sort; first key is primary. |
| `filterBy` | `filterBy(col: number, needle: string): void` | Shorthand for a case-insensitive `contains` column filter. |
| `setColumnFilter` | `setColumnFilter(col: number, filter: ColumnFilter \| null): void` | Set or clear one column filter. |
| `getColumnFilters` | `getColumnFilters(): ReadonlyMap<number, ColumnFilter>` | Current active column filters. |
| `distinctValues` | `distinctValues(col: number, limit = 1000): CellScalar[]` | First-seen distinct resolved values for a column. |
| `hideRows` / `showRows` | `hideRows(rows)` / `showRows(rows?)` | Hide/show data rows independent of sort/filter state. |
| `hiddenRows` | `hiddenRows(): readonly number[]` | Currently hidden data rows. |
| `groupRows` / `ungroupRows` | `groupRows(start, end)` / `ungroupRows(start, end)` | Create/remove an inclusive data-row group. |
| `setGroupCollapsed` | `setGroupCollapsed(start, collapsed): void` | Collapse or expand the group starting at `start`. |
| `rowGroups` | `rowGroups(): readonly RowGroup[]` | Current row-group definitions. |
| `clearView` | `clearView(): void` | Clears sort/filter state. Hidden rows and row groups are preserved. |

`clearView()` deliberately does **not** unhide rows or expand row groups. This
matches spreadsheet behavior: clearing a filter removes the query, but explicit
hidden rows and collapsed groups remain a separate visibility state. Use
`showRows()` and `setGroupCollapsed(start, false)` to reverse those states.

Because a view reorders or hides rows, two features that depend on a stable
row-to-cell mapping are disabled while a view is active:

- **Merged cells** are not drawn (the layout reports no merges under a view).
- **Drag-to-fill** is unavailable (the fill handle is hidden).

Call `clearView()` to remove sort/filter state; also show hidden rows / expand
row groups if you need the full natural data order.

## Aggregate

`aggregate` computes a column reduction over the active sheet's data and returns a
number:

```ts
type Aggregate = Grid["aggregate"];
```

```ts
const total = grid.aggregate(4, "sum");
const rows = grid.aggregate(0, "count");
```

## Frozen panes and zoom

Frozen panes and zoom are view geometry, not data mutations:

```ts
grid.setFrozen(1, 1); // pin first view row and first column
grid.setFrozen(0, 0); // unfreeze

grid.setZoom(1.25);
console.log(grid.getZoom());
```

`setFrozen(rows, cols?)` pins leading view rows and columns while the body
scrolls. `setZoom(z)` clamps to `0.5`-`2` and scales painted row/column geometry
and fonts; workbook widths/heights remain in base units.

## See also

- [Interaction](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/) for clipboard TSV and the toolbar sort control.
- [Concepts](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/documents-and-operations/#document-protocol-and-storage-transactions) for row/column `DocumentOp` transactions.

### Datasources

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/datasources/

```ts
createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  datasource,
  datasourceStorage: { mode: "paged" },
});
```

| Notebook | 3 | 8 | **$24.00** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pen | 5 | 2 | **$10.00** |

For this result, the workbook columns are `label`, `quantity`, `price`, and `total`, in that order. The host endpoint returns `[{ "label": "Notebook", "quantity": 3, "price": 8 }, { "label": "Pen", "quantity": 5, "price": 2 }]`. The adapter below supplies the formula and bold currency style for each total; D1 evaluates `=B1*C1`.

**Try it live:** [Engine showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/engine/) — jump between rows and inspect the datasource request and arrival events. Its datasource is local to the page, not a remote server.

Start with the host and initialization in [Your first grid](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/first-grid/), replacing eager `data` with `datasource`. A `DataSource` loads cancellable pages for the visible window, so the grid does not need the whole sheet in memory. The HTTP endpoint and its backing data remain your responsibility.

Datasource adapter setup — requires your server endpoint

```ts
import type { RowData } from "@sheetwrite/core";

interface ApiRow {
  label: string;
  quantity: number;
  price: number;
}

const datasource: DataSource = {
  capabilities: { protocol: 2, columns: "windowed" },
  async getRows({ sheet, start, end, columns, signal, revision }) {
    const response = await fetch(
      `/sheets/${encodeURIComponent(sheet)}?start=${start}&end=${end}`,
      { signal },
    );
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Datasource request failed: ${response.status}`);
    const records = (await response.json()) as ApiRow[];
    return {
      protocol: 2,
      start,
      columns,
      revision: response.headers.get("etag") ?? revision,
      rows: records.map((record, index) => {
        const row = start + index + 1;
        const cells: RowData = {
          label: record.label,
          quantity: record.quantity,
          price: record.price,
          total: {
            value: { kind: "formula", src: `=B${row}*C${row}` },
            style: { numberFormat: "$#,##0.00", bold: true },
          },
        };
        // Return exactly the column runs the grid asked for.
        return Object.fromEntries(
          columns.flatMap((band) => band.keys.map((key) => [key, cells[key] ?? null])),
        );
      }),
    };
  },
};

createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  datasource,
  datasourceStorage: { mode: "paged" },
});
```

The grid requests rows only for the visible window. The endpoint must return records for the requested row interval; this example selects the requested column runs before returning each page to the grid.

## Requests and pages

The cancellable request API owns one visible-window generation. Pages can carry authoritative formula source and style, not only resolved scalars.

| Field | Where | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capabilities.columns` | `DataSource` | `"windowed"` loads only the requested column runs. `"full-width"` loads every column; it does not scale horizontally. |
| `start` / `end` | request | Inclusive first row and exclusive end row. |
| `columns` | request and page | Exact visible, frozen, or prefetched column runs. Each run has `start`, exclusive `end`, and the stable column `keys`. |
| `signal` | request | Aborted when the request is no longer needed. Stop work when it aborts. |
| `revision` | request and page | The request carries a number; a page may return a string or number revision. |
| `rows` | page | Each value is a scalar, a `CellValue` object, or a `{ value: CellValue, style?: CellStyle }` wrapper. |

## Storage

| `datasourceStorage` field | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `"dense"` | `"paged"` allocates power-of-two row chunks only for loaded or locally edited areas. |
| `chunkRows` | 4,096 | Paged row chunk size, normalized to a power of two. |
| `cacheBytes` | 32 MiB | Per-sheet budget for clean cached chunks. Dirty chunks remain pinned until acknowledgement. |
| `dirtyCellLimit` | 1,000,000 | Maximum sparse local edits retained outside the clean page cache. |

Full-sheet queries and exports report incomplete data until all required pages are loaded. `Store.queryCapability(sheet)` and `getCellLoadState(addr)` expose that state. Default chunk and cache values and eviction behavior are also listed in [Compatibility and limits](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/compatibility-limits/#rendering-interaction-and-paged-data).

## Cells that visible formulas read

A visible formula can read cells outside the visible window. For example, a variance column can read a plan column far to the right. The grid asks the engine which same-sheet cells the painted formulas read, also through other formulas, and requests those cells with the window. This includes frozen bands, overscan, and merge anchors reached by the paint plan. The formula then resolves instead of staying `#LOADING!`.

- One shared 32,768-cell budget bounds dependency loading across these roots. A whole-column read does not load the full column in one window.
- The painted cells and their bounded dependency closure stay protected from clean-cache eviction while visible.
- Bulk reads such as exports and search use separate, transient protection. They do not replace the viewport's pins.
- Reads from other sheets are not loaded this way. Return those values from the datasource, or keep that sheet dense.

## Edge cases and limits

- Hydrated formulas, references, and styles do not emit user change events.
- A short page marks only the returned rows loaded.
- A malformed range emits `datasource-error` and stays retryable.
- Resetting or destroying the grid aborts outstanding requests.
- A late page never overwrites a cell edited after that request began.

## See also

- [Grid options and presentation](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/options-and-presentation/)
- [Events](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/events/)
- [Compatibility and limits](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/compatibility-limits/#rendering-interaction-and-paged-data)
- Generated [`DataSource`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/data-source/), [`DataSourceRequest`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/data-source-request/), [`DataSourcePage`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/data-source-page/) and [`DataSourceStorageOptions`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/data-source-storage-options/) contracts

### Keep app rows in your store

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/host-owned-rows/

Use the row bridge when your app owns the row objects and Sheetwrite owns editing, history, sorting, and filtering. The bridge is optional. Without `getRowId`, `defaultRows` keeps its existing one-time, uncontrolled behavior.

```ts
import { createRowBridge } from "@sheetwrite/core";

interface InvoiceRow { id: string; customer: string; total: number }
declare const entities: Map<string, InvoiceRow>;
declare let nextId: number;

const bridge = createRowBridge({
  columns: [{ key: "customer" }, { key: "total" }],
  defaultRows: [...entities.values()],
  getRowId: (row: InvoiceRow) => row.id,
  createRowId: () => `invoice-${nextId++}`,
});
// Mount: <SheetwriteGrid defaultRows={rows} rowBridge={bridge} onRowDelta={applyProjection} />
```

| Ada | 120 |
| --- | ---: |
| Lin | 75 |

Result: one grid row per `InvoiceRow` in `entities`, with its `getRowId` ID beside the row number. Column A is `customer` and B is `total`. Editing Lin's total projects a cell delta with `rowId` `"invoice-2"` and `columnKey` `"total"`, which `applyProjection` writes back to the map. An inserted row gets `invoice-3` from `createRowId`.

[Try it live → Host-owned rows showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/host-rows/). Sort and filter host-owned accounts and watch each delta name the same record ID.

Full setup

```ts
import { createRowBridge, type RowBridgeProjection } from "@sheetwrite/core";

interface InvoiceRow {
  id: string;
  customer: string;
  total: number;
}

const entities = new Map<string, InvoiceRow>([
  ["invoice-1", { id: "invoice-1", customer: "Ada", total: 120 }],
  ["invoice-2", { id: "invoice-2", customer: "Lin", total: 75 }],
]);
const rows = [...entities.values()];
let nextId = 3;

const bridge = createRowBridge({
  columns: [{ key: "customer" }, { key: "total" }],
  defaultRows: rows,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  createRowId: () => `invoice-${nextId++}`,
});

function applyProjection(projection: RowBridgeProjection<string>) {
  if (projection.status === "rejected" || projection.status === "duplicate") return;
  for (const delta of projection.deltas) {
    if (delta.kind === "cell") {
      const { rowId, columnKey, next } = delta.cell;
      if (rowId === null || columnKey === null || next?.kind !== "literal") continue;
      const row = entities.get(rowId);
      if (row) entities.set(rowId, { ...row, [columnKey]: next.value });
    }
    if (delta.kind === "row-structure" && delta.action === "delete") {
      for (const rowId of delta.removed) if (rowId !== null) entities.delete(rowId);
    }
    if (delta.kind === "row-structure" && delta.action === "insert") {
      for (const rowId of delta.inserted) {
        if (rowId !== null) entities.set(rowId, { id: rowId, customer: "", total: 0 });
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Attach the same bridge and callback in any adapter:

```tsx
import {
  SheetwriteGrid,
  type RowBridge,
  type RowBridgeProjection,
  type SimpleColumn,
} from "@sheetwrite/react";

interface InvoiceRow {
  id: string;
  customer: string;
  total: number;
}

declare const columns: readonly SimpleColumn<InvoiceRow>[];
declare const rows: readonly InvoiceRow[];
declare const bridge: RowBridge<string>;
declare const applyProjection: (projection: RowBridgeProjection<string>) => void;
<SheetwriteGrid
  columns={columns}
  defaultRows={rows}
  rowBridge={bridge}
  onRowDelta={applyProjection}
  height={420}
/>
```

Vue emits `row-delta`; Svelte and the imperative controller use `onRowDelta`. All adapters call the same core bridge. Sorts, filters, and hidden rows only change the visible order, so emitted row IDs still refer to data-space rows.

Remote changes should enter through `grid.applyRemoteOperations(...)`. Their projections have `status: "remote"` and `source: "remote"`. An echoed local transaction is returned as `duplicate` with no deltas. For a server rejection or transformed acceptance, call `bridge.reconcile(...)` with the server result and the canonical applied operations. The bridge does not update your store automatically; your callback remains the only place that changes host rows.

By default, the bridge retains at most 8,192 recent transaction IDs and 8,192 recent local operation fingerprints. If your host applies its own echoes directly through `applyRemoteOperations`, deliver each echo before its identity leaves this window. An echo outside this window is no longer recognized and projects as a remote change. `SyncCoordinator` removes acknowledged local echoes before they become Grid change events, so its separate 4,096 acknowledgement window does not set the bridge limit.

Set `maxRecentTransactions` in `createRowBridge` to change the limit for each identity window. The value must be a positive safe integer; invalid values throw a `RangeError`. Raise the limit if your host can project more than 8,192 transactions before an echo arrives. A larger limit retains more identity strings and uses more memory.

```ts
import { createRowBridge } from "@sheetwrite/core";

const bridge = createRowBridge({
  columns: [{ key: "total" }],
  defaultRows: [{ id: "invoice-1", total: 120 }],
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  maxRecentTransactions: 16384,
});
```

### Validation, protection and notes

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/validation-protection-and-notes/

```ts
grid.setValidationRule({
  id: "status",
  range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 1, col: 2 }, end: { row: 99, col: 2 } },
  condition: { kind: "list", values: ["Open", "Closed"] },
  policy: "reject",
  helpText: "Choose Open or Closed.",
});
grid.setProtectedRange({
  id: "header",
  range: { sheet: "sheet1", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 0, col: 9 } },
  label: "Header row",
});
grid.setProtectionResolver(() => "deny", "atomic");
grid.setNote({ sheet: "sheet1", row: 1, col: 0 }, "Checked by finance");
```

| **Invoice** | **Amount** | **Status** |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| INV-001 | 120 | Open |
| INV-002 | 80 | Closed |

- **C2:C100 · list validation**: Open or Closed. Other values are rejected; an attempted “Pending” leaves C2 as Open.
- **A1:J1 · protected header**: Local edits denied. Atomic mode rejects the whole transaction.
- **A2 · note**: Checked by finance

Result: the rules applied to the existing invoice rows. As in the grid, the amber corner marks the note and the arrow marks a list cell.

The setup has ten columns and at least 100 rows; A1:C3 contain the invoice data shown above. The code adds metadata, not those input values. The result also shows what stays in C2 after an invalid local edit. `grid.getNote({ sheet: "sheet1", row: 1, col: 0 })` returns `"Checked by finance"`.

**Try it live:** [Data tools showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/data-tools/) — try an invalid units value or a protected order-ID edit, and inspect the validation/protection feedback. Its rules differ from this invoice example.

**Full setup:** create and initialize the grid with [Your first grid](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/first-grid/), using the sheet dimensions and input rows described above, then apply this snippet.

## Validation

`DataValidationRule` covers list, numeric range, date range, text-length, and checkbox conditions. A rule has a stable ID, a range, a `reject` / `warn` / `allow` policy, optional blank handling, and help text.

List rules open a keyboard-operable `listbox`. Checkbox rules open a real ARIA `checkbox`. Arrow keys and typeahead change a list choice, Space toggles a checkbox, Enter commits, Tab commits and moves, and Escape cancels.

Every mutation path passes through the same validation boundary, including paste, fill, clear, and host transactions.

## Protection

`ProtectedRange` is serializable client policy metadata. Local writes to it are denied by default. A host `ProtectionResolver` can allow them. Atomic mode rejects the whole transaction. Partial mode applies the allowed operations and reports the rest.

## Notes

Plain-text notes use `setNote(addr, text)` and `getNote(addr)`. The focused cell's note is its ARIA description. Notes serialize, rebase with structural edits, take part in undo and redo, and round-trip through Sheetwrite XLSX metadata.

## Options

| Field or API | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataValidationRule.condition.kind` | `list`, `number`, `date`, `textLength`, `checkbox` | The kind of check. |
| `DataValidationRule.policy` | `"reject"`, `"warn"`, `"allow"` | What happens to a value that fails the check. |
| `DataValidationRule.allowBlank` | `boolean` | Blank cells are allowed unless you turn this off. |
| `DataValidationRule.helpText` | `string` | Help text for the rule. |
| `ProtectedRange.label` / `permissionKey` | `string` | Optional metadata for the resolver and UI. |
| `GridOptions.protectionResolver` / `grid.setProtectionResolver(resolver, mode?)` | `(request) => "allow" \| "deny"` | Decides each local write to a protected range. |
| `GridOptions.mutationPolicy` | `"atomic"`, `"partial"` | Reject the whole transaction, or skip only the denied operations. |
| `grid.setNote(addr, text)` | `string`, or `null` to remove | Set or remove a cell's note. |

Sheets can also carry `validationRules`, `protectedRanges` and `notes` in the workbook. See [DataValidationRule](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/data-validation-rule/), [ProtectedRange](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/protected-range/) and [ProtectionResolver](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/protection-resolver/).

## Edge cases and limits

- Remote operations bypass the protection policy. Protection is client UX, not authorization: a server must enforce its own authorization.
- Validation applies to paste, fill, clear, and host transactions, not only to typing.

## See also

- [Editing and clipboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/)
- [Collaboration](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/)
- [Accessibility](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/accessibility/)

### Persistence and recovery

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/persistence/

```ts
const loaded = validateWorkbookSnapshot(await (await fetch("/documents/products")).json());
if (!loaded.ok) throw new Error(`Invalid snapshot: ${loaded.errors.length} error(s)`);

const grid = createGridFromSnapshot(host, loaded.value);
const sync = new SyncCoordinator(grid, adapter, {
  documentId: "products",
  serverVersion: loaded.value.version ?? 0,
});

saveButton.onclick = () => void sync.sendNext();
```

| Notebook | 3 | 8 | **$24.00** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pen | 5 | 2 | **$10.00** |

| Snapshot / session state | Immediately after opening this example |
| --- | --- |
| Loaded document | `products`, version `7` (the example response's `version`) |
| Restored cells | A1:C2 contain the product inputs shown above. D1 and D2 retain `=B1*C1` and `=B2*C2`, with bold currency formatting. |
| Outgoing queue | Empty: hydration creates no local change event or undo entry. |
| Next local edit | Queued until the host calls `sync.sendNext()`, here through the Save button. |

This preview assumes `/documents/products` returns a valid snapshot at version `7` containing those cells and styles. It is not a built-in endpoint or a save acknowledgement: mounting a snapshot does not prove that a later edit has been persisted.

**Try it live:** [Database showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/database/) — edit cells, hold commits, and reload to inspect recovery. The showcase uses IndexedDB in your browser, not your server.

**Full setup:** use the host and initialization from [Your first grid](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/first-grid/), then the [complete HTTP adapter and load/mount flow](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/#load-mount-queue-and-acknowledge). You supply `adapter`, the document endpoint, and `saveButton`; `serverVersion` must come from the loaded snapshot.

Sheetwrite supplies contracts, not a database or endpoint. A `PersistenceAdapter` loads a schema-versioned `WorkbookSnapshot` and commits immutable `PendingCommit` records carrying a stable `clientMutationId` and `baseVersion`.

## What your host implements

| Part | You provide | Sheetwrite provides |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Load | `PersistenceAdapter.load` returns a validated `WorkbookSnapshot` with its `version`. | `createGridFromSnapshot`, `validateWorkbookSnapshot` |
| Save | `PersistenceAdapter.commit` appends one version in one database transaction. | `SyncCoordinator` queues, sends, and acknowledges commits in order. |
| Large undo | `restoreBlock` in your operation handler. Optional: `PersistenceAdapter.commitBatch`. | The Grid encodes large restores and, if needed, splits them into atomic batches. |
| Offline work | Nothing, in the browser. | `IndexedDbPendingCommitStorage` keeps pending commits across reloads. |
| Conflicts | A recovery UX for conflicts that rebase cannot resolve. | Conservative rebase and typed conflict events. |

The [collaboration guide](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/#load-mount-queue-and-acknowledge) has a complete HTTP adapter, the server table design, and the commit steps.

A commit response is `applied`, `duplicate`, or `conflict`. Applied and duplicate acknowledgements advance the server version. A conflict may provide ordered operations since the base or a current snapshot. Ambiguous structural or formula conflicts require host UX rather than silent merge.

`IndexedDbPendingCommitStorage` from `@sheetwrite/core/browser` can retain optimistic work across reloads. Its typed errors report blocked upgrades, unsupported schemas, quota, transaction, and abort failures. The core continues without durable browser storage when no pending-storage adapter is supplied.

## Serializable documents

Use `WorkbookSnapshot` plus `validateWorkbookSnapshot()` at persistence boundaries. `schemaVersion: 1` rejects unsupported future schemas with structured errors. `DocumentOp` is the exhaustive reducer operation union, including metadata and sheet lifecycle operations.

| Call | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `createGridFromSnapshot(host, snapshot, options)` | Validates and hydrates every sheet before mounting. Hydration emits no change event or undo entry. |
| `grid.exportSnapshot()` | Uses bulk sheet reads and returns deterministic sparse blocks. |
| `grid.applyRemoteOperations(operations)` | Emits a change with `source: "remote"`. It stays outside local undo history and outside `SyncCoordinator`'s outgoing queue. |
| `new SyncCoordinator(grid, adapter, options)` | Queues each non-empty local transaction as an immutable mutation record. Its `serverVersion` option is required and should come from the loaded snapshot. |
| `sync.sendNext()` / `sync.retry(id)` | Host-controlled sends. Retries keep the original ID. |
| `sync.subscribe(source)` | Accepts a transport-neutral callback source and validates strict version order. |

Use `MemoryPersistenceAdapter` as an executable, server-sequenced reference, not as durable storage. Adapter methods accept `AbortSignal`. Transport failures use `PersistenceError`, while version conflicts are typed commit responses that keep local work.

### Document state and session state

Document snapshots include workbook and sheet data, formula source, formatting, validation, protection metadata, notes, names, filters, and related document state.

Session state never belongs in a snapshot: selection, scroll position, caret state, search overlays and temporary highlights, host read-only policy, local zoom, and session-only grid options such as `renderer` and `readOnly`.

## Large undo

Undo of a large clear can be larger than one transaction allows. Sheetwrite 0.5.0 sends such a restore as one compressed `restoreBlock` operation. Your server must accept that operation before it accepts 0.5.0 clients. When even the compressed restore needs more than one server version, the Grid uses an atomic batch, which needs `commitBatch`. Without `commitBatch`, only that undo is rejected; everything else works. See [Large undo and atomic batches](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/#large-undo-and-atomic-batches).

## Edge cases and limits

- A local commit costs the same at any offline queue depth. `SyncCoordinator` does not walk every pending commit to pick a base version or report its state.
- Remote operations never enter the outgoing queue, so they are not sent back.
- Version conflicts keep local work; recover them with host UX.

- [Document operations reference](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/document-operations/)
- [`PersistenceAdapter` and sync API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/persistence-adapter/)
- [`@sheetwrite/core/browser`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core-browser/)
