Cash flows for the finance examples are in `H1:I4`: −10,000 on 2026-01-01,
2,500 on 2026-04-01, 4,200 on 2026-09-01, and 6,000 on 2026-12-31.

Every result below comes from the full engine. Results that spill are shown as
the cells they fill.

## Summarize: GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, PERCENTOF

`GROUPBY` groups rows by one or more key columns and aggregates the values. It
adds a total row by default.

```text
=GROUPBY(A1:A12, E1:E12, SUM)
```

| Region | Revenue |
| --- | ---: |
| East | 1550 |
| North | 3090 |
| South | 2720 |
| Total | 7360 |

`PIVOTBY` adds column keys:

```text
=PIVOTBY(A1:A12, B1:B12, E1:E12, SUM)
```

| | Chair | Desk | Lamp | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| East | 560 | 750 | 240 | 1550 |
| North | 480 | 2250 | 360 | 3090 |
| South | 1520 | 750 | 450 | 2720 |
| Total | 2560 | 3750 | 1050 | 7360 |

The optional arguments control headers, totals, and sort order. `PERCENTOF` as
the function gives each group's share, and a `LAMBDA` can be the function:

| Formula | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `=GROUPBY(A1:A12, E1:E12, SUM, 0, 0, -2)` | North 3090, South 2720, East 1550 (no total, largest first) |
| `=GROUPBY(A1:A12, E1:E12, PERCENTOF, 0, 0)` | East 0.2106, North 0.4198, South 0.3696 |
| `=GROUPBY(B1:B12, C1:C12, LAMBDA(units, MAX(units)), 0, 0)` | Chair 10, Desk 5, Lamp 15 |

A vector of functions, such as `HSTACK(SUM, AVERAGE)`, returns `#VALUE!`. Use
one function per `GROUPBY`.

## Your own functions: LAMBDA, MAP, REDUCE, SCAN, BYROW

`LAMBDA` makes a function from parameters and a calculation. The helpers call it
for each value, row, or column.

| Formula | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `=MAP(C1:C3, D1:D3, LAMBDA(units, price, units * price))` | 1000; 800; 480 (spills down) |
| `=REDUCE(0, E1:E12, LAMBDA(total, x, IF(x >= 1000, total + x, total)))` | 2250 |
| `=SCAN(0, E1:E4, LAMBDA(running, x, running + x))` | 1000; 1800; 2280; 2780 (running total) |
| `=BYROW(C1:D3, LAMBDA(row, PRODUCT(row)))` | 1000; 800; 480 |
| `=LET(big, LAMBDA(x, x >= 1000), FILTER(B1:B12, MAP(E1:E12, big)))` | Desk; Desk |

`LET` can name a `LAMBDA` and call it later. An uncalled `LAMBDA` returns
`#CALC!`, and a call with the wrong number of arguments returns `#VALUE!`. Calls
nest up to 64 deep.

## Describe: statistics and ranking

| Formula | Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `=TRIMMEAN(E1:E12, 0.2)` | 587 | Mean revenue without the top and bottom 10% |
| `=PERCENTILE.EXC(E1:E12, 0.9)` | 1175 | 90th percentile order |
| `=RANK.AVG(E2, E1:E12)` | 3 | The South chair order is the third largest |
| `=SKEW(E1:E12)` | 0.784 | Revenue has a tail of large orders |
| `=FREQUENCY(E1:E12, {500, 1000})` | 6; 5; 1 | Orders up to 500, up to 1,000, and above |
| `=MODE.MULT({4, 10, 6, 4, 15, 10, 8})` | 4; 10 | Every most frequent value |

## Forecast: regression

Monthly revenue for six months was 1200, 1350, 1500, 1580, 1700, and 1850.

| Formula | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `=FORECAST.LINEAR(7, {1200,1350,1500,1580,1700,1850}, {1,2,3,4,5,6})` | 1968 |
| `=TREND({1200;1350;1500;1580;1700;1850}, {1;2;3;4;5;6}, {7;8;9})` | 1968; 2093.14; 2218.29 |
| `=LINEST({1200;1350;1500;1580;1700;1850}, {1;2;3;4;5;6})` | 125.14, 1092 (slope, intercept) |

`LINEST` and `LOGEST` accept more than one predictor column, the `const`
argument, and `stats = TRUE` for five rows of fit statistics. `TREND` and
`GROWTH` project new values from the same fit.

## Estimate risk: distributions

| Formula | Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `=NORM.INV(0.95, 1000, 120)` | 1197.38 | Demand that covers 95% of days, with mean 1000 and deviation 120 |
| `=BINOM.DIST(3, 10, 0.2, FALSE)` | 0.2013 | Chance of exactly 3 returns in 10 orders at a 20% return rate |
| `=CONFIDENCE.T(0.05, STDEV.S(E1:E12), 12)` | 193.05 | Half-width of the 95% interval for mean revenue |

The engine has 36 distribution functions: normal, Student t, chi-squared, F,
binomial, Poisson, exponential, gamma, beta, lognormal, and Weibull, with their
inverses.

## Plan money: finance

| Formula | Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `=XIRR(H1:H4, I1:I4)` | 0.3897 | Annual return of irregular cash flows (39%) |
| `=XNPV(0.08, H1:H4, I1:I4)` | 1999.96 | Their value today at 8% a year |
| `=PMT(0.06/12, 36, -25000)` | 760.55 | Monthly payment on a 25,000 loan over 3 years at 6% |
| `=CUMIPMT(0.06/12, 36, 25000, 1, 12, 0)` | −1286.73 | Interest paid in the first year of that loan |

The full engine also has `MIRR`, `NPER`, `CUMPRINC`, `EFFECT`, `NOMINAL`, and
depreciation functions (`SLN`, `DB`, `DDB`, `SYD`).

## Schedule: working days and dates

| Formula | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `=NETWORKDAYS.INTL(DATE(2026,1,1), DATE(2026,1,31), 1)` | 22 working days |
| `=WORKDAY.INTL(DATE(2026,1,30), 5, "0000011")` | 46059, that is 2026-02-06 |
| `=DATEDIF(DATE(2024,3,15), DATE(2026,1,5), "m")` | 21 full months |
| `=ISOWEEKNUM(DATE(2026,1,5))` | 2 |

The weekend argument is a number or a seven-character mask that starts on
Monday: `"0000011"` means Saturday and Sunday. A holiday range is the optional
last argument.

## Clean text: split, extract, and regex

| Formula | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `=TEXTSPLIT("North,South,East", ",")` | North, South, East (spills across) |
| `=TEXTBEFORE(G1, ";")` | Ref INV-1042 |
| `=TEXTAFTER(G1, "; ")` | ship by Friday |
| `=REGEXEXTRACT(G1, "INV-[0-9]+")` | INV-1042 |
| `=REGEXREPLACE(G4, "[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}", "***-****")` | Ref INV-1045; call \*\*\*-\*\*\*\* |
| `=REGEXTEST(G6, "ship by")` | TRUE |
| `=ARRAYTOTEXT({"North", "South"})` | North, South |

Regex uses the regex-lite syntax. Patterns with lookaround, backreferences, or
Unicode classes return `#VALUE!`, never a wrong match. Case-insensitive matching
folds ASCII letters only.

## Reshape arrays

| Formula | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `=VSTACK({"Region","Units"}, HSTACK(A1:A3, C1:C3))` | A header row on top of North 4, South 10, North 6 |
| `=TAKE(SORTBY(HSTACK(B1:B12, E1:E12), E1:E12, -1), 3)` | Desk 1250, Desk 1000, Chair 800 |
| `=WRAPROWS(SEQUENCE(6), 3)` | 1, 2, 3 / 4, 5, 6 |
| `=TOCOL({1,2;3,4})` | 1; 2; 3; 4 |
| `=EXPAND({1,2;3,4}, 3, 3, 0)` | The 2 × 2 array padded to 3 × 3 with 0 |

`SORTBY` keeps equal items in their order. `TOCOL` and `TOROW` can skip blanks
and errors and read by row or by column.

## Query tables: database functions

Database functions take a table with a header row, a field, and a criteria table
with the same headers. Criteria columns use AND, and criteria rows use OR.

| Formula | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `=DSUM({"Region","Units";"North",4;"South",10;"North",6}, "Units", {"Region";"North"})` | 10 |
| `=DAVERAGE({"Region","Units";"North",4;"South",10;"North",6}, "Units", {"Region";"North"})` | 5 |

In a workbook, the table and the criteria are usually ranges, such as
`=DSUM(A1:E200, "Revenue", H1:H2)`.

## Matrices

| Formula | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `=MMULT({1,2;3,4}, {5;6})` | 17; 39 |
| `=MINVERSE({4,7;2,6})` | 0.6, −0.7 / −0.2, 0.4 |
| `=MDETERM({4,7;2,6})` | 10 |
| `=SUMSQ(C1:C3)` | 152 |

## Limits

- All these functions use the normal spill, shape, memory, and work limits. A
result that does not fit returns an error, not a partial result.
- `AGGREGATE` options that skip hidden rows have no effect, because formulas do
not see hidden-row state.
- Each family's exact argument rules are in the
[formula function contract](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/formula-functions/).

## Full formula engine

Sheetwrite has two engine builds with the same API. `@sheetwrite/wasm` is the default engine: it has the standard function set and the smallest download. `@sheetwrite/formulas` is the full engine: the same engine with the analysis families below. An app selects one engine, one time, before it creates a Grid or a store:

```ts
import { initSheetwrite } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import * as formulas from "@sheetwrite/formulas";

await initSheetwrite(undefined, formulas);
```

| Family | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Distributions | `NORM.DIST`, `T.INV.2T`, `CHISQ.DIST.RT`, `BINOM.DIST`, `GAMMA.INV`, `CONFIDENCE.T` |
| Descriptive statistics | `TRIMMEAN`, `PERCENTILE.EXC`, `RANK.AVG`, `SKEW`, `KURT`, `FORECAST.LINEAR` |
| Regression | `LINEST`, `LOGEST`, `TREND`, `GROWTH`, `FREQUENCY`, `MODE.MULT` |
| Finance | `XIRR`, `XNPV`, `MIRR`, `NPER`, `CUMIPMT`, `DDB` |
| Dates | `NETWORKDAYS.INTL`, `WORKDAY.INTL`, `DATEDIF`, `ISOWEEKNUM` |
| Text and regex | `TEXTSPLIT`, `TEXTBEFORE`, `TEXTAFTER`, `REGEXEXTRACT`, `REGEXREPLACE`, `ARRAYTOTEXT` |
| Database | `DSUM`, `DAVERAGE`, `DCOUNT`, `DGET`, `DMAX`, `DSTDEV` |
| Math and matrices | `AGGREGATE`, `MMULT`, `MINVERSE`, `MDETERM`, `SUMSQ`, `COMBIN` |
| Reshaping | `SORTBY`, `HSTACK`, `VSTACK`, `TOCOL`, `WRAPROWS`, `EXPAND` |
| LAMBDA | `LAMBDA`, `MAP`, `REDUCE`, `SCAN`, `BYROW`, `BYCOL`, `MAKEARRAY`, `ISOMITTED` |
| Grouping | `GROUPBY`, `PIVOTBY`, `PERCENTOF` |

The default engine returns `#NAME?` for these functions, and formula assist does not suggest them. The [formula analysis showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/formulas/) runs thirteen panels of them live over 20,000 orders, and the [analysis formulas guide](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/analysis-formulas/) shows each family with examples.

Limits of the full engine:

- `LAMBDA` parameters bind lexically, and `LET` can bind a `LAMBDA`. An uncalled `LAMBDA` returns `#CALC!`. A call with the wrong number of arguments returns `#VALUE!`. Calls are limited to a depth of 64 and 2,000,000 work units per outer helper; more returns `#NUM!`.
- `GROUPBY` and `PIVOTBY` accept one built-in function name, such as `SUM`, or a `LAMBDA` with one or two parameters. A vector of functions, such as `HSTACK(SUM,AVERAGE)`, returns `#VALUE!`.
- Regex functions do not support lookaround, backreferences, or Unicode classes. Such patterns return `#VALUE!`, never a wrong match.
- `AGGREGATE` options that skip hidden rows have no effect, because formulas do not see hidden-row state.

### Analysis

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/analysis/

- [Pivot tables](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/analysis/pivot-tables/): Summarize a range or table into a pivot table with rows, columns, values and filters, edit it from the field list, and keep it through undo and sync.
- [Charts](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/analysis/charts/): Add column, bar, line, area, pie, doughnut and scatter charts that read cell ranges and redraw when those cells change; place, move and edit them in the grid.

### Pivot tables

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/analysis/pivot-tables/

```ts
grid.setPivot({
  id: "revenue",
  name: "Revenue",
  source: { range: { sheet: "orders", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 4, col: 2 } } },
  anchor: { row: 0, col: 0 },
  rows: [0], // Month
  columns: [1], // Region
  values: [{ field: 2, aggregation: "SUM" }], // Revenue
}, "summary");
```

| Month | Americas | EMEA | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | Sum of Revenue | Sum of Revenue | Sum of Revenue |
| 2026-01 | 120 | 80 | 200 |
| 2026-02 | 140 | 60 | 200 |
| Total | 260 | 140 | 400 |

[Try it live: a pivot and a chart over two years of orders](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/analysis/).

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (!host) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "320px";

// Pivot tables need the full engine.
await initSheetwrite(undefined, await import("@sheetwrite/formulas"));

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "summary",
  sheets: [
    {
      id: "orders",
      name: "Orders",
      rowCount: 5,
      columns: [
        { key: "month", header: "Month", width: 96, type: "text" },
        { key: "region", header: "Region", width: 96, type: "text" },
        { key: "revenue", header: "Revenue", width: 96, type: "number" },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: "summary",
      name: "Summary",
      rowCount: 10,
      columns: ["a", "b", "c", "d"].map((key) => ({ key, header: "", width: 96, type: "text" as const })),
    },
  ],
};
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook });

// The first source row holds the field names.
const rows = [
  ["Month", "Region", "Revenue"],
  ["2026-01", "Americas", 120],
  ["2026-01", "EMEA", 80],
  ["2026-02", "Americas", 140],
  ["2026-02", "EMEA", 60],
];
grid.applyTransaction({
  patches: rows.flatMap((cells, row) =>
    cells.map((value, col) => ({
      op: "set" as const,
      addr: { sheet: "orders", row, col },
      value: { kind: "literal" as const, value },
    })),
  ),
});

grid.setPivot({
  id: "revenue",
  name: "Revenue",
  source: { range: { sheet: "orders", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 4, col: 2 } } },
  anchor: { row: 0, col: 0 },
  rows: [0],
  columns: [1],
  values: [{ field: 2, aggregation: "SUM" }],
}, "summary");
```

A pivot table summarizes a source range or a workbook table into groups. The
pivot definition is part of the document. The full engine calculates the
output, and updates it when source cells change: an edit updates only the
groups that the edited rows belong to. `PIVOTBY` is a formula and is separate:
it does not create a pivot table.

## Insert and edit in the grid

Grids with the ribbon have **Insert › PivotTable**. It takes the selection, or
the table that holds it, as the source, and asks for the destination: a new
sheet or a cell. Then the field list opens in the side panel.

- Drag fields into **Rows**, **Columns**, **Values** and **Filters**, or use the
actions menu on each field to move it with the keyboard.
- A value field has an aggregation, and a row or column field has a sort order.
- Each change is one undo step. Select a cell in a pivot's output, or
right-click it and choose **PivotTable Fields**, to open its field list again.
Hosts can do the same with `grid.actions.showPivotFields()`.

With the default engine, **Insert › PivotTable** is disabled, and its tooltip
says that pivot tables need the full engine.

## Define a pivot

A pivot belongs to the sheet that holds its anchor cell. Commit the complete
definition with `setPivot`. A second `setPivot` with the same `id` replaces the
definition. Each call is one undo entry.

```ts
grid.setPivot({
  id: "sales-by-region",
  name: "Sales by region",
  // The first range row holds the field names.
  source: { range: { sheet: "orders", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 500, col: 4 } } },
  anchor: { row: 1, col: 1 },
  rows: [0],
  columns: [1],
  values: [{ field: 4, aggregation: "SUM", name: "Revenue" }],
  filters: [{ field: 2, values: ["Desk", "Chair"] }],
  sort: [{ axis: "rows", field: 0, descending: false }],
});

grid.removePivot("sales-by-region");
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | A stable ID, unique in the workbook. |
| `source` | A range with its header row, or `{ table: tableId }` for a workbook table. A table source excludes the header and totals rows. |
| `anchor` | The top-left output cell on the owning sheet. |
| `rows`, `columns` | Source field indices that group the output rows and columns, outermost first. A field can be on one axis only. |
| `values` | Aggregated fields: `SUM`, `COUNT`, `AVERAGE`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `COUNTA` or `DISTINCTCOUNT`. These use the `PIVOTBY` semantics. `SUM` and `AVERAGE` round the exact sum one time. `PIVOTBY` rounds after each value, so the results can be different. |
| `filters` | Keep-lists: a source row contributes only if its value is in the list. |
| `sort` | The label order of axis fields. Fields without a key sort ascending. |
| `rowTotals` | The grand-total row at the bottom. Default `true`. |
| `columnTotals` | The grand-total column at the right. Default `true`. |
| `subtotals` | Subtotal rows and columns for multi-field axes. Default `true`. |
| `layout` | `"compact"` (one label column) or `"tabular"` (one label column per row field). Default `"compact"`. |

A field index is an offset in the source: column `range.start.col + i`, or
table column `i`. Invalid definitions are rejected before the document
changes. Limits: 1,000 pivots in a workbook, 256 entries in each list, and
10,000 filter values in one pivot.

## Build your own field list

The side panel uses public methods, so a host can build its own field list. It
reads plain data and never reads engine structures.

- `getPivots(sheet?)` returns copies of the definitions. It does not need the
engine.
- `getPivotFields(sheet, id)` returns the source fields as
`{ index, header, type }`. The type is `number`, `text`, `boolean`, `mixed`
or `blank`.
- `getPivotResult(sheet, id)` returns the output: `status`, `anchor`, `rows`,
`cols`, `headerRows`, `labelCols` and the cell values in row-major order. The
status is `ok`, `saved`, `error` (with `error`, for example `#SPILL!`), or
`unavailable`.

The store has the same methods. The full engine calculates pivots. Select it
as shown in [Analysis formulas](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/analysis-formulas/). With the
default engine, the document keeps, saves, undoes and synchronizes the same
definitions. It shows values saved by Excel without recalculating the pivot.
`getPivotResult` reports `saved` for those values, or `unavailable` when no
saved output exists. `getPivotFields` returns an empty list. `setPivot` removes
saved output because it no longer matches the changed definition.

## Output

The output starts at the anchor and fills cells to the right and down, like a
spill. If source cells, formulas, another spill or another pivot are in the
way, the anchor shows `#SPILL!`. The pivot appears when the blocking cells are
cleared. Output that would cover its own source also shows `#SPILL!`.

Output cells are read-only. A local edit that writes a value into them is
rejected with a `pivot-output` mutation issue. Undo and redo are not checked:
a value that undo puts back blocks the pivot, and the anchor shows `#SPILL!`.

## Row and column edits

Edits keep pivots up to date, with the same rules as formula references:

- Rows or columns inserted or deleted around the source move or resize it.
Inside a range source, a deleted column removes its field from the pivot,
and the other field indices move with their columns.
- When the whole source disappears (every source row or column is deleted, or
the source sheet or table is removed), the pivot is kept. Its source gets
`invalid: true` and keeps the old reference. The anchor shows `#REF!`.
- When the row or column of the anchor is deleted, the pivot is kept. The
anchor moves to the first remaining row or column at the deleted position.
- If a structural edit moves two anchors to the same cell, both definitions
remain saved and both results report `#SPILL!`. Moving one anchor away lets
the engine retry. An explicit local `setPivot` cannot choose an occupied
anchor.

Undo restores the exact definition from before the edit.

### Differences from Excel

These Excel behaviors are not verified against Excel yet:

- Excel refuses a delete that cuts through part of a PivotTable. Sheetwrite
accepts it and draws the output again at the new position.
- Excel removes a PivotTable when whole rows or columns that cover it are
deleted. Sheetwrite keeps the pivot and moves its anchor.

## Snapshots and collaboration

Definitions are in `sheet.pivots` of the workbook snapshot. Snapshot
validation checks pivot references after it reads all sheets and tables, so a
pivot can refer to a sheet that comes later in the snapshot. A reference to a
missing sheet or table is an error unless the source is `invalid`.

The operations are `{ op: "setPivot", sheet, pivot }` and
`{ op: "removePivot", sheet, id }`. They synchronize like other document
operations. Two pending changes to the same pivot ID conflict during rebase.
`releaseEngineMemory` keeps the definitions and installs them in the new
engine.

## XLSX saves

Represented pivots remain pivot definitions when an imported workbook is edited
and saved. Supported definitions are written as native XLSX pivot tables and
caches. Definitions that cannot be written natively are preserved in Sheetwrite
metadata, with a warning; Excel does not calculate that metadata-only output.

The reader captures Excel's rendered pivot values in `pivot.savedOutput` and
removes them from ordinary source cells. The default engine installs those
values as read-only calculated output, so cell reads and formulas can use
them. The full engine ignores saved values and calculates fresh output.
Loading either engine does not change the document. Snapshots and
collaboration carry the same saved output across engines. XLSX export writes
saved output back when no fresh rendered values replace it.

Unsupported or opaque imported pivots are different: their original parts are
preserved only while the workbook is unchanged. Editing the workbook drops those
opaque parts under the XLSX preservation policy (#179), with a warning. This does
not drop represented pivot definitions.

### Charts

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/analysis/charts/

```ts
import { registerChartsBackend } from "@sheetwrite/charts";

registerChartsBackend();
grid.setChart({
  id: "revenue",
  kind: "line",
  title: "Revenue",
  anchor: { row: 0, col: 3, offsetX: 0, offsetY: 0, width: 480, height: 288 },
  series: [{
    nameRange: { sheet: "s", start: { row: 0, col: 1 }, end: { row: 0, col: 1 } },
    values: { sheet: "s", start: { row: 1, col: 1 }, end: { row: 3, col: 1 } },
    categories: { sheet: "s", start: { row: 1, col: 0 }, end: { row: 3, col: 0 } },
  }],
});
```

| Month | Revenue |
| --- | --- |
| Jan | 120 |
| Feb | 95 |
| Mar | 140 |

[Try it live: a chart over a pivot of two years of orders](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/analysis/).

Full setup

```ts
import { registerChartsBackend } from "@sheetwrite/charts";
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (!host) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "360px";

await initSheetwrite();
// Without this call a chart shows as a frame with its title.
registerChartsBackend();

const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "s",
  sheets: [{ id: "s", name: "Sales", rowCount: 4, columns: [
    { key: "month", header: "Month", width: 96, type: "text" },
    { key: "revenue", header: "Revenue", width: 96, type: "number" },
  ] }],
};
const grid = createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  data: { rowCount: 4, columns: {
    month: ["Month", "Jan", "Feb", "Mar"],
    revenue: ["Revenue", 120, 95, 140],
  } },
});

const result = grid.setChart({
  id: "revenue",
  kind: "line",
  title: "Revenue",
  anchor: { row: 0, col: 3, offsetX: 0, offsetY: 0, width: 480, height: 288 },
  series: [{
    nameRange: { sheet: "s", start: { row: 0, col: 1 }, end: { row: 0, col: 1 } },
    values: { sheet: "s", start: { row: 1, col: 1 }, end: { row: 3, col: 1 } },
    categories: { sheet: "s", start: { row: 1, col: 0 }, end: { row: 3, col: 0 } },
  }],
});
if (result.status !== "applied") throw new Error("The chart was not added");
```

A chart reads cell ranges. It does not copy their values: when a source cell
changes, by an edit, a formula, a spill or a pivot, the chart redraws. A chart
belongs to a sheet and floats over its cells.

## Add the charts package

Core keeps the chart definitions, and `@sheetwrite/charts` draws them. Install
it and call `registerChartsBackend()` once, before or after you create grids.
To register by import only, import `@sheetwrite/charts/register`.

```sh
npm install @sheetwrite/charts
```

Without the package, the document still keeps, saves, undoes and synchronizes
charts, and each one shows as a plain frame with its title. Grids that have no
charts do not load chart code.

## Define a chart

Commit the complete definition with `setChart(chart, sheet?)`. A second call
with the same `id` on the same sheet replaces the chart. Each call is one undo
step and returns the transaction result, so a rejected chart reports why.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | A stable ID, unique on its sheet. |
| `kind` | `column`, `bar`, `line`, `area`, `pie`, `doughnut` or `scatter`. |
| `title` | Text above the chart. Without it, the chart has no title. |
| `axes` | `{ xTitle, yTitle }`, the axis titles. |
| `legend` | `none`, `top`, `right`, `bottom` or `left`. |
| `anchor` | The top-left cell (`row`, `col`), the offset from that cell, and the size, all in CSS pixels. |
| `series` | One entry for each series: `values`, optional `categories`, and a `name` or a `nameRange`. |

Ranges can be on any sheet. Pie and doughnut charts draw the first series.
Scatter charts use numeric categories as x values.

- `getCharts(sheet?)` returns copies of the definitions.
- `removeChart(id, sheet?)` removes a chart as one undo step.
- `selectChart(id, sheet?)` selects a chart, and `null` clears the selection.

Limits: 100 charts on a sheet, 32 series in a chart, and 10,000 points in a
source range. A longer range draws its first 10,000 cells and shows a note.

## What the chart shows

- Text, booleans, errors and empty cells are gaps, not zeros.
- Axis labels use the number format of the source cells.
- A deleted source range becomes `#REF!`, and the chart shows a note.
- Dense line, area and scatter series are thinned to the lowest and highest
value in each horizontal pixel, so a 10,000-point series stays fast.
- Screen readers announce a chart by its title and kind. The chart image inside
it has a description that lists the series.

## Insert and edit in the grid

Grids with the ribbon have **Insert › Chart**. Its face makes a column chart
from the selection, and its menu makes any of the seven kinds. A text first row
gives the series names, and a text first column gives the categories. The chart
panel opens beside the grid, where you change the kind, the ranges and the
titles. Each change is one undo step.

Right-click a chart, or press Shift+F10 on a selected chart, for **Edit chart**
and **Delete chart**.

Click a chart to select it. Drag it to move it, or drag a handle to resize it.
On a read-only grid you can select a chart, but not change it.

| Key | Action on the selected chart |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Move by one pixel |
| Shift+arrow keys | Move by one cell |
| Enter | Open the chart panel |
| Delete or Backspace | Remove the chart |
| Escape | Return to the grid |

The grid emits `chart-select` with `{ sheet, id }`, or `null`, when the
selection changes, and `chart-activate` when Enter is pressed on a chart.

## Colors

Series take their colors in order from `--sheetwrite-chart-1` to
`--sheetwrite-chart-8`. The defaults have enough contrast on light and dark
themes. Set the variables on the grid's host element to use your palette.

## Live data without a grid

A host that draws its own charts can read the same live data.
`createChartViewCache(store)` from `@sheetwrite/charts` returns resolved views:
the values, categories and number formats of each series. It notifies its
listeners when a chart's data changes, and gives no notice for edits to other
cells.

### Collaboration and offline work

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/

Sheetwrite provides transport-, database-, and authentication-neutral collaboration primitives. The host still owns server sequencing, durable document storage, user identity, authorization, and network lifecycle.

## Load, mount, queue, and acknowledge

```ts
const edit = (col: number, value: number) =>
  grid.applyTransaction({
    patches: [{ op: "set", addr: { sheet: grid.getActiveSheet(), row: 0, col },
      value: { kind: "literal", value } }],
  });

edit(0, 10);
edit(1, 20);
console.log(sync.pendingCommits().map((record) => [record.baseVersion, record.status]));

await sync.flush(); // sends in order; each response acknowledges only its mutation ID
console.log(sync.pendingCommits().length); // 0
```

| Moment | `sync.pendingCommits()` | `acknowledged` events |
| --- | --- | --- |
| After the two edits | edit 1: `baseVersion` 41, `status` `"pending"`edit 2: `baseVersion` 42, `status` `"pending"` | none |
| After `flush()` | empty | edit 1: `version` 42edit 2: `version` 43 |

Result with a server that applies both commits: the grid shows both edits at once, and the queue keeps them until each `applied` response acknowledges its own `clientMutationId`.

[Try it live → Collaboration showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/collaboration/). Two live clients share one sequencing server; edit offline, reconnect, and watch the queue drain in order.

Full setup

```ts
import {
  createGridFromSnapshot,
  SyncCoordinator,
  type PersistenceAdapter,
  type RemoteOperationSource,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";

const documentId = "workbook-42";
const snapshot = await persistenceAdapter.load(documentId);
const grid = createGridFromSnapshot(document.querySelector("#grid")!, snapshot);
const sync = new SyncCoordinator(grid, persistenceAdapter, {
  documentId,
  serverVersion: snapshot.version ?? 0,
});

sync.on((event) => {
  if (event.type === "acknowledged") {
    console.log(`server version ${event.version} acknowledged ${event.clientMutationId}`);
  } else if (event.type === "conflict") {
    console.error("conflict retained for host recovery", event.mutation);
  }
});

await sync.ready();
const unsubscribeRemote = sync.subscribe(remoteOperationSource);

saveButton.addEventListener("click", () => {
  void sync.flush(); // sends in order; each response acknowledges only its mutation ID
});

// Teardown:
// unsubscribeRemote();
// sync.destroy();
// grid.destroy();
```

Load a validated snapshot before mounting, then let one `SyncCoordinator`
observe local grid transactions, as the Full setup does. Do not also save
`event.changes`: that list is cell-oriented rollback detail and omits document
metadata operations.

`SyncCoordinator` subscribes to `Grid` changes itself. Local rendering remains
optimistic; the host controls when to call `sendNext`, `flush`, or `retry`.
`applied` and `duplicate` responses acknowledge the matching operations and
remove that mutation. A transport error leaves the immutable record pending.

An HTTP adapter can stay transport-neutral at the core boundary:

```ts
import type {
  PersistenceAdapter,
  PersistenceBatchCommitRequest,
  PersistenceCommitRequest,
  PersistenceCommitResponse,
  WorkbookSnapshot,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";

async function responseJson<T>(response: Response): Promise<T> {
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Persistence request failed: ${response.status}`);
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

const persistenceAdapter: PersistenceAdapter = {
  async load(documentId, signal) {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/documents/${encodeURIComponent(documentId)}`, { signal });
    return responseJson<WorkbookSnapshot>(response);
  },
  async commit(request: PersistenceCommitRequest) {
    const { signal, ...body } = request;
    const response = await fetch(`/api/documents/${encodeURIComponent(request.documentId)}/operations`, {
      method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal,
    });
    return responseJson<PersistenceCommitResponse>(response);
  },
  // Required for undo of very large edits; see "Large undo and atomic batches".
  async commitBatch(request: PersistenceBatchCommitRequest) {
    const { signal, ...body } = request;
    const response = await fetch(`/api/documents/${encodeURIComponent(request.documentId)}/operation-batches`, {
      method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal,
    });
    return responseJson<PersistenceCommitResponse>(response);
  },
};
```

The server must authenticate the request, authorize every operation, validate
the document schema/policy, and assign the version. Client protection metadata
is not authorization.

## Database-neutral server model

A snapshot plus append-only operation log is the default persistence shape:

```sql
documents(
  document_id       primary key,
  current_version   integer not null,
  snapshot_version  integer not null,
  snapshot_json     json not null
)

document_operations(
  document_id        not null,
  version            integer not null,
  client_mutation_id text not null,
  operations_json    json not null,
  created_at         server_timestamp not null,
  primary key(document_id, version),
  unique(document_id, client_mutation_id)
)
```

Handle `commit()` in one database transaction:

1. Return `duplicate` with the existing version when
`(document_id, client_mutation_id)` already exists.
2. Lock/read the document version. If it differs from `baseVersion`, return
`conflict` with ordered operations since base or a current snapshot.
3. Validate and authorize the submitted `DocumentOp[]` on the server.
4. Append at `current_version + 1`, update the document version, and return
`applied` with the same mutation ID.
5. Periodically fold the log into `snapshot_json`; never rewrite operation
versions or accept client-authored server timestamps.

Handle `commitBatch()` the same way, with one difference: the request has
`versionOperationCounts`, and it fills several consecutive versions. In one
database transaction, check the duplicate and the base version once, validate
every version, then append all of them or none. Store each version with its
`batch: { index, count }` position, and acknowledge with the last version.

Normalized cell tables are an alternative for products that need SQL queries
over cell values. They do not replace the protocol: the host must still
reconstruct a complete schema-versioned `WorkbookSnapshot`, preserve formula
source/style/metadata, and serialize structural operations under one document
version. Mixing independent cell writes with the operation log breaks atomic
row/column/formula semantics.

## Large undo and atomic batches

Undo of a large clear restores the old cells. When the ordinary `setBlock`
operation is too large for one version, the Grid sends one `restoreBlock`
operation instead: the same cells as compressed JSON (`deflate-json-v1`). If
even that does not fit one version, the Grid splits the restore into an atomic
batch of up to 16 versions and 64 MiB. Undo stays one history step and one
`change` event.

Before you accept 0.5.0 clients, make sure that your server:

1. accepts `restoreBlock` wherever it switches over the `DocumentOp` union, and
decodes it as untrusted input. `@sheetwrite/core` does not export a server
decoder, so your decoder must do these checks, in this order, before it
changes the document:
- `encoding` is `"deflate-json-v1"`, and `decodedBytes` is a positive
integer of at most 64 MiB;
- `data` is canonical base64 (it decodes and re-encodes to the same text);
- the raw DEFLATE stream inflates into a buffer of exactly `decodedBytes`
bytes. Never inflate without that output limit: a small stream can expand
to gigabytes. Reject a stream that ends early or has bytes left over;
- the bytes are valid UTF-8 JSON of a `PackedCellBlock` whose row and
column counts match `range`, with at most 4,000,000 cells;
- every value, formula, reference, and style in the block passes the same
validation as a `setBlock` operation;
2. implements `commitBatch` as above, or accepts that `SyncCoordinator`
rejects a local step that needs more than one version;
3. publishes batch members with their `batch` field, so that peers apply the
whole batch at once; and
4. folds `restoreBlock` into snapshots as ordinary cells. Snapshots never
store restore streams.

The [document operations reference](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/document-operations/#atomic-multi-version-batches)
has the exact field rules, limits, and error codes. When an undo is above the
transaction limits even after this, the Grid changes nothing and reports it;
see [Interaction](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/#undo-and-redo).

## Durable pending commits

`SyncCoordinator` can receive a `PendingCommitStorage` adapter. With one configured, it:

1. persists each immutable commit before it can be sent;
2. restores pending commits on startup and reapplies them locally as remote-source operations, so restoration does not echo into the outgoing queue;
3. retries with the original `clientMutationId` after reconnect or reload;
4. removes durable work only after an `applied` or `duplicate` acknowledgement; and
5. retains conflicts and storage failures for explicit host recovery.

Await `coordinator.ready()` before declaring startup synchronized. Use `initialConnection: "offline"` for offline-first startup, `setOnline(false)` on disconnect, and `setOnline(true)` to reconnect and drain pending work in order. `coordinator.state` distinguishes connection state from hydration, persistence, sending, conflict, and error activity.

The browser IndexedDB implementation is intentionally isolated from Node and SSR entrypoints:

```ts
import { SyncCoordinator } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import { IndexedDbPendingCommitStorage } from "@sheetwrite/core/browser";

const pendingStorage = new IndexedDbPendingCommitStorage({
  databaseName: "my-product-sheetwrite",
});

const sync = new SyncCoordinator(grid, persistenceAdapter, {
  documentId: "workbook-42",
  serverVersion: snapshot.version ?? 0,
  pendingStorage,
  initialConnection: navigator.onLine ? "online" : "offline",
});

await sync.ready();
window.addEventListener("online", () => sync.setOnline(true));
window.addEventListener("offline", () => sync.setOnline(false));
```

IndexedDB record migration is versioned. Unsupported future schemas, blocked upgrades, quota exhaustion, transaction failures, and aborts surface as typed `IndexedDbPendingCommitStorageError` codes. Core continues to work without IndexedDB when no durable adapter is supplied.

## Remote operations and version gaps

`SyncCoordinator.subscribe` accepts either `RemoteOperationSource` or `AsyncIterable<VersionedOperation>`. Operations apply only at `serverVersion + 1`; own echoed mutation IDs and already acknowledged IDs are deduplicated. Remote application uses `Grid.applyRemoteOperations`, so it does not create outgoing dirty work or local undo entries. Remote row and column inserts and deletes move existing undo entries, so a later undo restores the cell the user edited.

A gap emits `reload-required`. Prefer fetching missing ordered operations through
`recoverVersionGap`; the coordinator applies them in sequence. A returned
snapshot is a host remount signal, not an automatic store replacement.
`resumeAfterReload(snapshot)` updates retained queue base versions only after the
host has installed that snapshot and reapplied local work; it does not hydrate a
grid or attach the coordinator to a newly created grid.

### Conflict and snapshot reload

Never acknowledge or discard a conflicted mutation implicitly. First call
`sync.recoverConflict()`. It recovers on the live Grid, without a reload, when
the server returns `operationsSinceBase`, the pending work and the server
versions it did not see change different cells and sheets, and neither side
inserts, deletes, or moves rows or columns. It applies the missed versions,
moves the queue onto the server head, and emits `recovered`; call
`sync.flush()` to resend:

```ts
import type { PersistenceCommitResponse, SyncConflictReloadReason } from "@sheetwrite/core";

/** Host fallback: the rebase-and-remount recipe below. */
declare function reloadSession(
  response: Extract<PersistenceCommitResponse, { status: "conflict" }>,
  reason: SyncConflictReloadReason,
): Promise<void>;

sync.on((event) => {
  if (event.type !== "conflict") return;
  void sync.recoverConflict().then((result) => {
    if (result.status === "recovered") return sync.flush();
    if (result.status === "reload-required") return reloadSession(event.response, result.reason);
  });
});
```

Otherwise the result is `reload-required` with a reason and nothing changes.
If the server returns both `operationsSinceBase` and a current snapshot, the
host can then gate every pending transaction through the conservative rebaser,
clear the old durable IDs, remount, and submit the safe results as new
mutations:

```ts
import {
  createGridFromSnapshot,
  rebaseDocumentOperations,
  SyncCoordinator,
  type Grid,
  type PersistenceCommitResponse,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";

type ConflictResponse = Extract<PersistenceCommitResponse, { status: "conflict" }>;
interface SyncSession {
  grid: Grid;
  sync: SyncCoordinator;
  unsubscribeRemote: () => void;
}

async function reloadAfterConflict(
  session: SyncSession,
  response: ConflictResponse,
): Promise<SyncSession> {
  if (!response.operationsSinceBase) {
    console.error("Manual conflict review required: server did not return an operation tail");
    return session;
  }

  // Freeze local edits and let queued writes finish before reading the queue.
  session.grid.setReadOnly(true);
  await session.sync.ready();
  const pending = session.sync.pendingCommits();
  const remoteOperations = response.operationsSinceBase.flatMap((entry) => [
    ...entry.operations,
  ]);
  const safeBatches: Array<ReturnType<typeof rebaseDocumentOperations> & {
    status: "rebased";
  }> = [];

  for (const record of pending) {
    const result = rebaseDocumentOperations(record.operations, remoteOperations);
    if (result.status === "conflict") {
      console.error("Manual conflict review required", result.conflict);
      session.grid.setReadOnly(false);
      return session; // old queue and grid remain intact
    }
    safeBatches.push(result);
  }

  const latest = response.snapshot ?? (await persistenceAdapter.load(documentId));
  for (const record of pending) {
    await pendingStorage.remove(documentId, record.clientMutationId);
  }

  session.unsubscribeRemote();
  session.sync.destroy();
  session.grid.destroy();

  const grid = createGridFromSnapshot(document.querySelector("#grid")!, latest);
  const sync = new SyncCoordinator(grid, persistenceAdapter, {
    documentId,
    serverVersion: latest.version ?? 0,
    pendingStorage,
  });
  await sync.ready(); // the stale IDs were removed before hydration

  for (const batch of safeBatches) {
    const outcome = grid.applyTransaction({ patches: [...batch.operations] });
    if (outcome.status !== "applied") {
      throw new Error(`Rebased local transaction was not applied: ${outcome.status}`);
    }
  }

  const unsubscribeRemote = sync.subscribe(remoteOperationSource);
  await sync.flush();
  return { grid, sync, unsubscribeRemote };
}
```

When the rebaser reports `conflict`—overlap, formulas across structural changes,
concurrent moves, or sheet lifecycle ambiguity—keep the original queue and show
product-specific conflict UI. If the server returns only a snapshot, the host
cannot infer a safe transform; offer explicit discard/export/manual re-entry
instead. Reloading a snapshot over pending edits without this decision loses
intent.

Two ordering rules keep recovery from losing work:

- Freeze the Grid and await `sync.ready()` before reading `pendingCommits()`.
An edit made while recovery awaits would be neither rebased nor removed, and
a queue write still in flight could land after its removal. Either comes back
on the remounted client with a stale base version.
- Keep remote operations that arrive between loading `latest` and
`sync.subscribe(...)`, and deliver them to the new coordinator. Drop versions
at or below `latest.version`, which the snapshot already contains. A
transport that only forwards to the current subscriber loses them, and the
client then waits on a version gap that never closes.

## Presence

`PresenceCoordinator` publishes actor metadata, active sheet, and bounded selection ranges through a host `PresenceTransport`. Presence:

- is never written to document operations, snapshots, dirty state, or history;
- expires according to local heartbeat receipt time;
- is bounded by actor and range limits;
- clamps ranges to valid visible grid geometry and hides other-sheet or filtered selections;
- reuses the grid overlay element pool rather than mutating canvas cells; and
- supports privacy controls for display name, selections, inbound presence, and actor filtering.

Presence is advisory UI state. Do not use it for authorization, locking, or conflict prevention.

## Revisions

`RevisionCoordinator` delegates revision listing, loading, and restore to a `RevisionAdapter`. Preview snapshots pass through the optional host schema migrator and mount with `readOnly: true`. Restore requests include `targetVersion`, current `baseVersion`, and a stable mutation ID. The adapter contract requires restore to create a newer auditable server version; it must never rewind database state in place.

## Comments

Comments are document-adjacent server entities, not fields on every cell. `CommentCoordinator` stores stable thread/message IDs and range or cell anchors, while adapters supply authenticated author references and server timestamps. Create, reply, and resolve requests contain no client-authored identity or time fields. Authorization remains entirely host/server-owned.

Comment streams are versioned independently. Out-of-order events emit a gap rather than being applied speculatively.

## Concurrent structural editing decision

Sheetwrite uses deterministic server ordering plus conservative rebase, not a CRDT or general OT layer.

`rebaseDocumentOperations` safely shifts non-overlapping literal edits and references across server-ordered row/column insertions and deletions. It reports explicit conflicts for:

- edits or range pastes overlapping inserted/deleted boundaries;
- targets or references deleted by a concurrent operation;
- formula source crossing structural edits, because text-only rewriting cannot preserve sheet-aware reference intent;
- concurrent row/column moves;
- conflicting sheet lifecycle operations; and
- metadata families that need domain-specific transforms.

This choice preserves stable sheet IDs and authoritative formula source without lossy adapters. A CRDT/OT dependency is not justified by current scenarios: short-lived offline and online collaboration converge under server sequencing, while long-lived offline concurrent structural edits require product-level conflict UX and spreadsheet-specific formula/range semantics that generic sequence CRDTs do not supply. Revisit only if requirements demand automatic preservation of those ambiguous edits and scenario tests define the intended result for every structural/formula case.

### Worker rendering

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/worker-rendering/

By default Sheetwrite paints on the main thread (`renderer: "canvas"`). For sheets
where a busy main thread could stall scrolling, you can move painting onto a Web
Worker with an OffscreenCanvas — same `Renderer` contract, drop-in.

## Enabling it

Set `renderer: "worker"`. With a bundler that understands module workers, that
is all: Sheetwrite creates its worker as
`new Worker(new URL("./worker.js", import.meta.url), { type: "module" })`, the
pattern bundlers look for, so the bundler builds the worker with its imports.
Vite does this, verified by the fixture build in `test/bundler-fixtures/vite`
(`bun run verify:bundlers`). webpack 5 and Parcel recognize the same pattern;
check with the steps under [Verify it actually started](#verify-it-actually-started).

```ts
const grid = createGrid(host, { workbook, datasource, renderer: "worker" });
```

Pass `workerUrl` when the default cannot work: no bundler, or a bundler that
copies the file instead of building it. It must be the worker module's URL
**as the browser will fetch it**. The worker entry ships at
`@sheetwrite/core/dist/worker.js` (export subpath `@sheetwrite/core/worker`),
but the platform `Worker`/`URL` constructors do not consult package exports —
`new URL("@sheetwrite/core/worker", import.meta.url)` treats the bare
specifier as a relative path and produces a 404 URL unless your bundler
happens to rewrite that exact form. Two reliable recipes:

**Universal (any bundler, no bundler):** the worker entry is an ES module with
relative imports (`./canvas-paint.js`, …), so a single-file copy breaks — copy
the package's whole `dist/` directory into your public/static assets and pass
the served `worker.js` URL (a module worker fetches its sibling imports over
HTTP):

```sh
cp -r node_modules/@sheetwrite/core/dist public/sheetwrite
```

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite } from "@sheetwrite/core";

await initSheetwrite();

const grid = createGrid(host, {
  workbook,
  datasource,
  renderer: "worker",
  workerUrl: "/sheetwrite/worker.js",
});
```

**Vite dependency-worker import (machine-verified):** Vite bundles the whole
worker graph into one chunk and returns its URL via the `?worker&url` query —
verified by the fixture build in `test/bundler-fixtures/vite`
(`bun run verify:bundlers`):

```ts
import workerUrl from "@sheetwrite/core/worker?worker&url";
```

`workerUrl` accepts a `string | URL`.

## Verify it actually started

A worker that fails to construct falls back to the main-thread canvas renderer
(see below) — verify instead of assuming:

```ts
grid.on("renderer-fallback", ({ error }) => {
  console.warn("Sheetwrite worker renderer unavailable, using canvas:", error);
});

if (grid.rendererKind() !== "worker") {
  // main-thread rendering is active
}
```

## How it works

- On mount the renderer constructs the `Worker`, creates a `<canvas>`, and
transfers control of it to the worker with `transferControlToOffscreen()`. The
worker paints into that `OffscreenCanvas` off the main thread.
- Layout, theme, viewport, and each painted window are posted to the worker as
messages. The window snapshot is the same typed-array-backed `VisibleWindowView`
the store produces, so it is cheap to transfer.
- Painting therefore continues smoothly even when the main thread is busy.

### Raw string IDs and epochs

Every `VisibleWindowView` carries a store-wide `stringPoolEpoch` (a u32 exposed
as a JavaScript number). Its `stringPoolIds` and `stringPoolUpdateIds` are valid
only in that epoch. Committed string collection can remap IDs: the same numeric
ID may name different text afterward. Never persist raw pool IDs as document
values or retain an ID-to-text cache across an epoch change.

Both transferable and shared-memory frames, including frozen panes, carry the
issuing epoch. The host reader and paint worker invalidate their own caches
before resolving IDs or applying that epoch's string updates. Resolved `values`
and window-local error strings do not require pool lookup; the view still has
its normal lifetime until the next store mutation or window refresh.

Direct WASM readers must compare `WindowView.stringPoolEpoch()` with
`CellStore.stringPoolEpoch()` before passing IDs to `poolStrings`. For raw
`persistedCellData` projections, capture the store epoch alongside the read and
resolve those IDs before any operation that can collect strings. If the epoch
has changed, discard the raw projection and read it again.

## Automatic fallback

The worker is constructed **first**, before the canvas is transferred. If
construction throws — no `OffscreenCanvas` support, or a bundler/security
restriction on the worker URL — the grid switches to the main-thread
`CanvasRenderer` and emits one `renderer-fallback` event with a
`SheetwriteError`. You still get a working grid; worker rendering is an
enhancement, never a hard requirement.

## Limitation: no custom renderers

Custom cell renderers are functions, and functions can not cross the worker
boundary. Under `renderer: "worker"` the `renderers` option (and
`defineCellRenderer`) have no effect — the worker's renderer registry is always
empty. If you rely on custom [`CellRenderer`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/options-and-presentation/#gridoptions)s,
use the main-thread `canvas` renderer.

## See also

- [Configuration](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/options-and-presentation/#gridoptions) for `renderer` and `workerUrl`.
- [Concepts](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/runtime-ownership/#canvas-rendering-and-the-wasm-columnar-store) for the transferable window snapshot.

### Accessibility

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/accessibility/

The grid paints to a `<canvas>`, which assistive technology can not read. To make
it navigable, Sheetwrite maintains a parallel **ARIA shadow tree**: a
visually-hidden DOM mirror of the visible window that carries the grid semantics,
while the canvas itself is hidden from the accessibility tree.

```ts
grid.setSelection({ kind: "cell", addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 } });

// The mirror updates with the next painted frame.
requestAnimationFrame(() => {
  const mirror = host.querySelector(".sheetwrite-aria");
  console.log(host.getAttribute("aria-activedescendant")); // "sheetwrite-grid-1-0-0"
  console.log(mirror?.querySelectorAll('[role="gridcell"]').length); // 4
});
```

| Element | role | ARIA attributes | Text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Host `#grid` | `grid` | `aria-multiselectable="true"` `aria-rowcount="3"` `aria-colcount="2"` `aria-label="Spreadsheet grid"` `aria-activedescendant="sheetwrite-grid-1-0-0"` | |
| Canvas, scroller, overlay | | `aria-hidden="true"` | |
| Mirror `div.sheetwrite-aria#sheetwrite-grid-1` | `rowgroup` | | |
| Header row | `row` | `aria-rowindex="1"` | |
| Header cells | `columnheader` | `aria-colindex="1"`, `"2"` | A, B |
| Data row 1 | `row` | `aria-rowindex="2"` | |
| `#sheetwrite-grid-1-0-0` | `gridcell` | `aria-colindex="1"` `aria-selected="true"` | Widget |
| `#sheetwrite-grid-1-0-1` | `gridcell` | `aria-colindex="2"` | 12 |
| Data row 2 | `row` | `aria-rowindex="3"` | |
| `#sheetwrite-grid-1-1-0`, `-1-1` | `gridcell` | `aria-colindex="1"`, `"2"` | Gadget, 7 |

Result: the hidden mirror for the first grid on the page, with A1 focused. The two data rows plus the column-letter header make `aria-rowcount` 3.

[Try it live → Spreadsheet showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/spreadsheet/). Open your browser's accessibility inspector on the grid to read its mirror while you move the selection.

Full setup

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#grid");
if (host === null) throw new Error("Missing #grid host");
host.style.height = "240px";

await initSheetwrite();
const grid = createGrid(host, {
  workbook: {
    activeSheet: "sheet1",
    sheets: [{
      id: "sheet1", name: "Sheet1", rowCount: 2,
      columns: [
        { key: "product", header: "Product", type: "text", width: 140 },
        { key: "qty", header: "Qty", type: "number", width: 100 },
      ],
    }],
  },
  data: { rowCount: 2, columns: { product: ["Widget", "Gadget"], qty: [12, 7] } },
});

grid.setSelection({ kind: "cell", addr: { sheet: "sheet1", row: 0, col: 0 } });

// The mirror updates with the next painted frame.
requestAnimationFrame(() => {
  const mirror = host.querySelector(".sheetwrite-aria");
  console.log(host.getAttribute("aria-activedescendant")); // "sheetwrite-grid-1-0-0"
  console.log(mirror?.querySelectorAll('[role="gridcell"]').length); // 4
});
```

## The host grid

`createGrid` annotates the host element as the grid:

| Attribute | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `role` | `"grid"` |
| `aria-multiselectable` | `"true"` |
| `aria-rowcount` | total rows **+ 1** (the column-letter header counts as a row) |
| `aria-colcount` | number of visible columns |
| `aria-readonly` | `"true"` when the grid is `readOnly` (omitted otherwise) |
| `aria-label` | `"Spreadsheet grid"` (default; not overwritten if you set your own) |
| `aria-activedescendant` | the id of the focused cell in the mirror |

The visual layers — the scroller, the overlay, and the `<canvas>` — are all marked
`aria-hidden="true"`, so screen readers ignore the pixels and read the mirror.

## The SR-only mirror

Alongside the host the grid appends a visually-hidden `<div class="sheetwrite-aria">`
with a unique id (`sheetwrite-grid-<n>`) and `role="rowgroup"`. It contains:

- A **header row** — `role="row"`, `aria-rowindex="1"` — whose cells are
`role="columnheader"` with a 1-based `aria-colindex`. Spreadsheet presentation
uses the positional column letter (`A`, `B`, …); data-grid presentation uses
the semantic `Column.header`.
- One **data row** per visible row — `role="row"` with `aria-rowindex` set to the
true row position (data row + 2, leaving index 1 for the header). Its cells are
`role="gridcell"` with a 1-based `aria-colindex`, a stable id
(`<gridId>-<row>-<col>`), and the cell's value as text.
- Every visible cell covered by the current cell/range/multi selection carries
`aria-selected="true"`. A row selection marks its visible row; a column
selection marks both its header and visible cells. The focused cell's id is
mirrored into the host's `aria-activedescendant`.

Sketch of the emitted structure:

```html
<div role="grid" aria-multiselectable="true" aria-rowcount="100001" aria-colcount="5"
     aria-activedescendant="sheetwrite-grid-1-0-0" tabindex="0">
  <!-- canvas / scroller / overlay, all aria-hidden -->
  <div class="sheetwrite-aria" id="sheetwrite-grid-1" role="rowgroup">
    <div role="row" aria-rowindex="1">
      <div role="columnheader" aria-colindex="1">A</div>
      <div role="columnheader" aria-colindex="2">B</div>
    </div>
    <div role="row" aria-rowindex="2">
      <div role="gridcell" aria-colindex="1" id="sheetwrite-grid-1-0-0"
           aria-selected="true">Widget</div>
      <div role="gridcell" aria-colindex="2" id="sheetwrite-grid-1-0-1">12</div>
    </div>
    <!-- … one row per visible row … -->
  </div>
</div>
```

As keyboard or pointer input changes the selection, `aria-selected` and the
host's `aria-activedescendant` update. Scrolling rebuilds the visible mirror.
Horizontal virtualization does not renumber the mirror: if the visible window
starts at sheet column G, its header and cells use `aria-colindex="7"`. Frozen
and scrolling columns likewise keep their absolute one-based sheet positions.
A focused cell note is connected through `aria-describedby` to hidden plain text.
Validation list and checkbox editors use real `listbox` / `option` and `checkbox`
semantics, with the rule help text as their accessible label.
Host-supplied editors receive a `context.label` composed from that same
semantic/positional header and row number. Core applies it to the retained editor
wrapper and to the first focusable control when the editor did not provide its
own name. Commit, cancel, reset, and unmount return focus to the grid; teardown
aborts the editor signal before removing its DOM.

Custom DOM renderer output uses the same mirror for its default cell value.
Non-semantic renderer elements are hidden from assistive technology to avoid a
duplicate announcement. A renderer can expose an explicitly interactive,
labelled control; its keyboard events remain with that control, its element is
retained across scroll and geometry updates, and focus returns to the grid if
virtualization or renderer replacement removes it.

## Limitation: the mirror reflects the visible window

The mirror contains **only the rows and columns currently rendered** (the same
virtualized window the canvas paints, plus overscan) — not the entire sheet. This
is deliberate: materializing 100k+ rows of DOM would defeat the point of canvas
rendering.

The consequences to be aware of:

- `aria-rowindex` / `aria-colindex` carry the **true** positions, so assistive
technology can announce "row N of `aria-rowcount`" correctly even though only a
window is present.
- A screen reader's own virtual cursor can only walk the cells in the rendered
window. Use the grid's keyboard navigation (arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End — see
[Interaction](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/#keyboard-navigation)) to move focus; that scrolls
new rows into view and into the mirror, and updates `aria-activedescendant`.

### XLSX import

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-import/

```ts
import { fromXlsxWorkbook, SheetwriteStore } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

declare const bytes: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array;
const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbook(bytes, {
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
});
const importedStore = SheetwriteStore.fromSnapshot(snapshot);
```

For a workbook containing `10`, `20` and `=SUM(A1:A2)` in A1:A3, the imported grid evaluates:

| 10 |
| --- |
| 20 |
| 30 |

The snapshot retains `=SUM(A1:A2)`, not a cached result or a raw formula handle.

[Try it live: import a source workbook](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/interoperability/#fixtures).

Full setup

Install `@sheetwrite/xlsx` and register it on the import path. This complete example makes its own XLSX input:

```ts
import {
  fromXlsxWorkbook, initSheetwrite, SheetwriteStore, toXlsxWorkbook,
  type WorkbookSnapshot,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

await initSheetwrite();
const source: WorkbookSnapshot = {
  schemaVersion: 1,
  workbook: { activeSheet: "s" },
  sheets: [{
    id: "s", name: "Sales", order: 0, rowCount: 3,
    columns: [{ key: "amount", header: "Amount", width: 100, type: "number" }],
    cells: [{ startRow: 0, startCol: 0, rowCount: 3, colCount: 1, cells: [
      { rowOffset: 0, colOffset: 0, value: { kind: "literal", value: 10 } },
      { rowOffset: 1, colOffset: 0, value: { kind: "literal", value: 20 } },
      { rowOffset: 2, colOffset: 0, value: { kind: "formula", src: "=SUM(A1:A2)" } },
    ] }],
  }],
};
const bytes = await toXlsxWorkbook(source);
const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbook(bytes, {
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
});
const importedStore = SheetwriteStore.fromSnapshot(snapshot);
console.log(importedStore.exportSnapshot().sheets[0]?.name); // Sales
```

## Choose an import contract

| Function | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fromXlsxWorkbook(data, options?)` | `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array` | `Promise<WorkbookSnapshot>`; preserves supported workbook state with no header synthesis. |
| `fromXlsxWorkbookFile(file, options?)` | `File` or `Blob` | Same snapshot contract, without first buffering the compressed file. |
| `fromXlsxTable(data, options?)` | `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array` | `Promise<ColumnarData>`; one rectangular table with first-row headers and resolved scalars. |

Table import reads boolean literals. It is not a workbook round-trip API. See the [fidelity table](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#workbook-interchange) for supported workbook state.

Workbook formulas import as source. `SheetwriteStore.fromSnapshot` recompiles them into the selected formula engine; no raw handles enter the serialized snapshot. Import also keeps eligible [opaque parts](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/).

## Warnings

`onWarning` receives `XlsxWorkbookWarning` with `code`, `message`, and optional `sheet`, `cell` and `part`. Rich-text flattening uses `rich-text`; unsupported conditional rules use `format-loss`; dropped unmodelled features use structured warnings such as `unsupported-feature`. Do not assume that a successful import was lossless.

Supported native hyperlinks, conditional formats, tables, validation and notes are not all dropped merely because a file lacks Sheetwrite metadata. Unsupported content still produces warnings. The [checked compatibility results](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/compatibility-results/) distinguish evaluated, preserved, flattened, warning and unsupported behavior by file and producer.

## Hyperlinks

Hyperlinks retain stable IDs in Sheetwrite metadata. Internal targets use stable sheet IDs: a sheet rename does not retarget a link. Removing the destination atomically removes inbound links; undo restores them with the sheet. Activation of stale host-held targets fails closed.

External mutation and activation allow only absolute `https://` and `mailto:` targets. `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`, HTTP, credentials, malformed URLs and internal OOXML relationship traversal are rejected before document mutation or activation.

Sheetwrite never calls `window.open`. Ctrl/Meta-click and `grid.activateHyperlink()` emit `hyperlink-activate` with a validated target. Set `hyperlinkActivation: "internal-navigation"` to also navigate internal targets, or `"disabled"` to suppress activation.

## Conditional formats

Rules run in array order. Earlier rules have style precedence. A matching `stopIfTrue` blocks later rules from the main/Worker match mask. Formula predicates are anchored at the rule range's top-left: relative A1 references move per cell; `$`-absolute components stay fixed.

A sheet supports at most 32 rules (the renderer's deterministic `u32` mask). One predicate formula is limited to 8,192 characters. SpreadsheetML `cellIs`, blank/text and expression rules round-trip with priority and stop behavior. Color scales, data bars, icon sets and unrepresentable differential styles enter neither the live model nor the renderer. Import emits a deterministic `format-loss` warning naming the dropped rule kind.

## Options and limits

Every import path uses `XlsxWorkbookOptions`. Missing registration and codec errors reject with `SheetwriteError`; resource errors remain `XlsxResourceError` and satisfy `isSheetwriteError`. Read error `code` rather than matching installation text. Use [bounded resource options](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/#resource-limits), including cancellation, for untrusted files.

## See also

- [XLSX export](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/)
- [Large files and streaming](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/)
- [LibreOffice compatibility](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/libreoffice-compatibility/)

### XLSX export

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/

```ts
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

await grid.exportXlsx("sales.xlsx");
```

For columns named Customer and Total with one row `Ada, 120`, the table file opens as:

| Customer | Total |
| --- | --- |
| Ada | 120 |

[Try it live: export the workbook](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/interoperability/#xlsx).

Full setup

Install the optional package on the path that needs XLSX:

```sh
npm install @sheetwrite/xlsx
```

Use the workbook API to save an existing store without adding a header row:

```ts
import { downloadBytes, toXlsxWorkbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const bytes = await toXlsxWorkbook(store.exportSnapshot(), {
  maxCells: 250_000,
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
});
downloadBytes(bytes, "workbook.xlsx",
  "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet");
```

## Table interchange

`toXlsxTable(workbook, store, options?)` returns `Promise<Uint8Array>`. `grid.exportXlsx` uses this contract: active sheet only, synthesized first-row column headers, and resolved scalars instead of formula source. Styles, borders, number/date formats, merges, column widths and row heights are preserved on active-sheet export. Frozen panes, active worksheet state and names are not table round-trip state.

## Workbook interchange

`toXlsxWorkbook(snapshot, options?)` returns `Promise<Uint8Array>` from the same `WorkbookSnapshot` used by persistence. It does not synthesize a header row.

| Feature | Workbook result |
| --- | --- |
| Worksheets, order and active sheet | Preserved. |
| Formula source, including cross-sheet formulas | Preserved; requests full recalculation on open. |
| Styles, borders, number/date formats, merges, dimensions and frozen panes | Preserved. |
| Named ranges and native booleans | Preserved. |
| HTTPS/mailto and internal range hyperlinks | Preserved, with stable IDs in Sheetwrite metadata. |
| Supported ordered conditional formats | Native rules preserve priority and stop behavior. |
| Tables | Autofilter rules, sort state, calculated-column formulas and totals-row functions round-trip. |
| Validation | Sheetwrite metadata preserved; supported list/numeric/date/text-length rules also emit native Excel validation. |
| Protected ranges | Metadata preserved; no Excel sheet-protection claim is made. |
| Cell notes | Metadata preserved and native Excel notes emitted. |
| Row groups | Preserved in metadata and emitted as native row outlines with hidden/collapsed state; native outline depth is capped at seven. |
| Rich text | Display text preserved; structured warnings report flattening. |
| Unmodelled package parts | [Kept under explicit edit rules](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/), not automatically discarded. |

Every dropped native feature is reported through `onWarning` (`XlsxWorkbookWarning`). Surface these warnings when fidelity matters. [Import limits and conditional-rule support](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-import/#conditional-formats) describe the supported subset.

## Errors and built-in actions

`grid.exportXlsx(...)` rejects on missing registration or encoding failure and preserves the backend error. The four buffered table/workbook import/export functions are asynchronous. Missing registration and codec failures reject with `SheetwriteError`; inspect `code`, not the installation message. Resource failures remain `XlsxResourceError` instances and satisfy `isSheetwriteError`.

Built-in toolbar and context-menu actions show an alert and emit one `export-error` event with `{ format: "csv" | "xlsx", error }`:

```ts
grid.on("export-error", ({ format, error }) => {
  console.error(`${format} export failed`, error);
});
```

`grid.actions.exportXlsx()` returns a promise that resolves after the command finishes, including when export fails. Built-in buttons ignore repeated starts for the same pending command and show a busy state.

## XLSX backends

Core and framework entry points do not resolve the optional codec. Register it before invoking XLSX functions or framework toolbar actions. A missing backend error names both remedies: install `@sheetwrite/xlsx`, then import `@sheetwrite/xlsx/register`.

The root `@sheetwrite/xlsx` entry is side-effect free. Its `./register` entry registers idempotently. Explicit registration and individual backend composition are also public:

```ts
import {
  registerXlsxBackends,
  sheetwriteTableExportBackend,
  sheetwriteTableImportBackend,
  sheetwriteWorkbookBackend,
} from "@sheetwrite/xlsx";
import {
  setXlsxTableExportBackend,
  setXlsxTableImportBackend,
  setXlsxWorkbookBackend,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";

registerXlsxBackends();
// Or register the roles individually when composing backends.
setXlsxTableExportBackend(sheetwriteTableExportBackend);
setXlsxTableImportBackend(sheetwriteTableImportBackend);
setXlsxWorkbookBackend(sheetwriteWorkbookBackend);
```

Hosts can implement `XlsxWorkbookBackend`, `XlsxTableExportBackend`, or `XlsxTableImportBackend` to replace a role. `@sheetwrite/xlsx` is the only concrete implementation package. Its bounded OOXML codec owns OPC part resolution, XML tokenization, styles and worksheet mapping over the audited compression primitive `fflate`.

## Options and limits

All XLSX paths share `XlsxWorkbookOptions`: `maxCells`, `resourceLimits`, `signal` and `onWarning`. See [resource limits and streaming](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/#resource-limits) before increasing a budget. Buffered export holds its output in memory.

- [CSV and TSV](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/csv-and-tsv/)
- [Detailed compatibility evidence](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/compatibility-results/)
- [`@sheetwrite/xlsx` API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/xlsx/)

### CSV and TSV

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/csv-and-tsv/

```ts
import { fromCsv } from "@sheetwrite/core";

const data = fromCsv("Customer,Total\r\nAda,120\r\nLin,75\r\n", [
  { key: "customer", header: "Customer", width: 140, type: "text" },
  { key: "total", header: "Total", width: 100, type: "number" },
]);
console.log(data.rowCount); // 2
```

| Ada | 120 |
| --- | --- |
| Lin | 75 |

[Try it live: CSV / TSV lab](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/interoperability/#delimited).

Full setup

```ts
import {
  downloadBytes, initSheetwrite, SheetwriteStore, toCsv, toTsv,
  type Workbook,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";

await initSheetwrite();
const workbook: Workbook = {
  activeSheet: "s",
  sheets: [{ id: "s", name: "Sales", rowCount: 2, columns: [
    { key: "customer", header: "Customer", width: 140, type: "text" },
    { key: "total", header: "Total", width: 100, type: "number" },
  ] }],
};
const store = new SheetwriteStore(workbook, {
  rowCount: 2, columns: { customer: ["Ada", "Lin"], total: new Float64Array([120, 75]) },
});
const sheet = workbook.sheets[0];
if (!sheet) throw new Error("Missing Sales sheet");
const csv = toCsv(sheet, store);
const tsv = toTsv({ sheet: "s", start: { row: 0, col: 0 }, end: { row: 1, col: 1 } }, store);
downloadBytes(csv, "sales.csv", "text/csv");
console.log(tsv); // Ada\t120\r\nLin\t75
```

## Functions

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `fromCsv(text, columns, options?)` | Materialized `ColumnarData`; first record consumed as a positional header. |
| `toCsv(sheet, store, options?)` | CSV string for visible columns, with UTF-8 BOM and CRLF line endings. |
| `toTsv(range, store, options?)` | TSV string for an explicit range, suitable for Excel/Sheets clipboard interchange. |
| `grid.exportCsv(filename)` | Synchronous active-sheet download. |
| `downloadBytes(bytes, filename, mime)` | Download a `Uint8Array` or string. |
| `toCsvStream` / `toTsvStream` | [Bounded byte streams](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/) with backpressure and cancellation. |

CSV and TSV are core-only. `fromCsv` projects input fields onto declared visible columns. Hidden declared columns initialize to `null`; extra fields are ignored and missing fields become `null`. It fully materializes the returned table.

## Output and injection safety

`toCsv` follows the current view row order after sorting, filtering, hidden rows and collapsed groups. `toTsv` instead uses canonical data-space coordinates: reversed corners are normalized, and active views do not remap the range. TSV uses CRLF with no BOM and also injection-hardens values. Both synchronous writers fetch at most `maxWriterWindowRows` rows per packed store read, but still return one in-memory string.

CSV output is UTF-8 with a BOM and CRLF endings. For string values, a leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with a single quote. The value cannot reopen as an executable formula. For example, the string `=1+1` exports as `'=1+1`, while a real formula cell exports its resolved scalar.

For the full setup, the CSV string is `\uFEFFCustomer,Total\r\nAda,120\r\nLin,75` (BOM and line endings shown as escapes).

Clipboard formulas and references retain rich behavior only when copied/cut and pasted through the same live Sheetwrite grid controller. Payloads from another controller or application, including spreadsheet HTML, paste as injection-neutralized text. `pasteValues` uses resolved literals.

## Options and edge cases

Delimited functions accept `DelimitedTextOptions` for bounded resources. See the [API contract](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/delimited-text-options/) and the [hostile-input lab](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/interoperability/#limits). These plain-text formats do not carry workbook styles, formula source, names or multiple worksheets.

Built-in toolbar/context-menu download failures show an alert and emit `export-error` with `{ format: "csv", error }`. See [export error handling](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#errors-and-built-in-actions).
