- [XLSX export](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/)
- [Editing and clipboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/)
- [`fromCsv`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/from-csv/)
- [`toCsv`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/to-csv/)
- [`toTsv`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/to-tsv/)

### Kept parts and round trips

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/

```ts
import { fromXlsxWorkbook, toXlsxWorkbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

declare const bytes: Uint8Array;
const options = {
  onWarning: (warning: import("@sheetwrite/core").XlsxWorkbookWarning) =>
    console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
};
const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbook(bytes, options);
const saved = await toXlsxWorkbook(snapshot, options);
console.log(snapshot.workbook.xlsxSource?.graphs.length ?? 0);
```

The saved workbook retains its modelled cells. Eligible charts, pivots, images and macros travel alongside them as opaque package parts, not as flattened cell values.

| Operation | Result for an eligible imported chart graph |
| --- | --- |
| Open → save, no edits | Original compressed payload retained. |
| Change a cell → save | Graph dropped; structured warning reports loss. |
| Undo that cell edit → save | Dropped graph is not restored. |

[Try it live: workbook round-trip and warnings](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/interoperability/#xlsx).

Full setup

Use the [complete import setup](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-import/) to obtain a snapshot, or read bytes from a host file input. Keep the imported snapshot's `workbook.xlsxSource` when persisting it. The source is JSON-safe; no separate original file is required for eligible parts.

```ts
import { fromXlsxWorkbookFile, toXlsxWorkbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[type="file"]');
const file = input?.files?.[0];
if (!file) throw new Error("Choose an XLSX or XLSM file first");
const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbookFile(file, {
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
});
const saved = await toXlsxWorkbook(snapshot, {
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
});
console.log(saved.byteLength);
```

## Parts Sheetwrite does not model

Import stores eligible parts in `snapshot.workbook.xlsxSource`. Each part keeps its original compressed ZIP payload and is written back byte for byte without recompression. Only opaque parts are kept, never worksheet XML. Verification inflates bounded chunks and discards them; only relationships are parsed.

The payload is base64-encoded for JSON-safe persistence: about four thirds of its compressed size, plus bounded graph metadata.

| Kept part graph | Kept on save when |
| --- | --- |
| VBA project (`.xlsm`), customXml items, XML maps, data connections, theme, core and custom document properties | Always: they do not read cells. Macro workbooks retain the macro content type. |
| Images and other drawings without charts, single-cell XML tables | Their sheet still exists and no row or column on it was inserted, removed, moved, resized, hidden or merged. |
| Charts and pivot tables, with their caches | No cell on any sheet changed, no sheet was renamed or removed, and no defined name changed. |

Shared parts such as a pivot and its cache form one graph: they are kept or dropped together.

## Drops and warnings

Parts reached through a relationship into worksheet, table, styles or workbook parts are dropped because Sheetwrite rewrites those parts. External links, chart sheets, digital signatures and graphs whose relationships point outside the kept parts are also dropped with warnings.

`resourceLimits.maxPreservedBytes` defaults to 64 MiB of compressed data. A graph over this kept-part budget is dropped with a warning rather than making preservation unbounded. This is distinct from hard input/decompression resource failures.

Kept parts retain their names and their own `.rels` bytes. New workbook, sheet and package relationship IDs point at them. Pivot caches are re-listed in `workbook.xml`; each kept part receives its content-type override. Relationship and content-type validity does not mean the graph is editable in Sheetwrite.

## Edits, undo and snapshots

A `SheetwriteStore`, or a `Grid` over one, drops a graph when an invalidating edit commits. It adds no per-cell cost. Undo cannot restore the graph because the original package is not retained.

A directly passed `WorkbookSnapshot` has no edit history. The backend compares each sheet's source values against its import-time 64-bit fingerprint. This reads all cells once, O(cells), and a difference drops the dependent graph.

Import and store hydration verify payload CRCs and sizes by inflating and discarding bounded chunks. Hydration also checks source values against fingerprints before enabling edit-time pruning. Verification is cached per immutable part object in process memory, never serialized. Direct external snapshots are checked on save. Corrupt payloads drop their graphs with warnings.

`xlsxSource` objects are frozen and shared between snapshots from one store. Clone them before changing them.

## See also

- [XLSX import](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-import/)
- [XLSX export](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/)
- [LibreOffice comparison limits](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/libreoffice-compatibility/#what-the-comparison-proves)
- [Resource limits](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/#resource-limits)
- [Preservation and streaming implementation details (PR #179)](https://github.com/chh-ay/sheetwrite/pull/179)

### Large files and streaming

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/

```ts
import { toXlsxWorkbookStream } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

declare const destination: WritableStream<Uint8Array>;
const controller = new AbortController();
await toXlsxWorkbookStream(store.exportSnapshot(), {
  signal: controller.signal,
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
}).pipeTo(destination);
```

| Output | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Destination receives bytes | Bounded `Uint8Array` chunks, not one complete file buffer. |
| Destination slows down | Backpressure slows the producer. |
| Reader cancels | Export stops reading the store. |

The output contains the same XLSX parts as buffered export. ZIP entry order and container bytes can differ.

[Try it live: resource-limit failures](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/interoperability/#limits). The lab demonstrates typed limits, not a whole-file memory guarantee.

Full setup

This browser example reads a selected `File` without calling `arrayBuffer()` on the whole compressed input. Its writable consumer counts bytes instead of collecting them:

```ts
import { fromXlsxWorkbookFile, toXlsxWorkbookStream } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[type="file"]');
const file = input?.files?.[0];
if (!file) throw new Error("Choose an XLSX file first");
const options = {
  onWarning: (warning: import("@sheetwrite/core").XlsxWorkbookWarning) =>
    console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
};
const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbookFile(file, options);
let outputBytes = 0;
await toXlsxWorkbookStream(snapshot, options).pipeTo(new WritableStream<Uint8Array>({
  write(chunk) { outputBytes += chunk.byteLength; },
}));
console.log(outputBytes); // Total depends on the selected workbook.
```

Replace the counting consumer with the host's actual writable destination to save bytes. Collecting chunks into a `Blob` or using `new Response(stream).arrayBuffer()` buffers the output again.

## Streaming functions

| Function | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toCsvStream(sheet, store, options?)` | Visible table view | `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>`. |
| `toTsvStream(range, store, options?)` | Canonical data-space range | `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>`. |
| `toXlsxTableStream(workbook, store, options?)` | Active-sheet table | `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>`. |
| `toXlsxWorkbookStream(snapshot, options?)` | Workbook snapshot | `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>`. |
| `fromXlsxWorkbookFile(file, options?)` | Seekable `File` or `Blob` | `Promise<WorkbookSnapshot>`. |

CSV/TSV remain core-only; XLSX requires backend registration. Existing string and `Uint8Array` APIs remain available.

Both buffered and Blob XLSX import retain the ZIP directory and parse each worksheet incrementally from bounded inflated chunks. Neither builds a whole-worksheet string or XML tree. Snapshot cells are built as rows stream, with one cell representation rather than a second parsed record. The snapshot still holds **every imported cell**: streaming is not a lazy or constant-memory workbook store.

## Resource limits

Every XLSX table/workbook path shares `XlsxWorkbookOptions`:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `maxCells` | Logical accepted cells; default `1_000_000`. |
| `resourceLimits` | Override specific input, archive, XML, dimension, preservation and output budgets. |
| `signal` | Abort between bounded codec stages. |
| `onWarning` | Surface structured fidelity losses. |

Defaults are exported as `DEFAULT_XLSX_RESOURCE_LIMITS`:

| Resource | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Input bytes | 32 MiB |
| Output bytes | 128 MiB |
| Archive entries | 1,024 |
| Per-entry uncompressed bytes | 64 MiB |
| Total uncompressed bytes | 256 MiB |
| Kept unmodelled part bytes | 64 MiB compressed |
| Compression ratio | ×100 |
| Sheets | 256 |
| Rows per sheet | 1,048,576 |
| Columns per sheet | 16,384 |
| Merges | 100,000 |
| Shared strings | 1,000,000 |
| Style records | 65,536 |
| XML elements | 2,000,000 |
| XML depth | 64 |
| XML attributes per element | 128 |
| XML text bytes | 16 MiB |

Hard resource bounds are checked before unsafe decompression or allocation. Exceeding one rejects with `XlsxResourceError`, which names the resource, limit and observed value. The [kept-part budget](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/#drops-and-warnings) instead drops over-budget graphs with warnings. Do not raise limits merely to suppress failures; budget for the resulting snapshot as well as the codec.

## Memory evidence and limits

[PR #186](https://github.com/chh-ay/sheetwrite/pull/186) measured seven interleaved fresh-process rounds per side with one CPU slot:

| Generated workbook | Import path | Peak RSS median before → after | Candidate maximum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 200,000 × 8 | Buffered | 1,095 → 800 MiB | 814 MiB |
| 200,000 × 8 | Blob | 1,112 → 779 MiB | 791 MiB |
| 1,000,000 × 8 | Buffered | 5,061 → 3,352 MiB | 3,512 MiB |
| 1,000,000 × 8 | Blob | 4,475 → 3,336 MiB | 3,504 MiB |

These are measured workloads with adjusted budgets, not default-limit promises. The later results supersede the earlier #179 import peak-risk observation; they do not establish a universal memory ceiling.

### LibreOffice compatibility

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/libreoffice-compatibility/

```ts
import { fromXlsxWorkbook, toXlsxWorkbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

declare const bytes: Uint8Array;
const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbook(bytes, {
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
});
const output = await toXlsxWorkbook(snapshot, {
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
});
```

The recorded LibreOffice 26.8 comparison in [PR #190](https://github.com/chh-ay/sheetwrite/pull/190) reports:

| Chain | Unexpected differences | Known producer difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sheetwrite → LibreOffice → Sheetwrite | 0 | LibreOffice omits conditional-rule `stopIfTrue`. |
| LibreOffice → Sheetwrite → LibreOffice → Sheetwrite | 0 | Known producer differences remain separately recorded. |

A passing semantic comparison does **not** mean byte-identical files or full Excel feature support.

[Try it live: producer compatibility evidence](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/interoperability/#contract).

Full setup

Use the public importer on bytes from a host-selected LibreOffice file. No special LibreOffice backend is required:

```ts
import { fromXlsxWorkbookFile, toXlsxWorkbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[type="file"]');
const file = input?.files?.[0];
if (!file) throw new Error("Choose a LibreOffice-saved XLSX file first");
const options = {
  onWarning: (warning: import("@sheetwrite/core").XlsxWorkbookWarning) =>
    console.warn(warning.code, warning.message),
};
const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbookFile(file, options);
const output = await toXlsxWorkbook(snapshot, options);
console.log(output.byteLength);
```

This converts the selected file. It does not invoke LibreOffice or run the repository's producer comparison.

## Display and layout fidelity

| Field | Import/export behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Vertical alignment | Native absent/bottom imports as bottom, matching Excel. Native center maps to the grid's middle default. Export writes the default as center and an explicit middle override where a bottom column default would otherwise apply. |
| Column width | Uses OOXML's maximum-digit-width conversion rather than adding 2–3 px on each cycle. Sheetwrite pixel widths round-trip exactly; native fixture widths no longer include the old extra 5 px. |
| Row height | `ht` without `customHeight="1"` remains automatic, not fixed. |
| Hyperlink display | An absent `display` uses the cell text. An explicitly empty display remains empty. |
| Hyperlink appearance | Export retains the link's font. Default link color/underline applies only to properties the cell style does not set. Explicit cell styling wins when painting. |

## What the comparison proves

The evidence compares normalized workbook semantics, not ZIP/XML identity. Generated hyperlink IDs may change. Hyperlink presentation moved into cell styles compares equal only when the painted appearance remains equal.

[PR #189](https://github.com/chh-ay/sheetwrite/pull/189) separates `workbook.xlsxSource` opaque bytes from semantic comparison. LibreOffice can rename parts and add its own theme or document-property graphs. Retained graphs are checked separately by **count per kind**: owner, sheet and relationship type. The result must retain at least as many graphs of each kind as the source; additions are allowed.

That detects a lost chart, pivot or drawing count. It cannot detect one graph dropped and replaced by another of the same kind on the same owner. It does not prove opaque payload identity across different producers. A direct Sheetwrite no-edit round trip retains [eligible original compressed payloads](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/).

## Known producer difference

LibreOffice does not write `stopIfTrue`. The comparison records its omission in `knownProducerDifferences`, separate from unexpected `differences`; it does not pretend the conditional-format behavior survived unchanged. If later matching rules matter, inspect the file and warnings after resaving in LibreOffice.

The reported pass is for the pinned fixtures and LibreOffice 26.8 in PR #190. It is not a claim that every workbook, feature or producer version round-trips without loss. The earlier #189 result still had 19 differences; #190 resolves the display/layout differences and records the known stop-rule loss.

- [Workbook export fidelity](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#workbook-interchange)
- [Kept parts and round trips](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/)

### Excel in JavaScript

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-javascript/

```ts
import { fromXlsxTable, type XlsxWorkbookOptions } from "@sheetwrite/core";

declare const options: () => XlsxWorkbookOptions;
declare function workbookFor(data: ColumnarData): Workbook;

async function openFile(file: File): Promise<Grid> {
  const data = await fromXlsxTable(await file.arrayBuffer(), options());
  grid.destroy();
  return createGrid(host, { workbook: workbookFor(data), data });
}
```

| Tea | 12 |
| --- | --- |
| Coffee | 18 |

The source file has headers `Item`, `Amount`, then rows `Tea, 12` and `Coffee, 18`. The headers become column keys, not data cells. Edit a value, then save the current workbook.

[Try it live → Vanilla example](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/vanilla/)

Full setup

Use a browser TypeScript entry in a Vite application. The code creates its own host and file controls; it needs no HTML IDs.

```sh
npm install @sheetwrite/core @sheetwrite/xlsx
```

```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";
import {
  fromXlsxTable, toXlsxWorkbook, downloadBytes, isSheetwriteError,
  type ColumnarData, type Workbook, type Grid, type XlsxWorkbookOptions,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const initialData: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2, columns: { Item: ["Tea", "Coffee"], Amount: [12, 18] },
};
function workbookFor(data: ColumnarData): Workbook {
  return { activeSheet: "sales", sheets: [{
    id: "sales", name: "Sales", rowCount: data.rowCount,
    columns: Object.keys(data.columns).map((key) => ({
      key, header: key, width: 160,
      type: typeof data.columns[key]?.[0] === "number" ? "number" : "text",
    })),
  }] };
}
const message = (error: unknown) => isSheetwriteError(error)
  ? `${error.code}: ${error.message}` : String(error);
const mime = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet";

export async function mountExcel(host: HTMLElement) {
  await initSheetwrite();
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const controls = document.createElement("div");
  const picker = document.createElement("input");
  picker.type = "file"; picker.accept = ".xlsx";
  const save = document.createElement("button");
  save.textContent = "Save XLSX";
  const status = document.createElement("p");
  status.setAttribute("role", "status");
  controls.append(picker, save, status);
  host.before(controls);
  host.style.height = "480px";
  let grid = createGrid(host, { workbook: workbookFor(initialData), data: initialData });
  const options = (): XlsxWorkbookOptions => ({
    signal: controller.signal, maxCells: 100_000,
    resourceLimits: { maxInputBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 },
    onWarning: (warning) => { status.textContent = warning.message; },
  });
  async function run(action: () => Promise<void>) {
    picker.disabled = save.disabled = true; status.textContent = "";
    try { await action(); }
    catch (error) {
      if (!controller.signal.aborted) status.textContent = message(error);
    } finally {
      if (!controller.signal.aborted) picker.disabled = save.disabled = false;
    }
  }
  picker.onchange = () => {
    const file = picker.files?.[0]; picker.value = "";
    if (!file) return;
    void run(async () => {
      if (file.size > 8 * 1024 * 1024) throw new Error("File exceeds 8 MiB");
      const data = await fromXlsxTable(await file.arrayBuffer(), options());
      if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
      grid.destroy();
      grid = createGrid(host, { workbook: workbookFor(data), data });
    });
  };
  save.onclick = () => void run(async () => {
    const bytes = await toXlsxWorkbook(grid, options());
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) downloadBytes(bytes, "sales.xlsx", mime);
  });
  return () => {
    controller.abort(); picker.onchange = null; save.onclick = null;
    grid.destroy(); controls.remove();
  };
}

const host = document.createElement("div");
document.body.append(host);
try {
  const dispose = await mountExcel(host);
  window.addEventListener("pagehide", dispose, { once: true });
} catch (error) { host.textContent = message(error); }
```

## Ownership and errors

Await `initSheetwrite()` before creating a Grid. Keep the returned disposer in a single-page application and call it when the view leaves; `pagehide` covers this standalone example. The disposer aborts conversion, removes controls and destroys the Grid. A file parse failure keeps the current Grid. A successful import replaces it, so prior undo history does not carry over.

Initialization errors appear in the host. Codec errors appear beside the controls. No file is substituted when import fails.

## Options and limits

| Choice | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Import | `fromXlsxTable` reads only the first sheet. Its first row supplies headers. Formula source and workbook formatting are not preserved by table import. |
| Save | `toXlsxWorkbook` saves the current Grid as a workbook, not only its visible viewport. |
| Budget | This example accepts 100,000 cells and at most 8 MiB of input. Codec defaults still bound ZIP entries, expanded bytes, XML depth and other resources. |
| Cancel | Unmount aborts work between bounded codec stages. Cancellation is not an immediate interrupt inside a stage. |

Import builds the full result in memory. The Blob workbook importer avoids an initial full-file buffer, but still returns an in-memory snapshot; it is not an unbounded-data reader. Use [workbook interchange](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#workbook-interchange) instead of table import when you must retain sheets, formulas, styles and kept parts. Surface its `onWarning` messages when fidelity matters. Resource failures are `XlsxResourceError` values and also satisfy `isSheetwriteError`.

See [Vanilla lifecycle](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/vanilla/) and [XLSX API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/xlsx/).

### Excel in React

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-react/

```tsx
import type { RefObject } from "react";

function ExcelGrid({ input, grid }: {
  input: { workbook: Workbook; data: ColumnarData };
  grid: RefObject<Grid | null>;
}) {
  return <SheetwriteGrid {...input} height={420}
    onReady={({ grid: ready }) => { grid.current = ready; }} />;
}
```

| Tea | 12 |
| --- | --- |
| Coffee | 18 |

The source file has headers `Item`, `Amount`, then rows `Tea, 12` and `Coffee, 18`. The headers become column keys, not data cells. Edit a value, then save the current workbook.

[Try it live → React example](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/react/)

Full setup

Install in an existing React application:

```sh
npm install @sheetwrite/react @sheetwrite/core @sheetwrite/xlsx
```

Save this as `ExcelTable.tsx` and render it from your application.

```tsx
"use client";
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { SheetwriteGrid } from "@sheetwrite/react";
import "@sheetwrite/react/styles.css";
import {
  fromXlsxTable, toXlsxWorkbook, downloadBytes, isSheetwriteError,
  type ColumnarData, type Workbook, type Grid, type XlsxWorkbookOptions,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const initialData: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2, columns: { Item: ["Tea", "Coffee"], Amount: [12, 18] },
};
function workbookFor(data: ColumnarData): Workbook {
  return { activeSheet: "sales", sheets: [{
    id: "sales", name: "Sales", rowCount: data.rowCount,
    columns: Object.keys(data.columns).map((key) => ({
      key, header: key, width: 160,
      type: typeof data.columns[key]?.[0] === "number" ? "number" : "text",
    })),
  }] };
}
const message = (error: unknown) => isSheetwriteError(error)
  ? `${error.code}: ${error.message}` : String(error);
const mime = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet";

export default function ExcelTable() {
  const [input, setInput] = useState(() => ({
    workbook: workbookFor(initialData), data: initialData,
  }));
  const grid = useRef<Grid | null>(null);
  const controller = useRef<AbortController | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");
  useEffect(() => {
    controller.current = new AbortController();
    return () => { controller.current?.abort(); grid.current = null; };
  }, []);
  const options = (): XlsxWorkbookOptions => ({
    signal: controller.current?.signal, maxCells: 100_000,
    resourceLimits: { maxInputBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 },
    onWarning: (warning) => setError(warning.message),
  });
  async function open(file: File) {
    setBusy(true); setError("");
    try {
      if (file.size > 8 * 1024 * 1024) throw new Error("File exceeds 8 MiB");
      const data = await fromXlsxTable(await file.arrayBuffer(), options());
      if (controller.current?.signal.aborted) return;
      grid.current = null;
      setInput({ workbook: workbookFor(data), data });
    } catch (error) {
      if (!controller.current?.signal.aborted) setError(message(error));
    } finally {
      if (!controller.current?.signal.aborted) setBusy(false);
    }
  }
  async function save() {
    const current = grid.current;
    if (!current) return;
    setBusy(true); setError("");
    try {
      const bytes = await toXlsxWorkbook(current, options());
      if (!controller.current?.signal.aborted) downloadBytes(bytes, "sales.xlsx", mime);
    } catch (error) {
      if (!controller.current?.signal.aborted) setError(message(error));
    } finally {
      if (!controller.current?.signal.aborted) setBusy(false);
    }
  }
  return <>
    <input type="file" accept=".xlsx" disabled={busy} onChange={(event) => {
      const file = event.currentTarget.files?.[0];
      if (file) void open(file);
      event.currentTarget.value = "";
    }} />
    <button disabled={busy} onClick={() => void save()}>Save XLSX</button>
    <p role="status">{error}</p>
    <SheetwriteGrid {...input} height={420}
      onReady={({ grid: ready }) => { grid.current = ready; }}
      onInitializationError={(event) => setError(message(event))} />
  </>;
}
```

## Readiness and cleanup

The adapter initializes WASM after client mount and destroys its Grid on unmount. Use the handle published by `onReady`, not a handle captured before initialization. Import replaces the workbook and data together. This creates a new Grid generation; ready publishes its replacement. Do not call `grid.destroy()` on an adapter-owned Grid.

React clears the host-held handle in effect cleanup. Vue and Svelte adapters also clear their exposed or bound handle on reset. Dispose any host subscriptions or persistence coordinators before attaching them to the replacement. This example attaches none. File controls are disabled during conversion, and unmount aborts the outstanding codec operation.

Use a client component in Next.js. Import the adapter stylesheet once. Keep `workbook` and `data` identities stable between imports so unrelated renders do not reset edits.

## Options and limits

| Choice | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Import | `fromXlsxTable` reads only the first sheet. Its first row supplies headers. Formula source and workbook formatting are not preserved by table import. |
| Save | `toXlsxWorkbook` saves the current Grid as a workbook, not only its visible viewport. |
| Budget | This example accepts 100,000 cells and at most 8 MiB of input. Codec defaults still bound ZIP entries, expanded bytes, XML depth and other resources. |
| Cancel | Unmount aborts work between bounded codec stages. Cancellation is not an immediate interrupt inside a stage. |

Import builds the full result in memory. The Blob workbook importer avoids an initial full-file buffer, but still returns an in-memory snapshot; it is not an unbounded-data reader. Use [workbook interchange](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#workbook-interchange) instead of table import when you must retain sheets, formulas, styles and kept parts. Surface its `onWarning` messages when fidelity matters. Resource failures are `XlsxResourceError` values and also satisfy `isSheetwriteError`.

See [adapter lifecycle](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/lifecycle/) and the [React adapter](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/react/).

### Excel in Vue

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-vue/

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { shallowRef } from "vue";

defineProps<{ input: { workbook: Workbook; data: ColumnarData } }>();
const activeGrid = shallowRef<Grid>();
function ready(event: GridReadyEvent) { activeGrid.value = event.grid; }
</script>

<template>
  <SheetwriteGrid :workbook="input.workbook" :data="input.data"
    :height="420" @ready="ready" />
</template>
```

| Tea | 12 |
| --- | --- |
| Coffee | 18 |

The source file has headers `Item`, `Amount`, then rows `Tea, 12` and `Coffee, 18`. The headers become column keys, not data cells. Edit a value, then save the current workbook.

[Try it live → Vue example](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/vue/)

Full setup

Install in an existing Vue application:

```sh
npm install @sheetwrite/vue @sheetwrite/core @sheetwrite/xlsx
```

Save this as `ExcelTable.vue` and render it from your application.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { shallowRef, ref, onBeforeUnmount } from "vue";
import { SheetwriteGrid, type GridReadyEvent } from "@sheetwrite/vue";
import "@sheetwrite/vue/styles.css";
import {
  fromXlsxTable, toXlsxWorkbook, downloadBytes, isSheetwriteError,
  type ColumnarData, type Workbook, type Grid, type SheetwriteError, type XlsxWorkbookOptions,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const initialData: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2, columns: { Item: ["Tea", "Coffee"], Amount: [12, 18] },
};
function workbookFor(data: ColumnarData): Workbook {
  return { activeSheet: "sales", sheets: [{
    id: "sales", name: "Sales", rowCount: data.rowCount,
    columns: Object.keys(data.columns).map((key) => ({
      key, header: key, width: 160,
      type: typeof data.columns[key]?.[0] === "number" ? "number" : "text",
    })),
  }] };
}
const message = (error: unknown) => isSheetwriteError(error)
  ? `${error.code}: ${error.message}` : String(error);
const mime = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet";

const input = shallowRef({ workbook: workbookFor(initialData), data: initialData });
const activeGrid = shallowRef<Grid>();
const busy = ref(false);
const error = ref("");
const controller = new AbortController();
onBeforeUnmount(() => { controller.abort(); activeGrid.value = undefined; });
function ready(event: GridReadyEvent) { activeGrid.value = event.grid; }
function initializationFailed(failure: SheetwriteError) { error.value = message(failure); }
const options = (): XlsxWorkbookOptions => ({
  signal: controller.signal, maxCells: 100_000,
  resourceLimits: { maxInputBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 },
  onWarning: (warning) => { error.value = warning.message; },
});
async function open(file: File) {
  busy.value = true; error.value = "";
  try {
    if (file.size > 8 * 1024 * 1024) throw new Error("File exceeds 8 MiB");
    const data = await fromXlsxTable(await file.arrayBuffer(), options());
    if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
    activeGrid.value = undefined;
    input.value = { workbook: workbookFor(data), data };
  } catch (failure) {
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) error.value = message(failure);
  } finally { if (!controller.signal.aborted) busy.value = false; }
}
async function save() {
  const current = activeGrid.value;
  if (!current) return;
  busy.value = true; error.value = "";
  try {
    const bytes = await toXlsxWorkbook(current, options());
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) downloadBytes(bytes, "sales.xlsx", mime);
  } catch (failure) {
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) error.value = message(failure);
  } finally { if (!controller.signal.aborted) busy.value = false; }
}
function choose(event: Event) {
  const target = event.currentTarget as HTMLInputElement;
  const file = target.files?.[0];
  if (file) void open(file);
  target.value = "";
}
</script>

<template>
  <input type="file" accept=".xlsx" :disabled="busy" @change="choose" />
  <button :disabled="busy" @click="save">Save XLSX</button>
  <p role="status">{{ error }}</p>
  <SheetwriteGrid :workbook="input.workbook" :data="input.data" :height="420"
    @ready="ready" @initialization-error="initializationFailed" />
</template>
```

## Readiness and cleanup

The adapter initializes WASM after client mount and destroys its Grid on unmount. Use the handle published by `@ready`, not a handle captured before initialization. Import replaces the workbook and data together. This creates a new Grid generation; ready publishes its replacement. Do not call `grid.destroy()` on an adapter-owned Grid.

The adapter clears its exposed or bound handle before reset. The ready callback receives the new generation. Dispose any host subscriptions or persistence coordinators before attaching them to the replacement. This example attaches none. File controls are disabled during conversion, and unmount aborts the outstanding codec operation.

Use a client-only boundary in Nuxt. Import the adapter stylesheet once. Keep `workbook` and `data` identities stable between imports so unrelated renders do not reset edits.

## Options and limits

| Choice | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Import | `fromXlsxTable` reads only the first sheet. Its first row supplies headers. Formula source and workbook formatting are not preserved by table import. |
| Save | `toXlsxWorkbook` saves the current Grid as a workbook, not only its visible viewport. |
| Budget | This example accepts 100,000 cells and at most 8 MiB of input. Codec defaults still bound ZIP entries, expanded bytes, XML depth and other resources. |
| Cancel | Unmount aborts work between bounded codec stages. Cancellation is not an immediate interrupt inside a stage. |

Import builds the full result in memory. The Blob workbook importer avoids an initial full-file buffer, but still returns an in-memory snapshot; it is not an unbounded-data reader. Use [workbook interchange](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#workbook-interchange) instead of table import when you must retain sheets, formulas, styles and kept parts. Surface its `onWarning` messages when fidelity matters. Resource failures are `XlsxResourceError` values and also satisfy `isSheetwriteError`.

See [adapter lifecycle](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/lifecycle/) and the [Vue adapter](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/vue/).

### Excel in Svelte

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-svelte/

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
let { input }: { input: { workbook: Workbook; data: ColumnarData } } = $props();
let activeGrid = $state<Grid | undefined>();
function ready(event: GridReadyEvent) { activeGrid = event.grid; }
</script>

<SheetwriteGrid workbook={input.workbook} data={input.data}
  height={420} bind:grid={activeGrid} onReady={ready} />
```

| Tea | 12 |
| --- | --- |
| Coffee | 18 |

The source file has headers `Item`, `Amount`, then rows `Tea, 12` and `Coffee, 18`. The headers become column keys, not data cells. Edit a value, then save the current workbook.

[Try it live → Svelte example](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/svelte/)

Full setup

Install in an existing Svelte 5 application:

```sh
npm install @sheetwrite/svelte @sheetwrite/core @sheetwrite/xlsx
```

Save this as `ExcelTable.svelte` and render it from your application.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
import { onMount } from "svelte";
import { SheetwriteGrid, type GridReadyEvent } from "@sheetwrite/svelte";
import "@sheetwrite/svelte/styles.css";
import {
  fromXlsxTable, toXlsxWorkbook, downloadBytes, isSheetwriteError,
  type ColumnarData, type Workbook, type Grid, type XlsxWorkbookOptions,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const initialData: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2, columns: { Item: ["Tea", "Coffee"], Amount: [12, 18] },
};
function workbookFor(data: ColumnarData): Workbook {
  return { activeSheet: "sales", sheets: [{
    id: "sales", name: "Sales", rowCount: data.rowCount,
    columns: Object.keys(data.columns).map((key) => ({
      key, header: key, width: 160,
      type: typeof data.columns[key]?.[0] === "number" ? "number" : "text",
    })),
  }] };
}
const message = (error: unknown) => isSheetwriteError(error)
  ? `${error.code}: ${error.message}` : String(error);
const mime = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet";

let input = $state({ workbook: workbookFor(initialData), data: initialData });
let activeGrid = $state<Grid | undefined>();
let busy = $state(false);
let error = $state("");
const controller = new AbortController();
onMount(() => () => { controller.abort(); activeGrid = undefined; });
function ready(event: GridReadyEvent) { activeGrid = event.grid; }
const options = (): XlsxWorkbookOptions => ({
  signal: controller.signal, maxCells: 100_000,
  resourceLimits: { maxInputBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 },
  onWarning: (warning) => { error = warning.message; },
});
async function open(file: File) {
  busy = true; error = "";
  try {
    if (file.size > 8 * 1024 * 1024) throw new Error("File exceeds 8 MiB");
    const data = await fromXlsxTable(await file.arrayBuffer(), options());
    if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
    activeGrid = undefined;
    input = { workbook: workbookFor(data), data };
  } catch (failure) {
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) error = message(failure);
  } finally { if (!controller.signal.aborted) busy = false; }
}
async function save() {
  const current = activeGrid;
  if (!current) return;
  busy = true; error = "";
  try {
    const bytes = await toXlsxWorkbook(current, options());
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) downloadBytes(bytes, "sales.xlsx", mime);
  } catch (failure) {
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) error = message(failure);
  } finally { if (!controller.signal.aborted) busy = false; }
}
function choose(event: Event) {
  const target = event.currentTarget as HTMLInputElement;
  const file = target.files?.[0];
  if (file) void open(file);
  target.value = "";
}
</script>

<input type="file" accept=".xlsx" disabled={busy} onchange={choose} />
<button disabled={busy} onclick={() => void save()}>Save XLSX</button>
<p role="status">{error}</p>
<SheetwriteGrid workbook={input.workbook} data={input.data} height={420}
  bind:grid={activeGrid} onReady={ready} onInitializationError={(failure) => { error = message(failure); }} />
```

## Readiness and cleanup

The adapter initializes WASM after client mount and destroys its Grid on unmount. Use the handle published by `onReady`, not a handle captured before initialization. Import replaces the workbook and data together. This creates a new Grid generation; ready publishes its replacement. Do not call `grid.destroy()` on an adapter-owned Grid.

The adapter clears its exposed or bound handle before reset. The ready callback receives the new generation. Dispose any host subscriptions or persistence coordinators before attaching them to the replacement. This example attaches none. File controls are disabled during conversion, and unmount aborts the outstanding codec operation.

For SvelteKit, use a client-only route or create this component after client mount. Import the adapter stylesheet once. Keep `workbook` and `data` identities stable between imports so unrelated renders do not reset edits.

## Options and limits

| Choice | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Import | `fromXlsxTable` reads only the first sheet. Its first row supplies headers. Formula source and workbook formatting are not preserved by table import. |
| Save | `toXlsxWorkbook` saves the current Grid as a workbook, not only its visible viewport. |
| Budget | This example accepts 100,000 cells and at most 8 MiB of input. Codec defaults still bound ZIP entries, expanded bytes, XML depth and other resources. |
| Cancel | Unmount aborts work between bounded codec stages. Cancellation is not an immediate interrupt inside a stage. |

Import builds the full result in memory. The Blob workbook importer avoids an initial full-file buffer, but still returns an in-memory snapshot; it is not an unbounded-data reader. Use [workbook interchange](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#workbook-interchange) instead of table import when you must retain sheets, formulas, styles and kept parts. Surface its `onWarning` messages when fidelity matters. Resource failures are `XlsxResourceError` values and also satisfy `isSheetwriteError`.

See [adapter lifecycle](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/lifecycle/) and the [Svelte adapter](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/svelte/).

### Excel in Node.js

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-nodejs/

```ts
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { fromXlsxWorkbook, toXlsxWorkbook, type XlsxWorkbookOptions } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

declare const source: string;
declare const destination: string;
declare const options: XlsxWorkbookOptions;

const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbook(await readFile(source), options);
await writeFile(destination, await toXlsxWorkbook(snapshot, options), { flag: "wx" });
```

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Tea | 12 |
| Coffee | 18 |

For this input the command prints `Saved 1 sheet(s) to output.xlsx`. This is a workbook conversion, not an image or a browser download.

[Try it live → Browser spreadsheet showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/spreadsheet/)

The live showcase is a browser counterpart. Run the command below for the Node file-system path.

Full setup

In a Node.js TypeScript project, install the codec and a TypeScript runner:

```sh
npm install @sheetwrite/core @sheetwrite/xlsx
npm install --save-dev tsx @types/node
```

Save as `roundtrip.mts`. The `.mts` extension selects ESM so the entry can use top-level `await`.

```ts
import { readFile, writeFile, stat } from "node:fs/promises";
import {
  fromXlsxWorkbook, toXlsxWorkbook, isSheetwriteError,
  type XlsxWorkbookOptions,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const [source, destination] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!source || !destination) throw new Error("Usage: roundtrip.mts input.xlsx output.xlsx");
if (source === destination) throw new Error("Choose a separate output path");
const controller = new AbortController();
const cancel = () => controller.abort();
process.once("SIGINT", cancel);
const options: XlsxWorkbookOptions = {
  signal: controller.signal,
  maxCells: 100_000,
  resourceLimits: { maxInputBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 },
  onWarning: (warning) => console.warn(`${warning.code}: ${warning.message}`),
};
try {
  if ((await stat(source)).size > 8 * 1024 * 1024) throw new Error("Input exceeds 8 MiB");
  const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbook(await readFile(source), options);
  const output = await toXlsxWorkbook(snapshot, options);
  if (controller.signal.aborted) throw new Error("Cancelled");
  await writeFile(destination, output, { flag: "wx" });
  console.log(`Saved ${snapshot.sheets.length} sheet(s) to ${destination}`);
} catch (error) {
  console.error(isSheetwriteError(error) ? `${error.code}: ${error.message}` : error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
} finally {
  process.removeListener("SIGINT", cancel);
}
```

Supply an existing XLSX file and a new output path:

```sh
npx tsx roundtrip.mts input.xlsx output.xlsx
```

## Server ownership and errors

These workbook codec functions operate on a `WorkbookSnapshot`. They do not create a Grid, initialize a formula engine, evaluate formulas, access the DOM or call `downloadBytes`. Formula source is preserved where supported, not recalculated by this script. Node's `Buffer` is a `Uint8Array`, so `readFile` bytes can go directly to `fromXlsxWorkbook`.

The script never substitutes a mock workbook. Missing or invalid files fail. `flag: "wx"` refuses to overwrite an existing output; use a separate output path. File helpers close their own file handles. The `finally` block removes the process listener, and SIGINT requests codec cancellation between bounded stages. It does not interrupt `writeFile` once that write has started.

## Options and resource limits

| Option | Effect in this command |
| --- | --- |
| `maxCells: 100_000` | Rejects inputs or outputs beyond this accepted-cell budget. |
| `maxInputBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024` | Bounds codec input bytes; the pre-read size check avoids reading an already oversized file. |
| `onWarning` | Prints structured fidelity losses instead of hiding them. |
| `signal` | Requests cancellation before or between codec stages. |

The stat check is not a security boundary for a file another process can modify. The codec also checks the bytes it actually receives. ZIP expansion, entry count, compression ratio and XML depth retain their default limits. `XlsxResourceError` also satisfies `isSheetwriteError`; report its stable code and resource details rather than parsing a message.

Buffered import holds input bytes and the resulting snapshot; buffered export also holds output bytes. Streaming workbook export can bound output chunks, but it does not make the snapshot disappear. Do not promise constant-memory processing for large workbooks. See [streaming](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/#streaming-functions) and [kept-part rules](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/#parts-sheetwrite-does-not-model) before using this as a fidelity-sensitive round trip. An unchanged chart or pivot graph can be kept; that is not a chart-authoring or pivot-calculation API.

### Spreadsheet app with a ribbon

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/spreadsheet-app-with-ribbon/

```ts
import { createSpreadsheetShell } from "@sheetwrite/core/shell";

const shell = createSpreadsheetShell(host, {
  ribbon: true,
  grid: { workbook, data },
});
```

| Tea | 12 |
| --- | --- |
| Coffee | 18 |

Select B1 and use Home to change its number format. The value stays `12`; the selected format changes its display. Save XLSX writes the current workbook, including supported styles and formula source.

[Try it live → Spreadsheet showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/spreadsheet/)

Full setup

Use a browser TypeScript entry in a Vite application:

```sh
npm install @sheetwrite/core @sheetwrite/xlsx
```

```ts
import { initSheetwrite } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import { createSpreadsheetShell } from "@sheetwrite/core/shell";
import "@sheetwrite/core/styles.css";
import {
  fromXlsxTable, toXlsxWorkbook, downloadBytes, isSheetwriteError,
  type ColumnarData, type Workbook, type Grid, type XlsxWorkbookOptions,
} from "@sheetwrite/core";
import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register";

const initialData: ColumnarData = {
  rowCount: 2, columns: { Item: ["Tea", "Coffee"], Amount: [12, 18] },
};
function workbookFor(data: ColumnarData): Workbook {
  return { activeSheet: "sales", sheets: [{
    id: "sales", name: "Sales", rowCount: data.rowCount,
    columns: Object.keys(data.columns).map((key) => ({
      key, header: key, width: 160,
      type: typeof data.columns[key]?.[0] === "number" ? "number" : "text",
    })),
  }] };
}
const message = (error: unknown) => isSheetwriteError(error)
  ? `${error.code}: ${error.message}` : String(error);
const mime = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet";

export async function mountExcel(host: HTMLElement) {
  await initSheetwrite();
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const controls = document.createElement("div");
  const picker = document.createElement("input");
  picker.type = "file"; picker.accept = ".xlsx";
  const save = document.createElement("button");
  save.textContent = "Save XLSX";
  const status = document.createElement("p");
  status.setAttribute("role", "status");
  controls.append(picker, save, status);
  host.before(controls);
  host.style.height = "480px";
  let shell = createSpreadsheetShell(host, {
    ribbon: true,
    grid: { workbook: workbookFor(initialData), data: initialData },
  });
  const options = (): XlsxWorkbookOptions => ({
    signal: controller.signal, maxCells: 100_000,
    resourceLimits: { maxInputBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 },
    onWarning: (warning) => { status.textContent = warning.message; },
  });
  async function run(action: () => Promise<void>) {
    picker.disabled = save.disabled = true; status.textContent = "";
    try { await action(); }
    catch (error) {
      if (!controller.signal.aborted) status.textContent = message(error);
    } finally {
      if (!controller.signal.aborted) picker.disabled = save.disabled = false;
    }
  }
  picker.onchange = () => {
    const file = picker.files?.[0]; picker.value = "";
    if (!file) return;
    void run(async () => {
      if (file.size > 8 * 1024 * 1024) throw new Error("File exceeds 8 MiB");
      const data = await fromXlsxTable(await file.arrayBuffer(), options());
      if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
      shell.destroy();
      shell = createSpreadsheetShell(host, {
        ribbon: true, grid: { workbook: workbookFor(data), data },
      });
    });
  };
  save.onclick = () => void run(async () => {
    const bytes = await toXlsxWorkbook(shell.grid, options());
    if (!controller.signal.aborted) downloadBytes(bytes, "sales.xlsx", mime);
  });
  return () => {
    controller.abort(); picker.onchange = null; save.onclick = null;
    shell.destroy(); controls.remove();
  };
}

const host = document.createElement("div");
document.body.append(host);
try {
  const dispose = await mountExcel(host);
  window.addEventListener("pagehide", dispose, { once: true });
} catch (error) { host.textContent = message(error); }
```

## Shell ownership

The shell owns one Grid and its ribbon, name box, formula bar, sheet tabs and selection status. Keep the host at a real size. Call `shell.destroy()` when the view leaves; it destroys its Grid and chrome and is safe to call twice. Do not also mount the Grid's built-in ribbon with `grid.config.ribbon`.

The file buttons are host-owned. A successful table import destroys the old shell and starts a new one. This also resets undo history and sheet selection. Parse failure leaves the old shell intact. On teardown, abort work before destroying the shell so a late conversion cannot recreate it.

## Ribbon behavior

| Choice | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `ribbon: true` | Shows Home, Insert, Data and View instead of the flat toolbar. |
| Narrow host | Labels shrink and groups fold into popup controls. |
| Double-click a tab | Minimizes the ribbon to its tab row. |
| Read-only Grid | Editing commands disable; view commands remain available. |
| Host commands | Read `shell.grid.getCommandState(...)` and subscribe to `command-state-change`; do not derive availability from CSS. |

The ribbon loads as a separate chunk. The shell reserves its height while loading and ignores a late chunk after destruction. A failed load falls back to the flat toolbar and still reports an unhandled promise rejection; the file-handler `try/catch` does not catch that asynchronous load failure. Keep chunk URLs available after deployment.

The built-in ribbon does not provide a chart-authoring API. Do not treat retained XLSX chart parts as editable charts.

## Options and limits

| Choice | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Import | `fromXlsxTable` reads only the first sheet. Its first row supplies headers. Formula source and workbook formatting are not preserved by table import. |
| Save | `toXlsxWorkbook` saves the current Grid as a workbook, not only its visible viewport. |
| Budget | This example accepts 100,000 cells and at most 8 MiB of input. Codec defaults still bound ZIP entries, expanded bytes, XML depth and other resources. |
| Cancel | Unmount aborts work between bounded codec stages. Cancellation is not an immediate interrupt inside a stage. |

Import builds the full result in memory. The Blob workbook importer avoids an initial full-file buffer, but still returns an in-memory snapshot; it is not an unbounded-data reader. Use [workbook interchange](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/#workbook-interchange) instead of table import when you must retain sheets, formulas, styles and kept parts. Surface its `onWarning` messages when fidelity matters. Resource failures are `XlsxResourceError` values and also satisfy `isSheetwriteError`.

See [toolbar and ribbon](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/toolbar-and-ribbon/) and [shell API](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core-shell/).

### Public API contract

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/api-contract/

Sheetwrite treats each package `exports` map as the public boundary. The release gate builds the packages first, analyzes the emitted declarations with TypeScript, and rejects undocumented, ambiguous, or accidentally exposed symbols before any package can publish.

## Entry-point classifications

Every exported subpath has one explicit classification:

| Classification | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `supported` | Public application API. Semver and the generated reference apply. |
| `internal` | Required runtime plumbing, such as the WASM loader. Published intentionally but not a general extension surface. |
| `testing-only` | Deterministic harnesses for consumers' tests; never production code. |
| `asset` | CSS, Worker, or WASM bytes rather than a TypeScript symbol surface. |

The [generated API index](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/) lists every package entry point, its classification, and every compiler-visible export. There is no manually maintained symbol inventory beside it.

## What the gate records

For every TypeScript export, the canonical manifest records:

- symbol name and declaration kind;
- normalized primary signature;
- owning declaration files and source location;
- source JSDoc and JSDoc tags;
- documented interface and class members.

Named re-exports preserve documentation from both the export statement and the declaration target. Framework-generated declarations are analyzed from the bytes that packages actually ship.

## Stability and changes

`bun run api:check` hashes the normalized manifest. A changed digest must be reviewed with the declaration diff and accepted explicitly; rebuilding alone cannot rewrite the baseline. This catches additions, removals, signature drift, duplicate declaration merges, missing documentation, and dependency types that leak into the public surface.

The API manifest describes type compatibility. Runtime behavior remains protected by package tests, adapter lifecycle contracts, browser scenarios, canonical tarball checks, and delivery-size budgets.

## Deprecations and removals

`supported` entry points get a deprecation period, marked with `@deprecated`, before removal. `internal` entry points, such as the WASM engine, may change in a minor release with a changelog entry.

| Package | Removed or deprecated | Replacement | Release |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@sheetwrite/wasm` | Removed `CellStore.setBlock` | `CellStore.setBlockPacked` | Next minor release |
| `@sheetwrite/wasm`, `@sheetwrite/formulas` | Removed `CellStore.sortRows`, `styleIdAt`, `hydratePageNumbers`, `hydratePageStringsPacked`, `pinRange` | `sortRowsMulti` with one key; `getCell(...).style`; `setSparseBlock` inside `beginPageLoad`/`commitSources`; no replacement for `pinRange` | 0.6.0 |
| `@sheetwrite/wasm`, `@sheetwrite/formulas` | Removed `CellStore.canDirtyCell`, `dirtyRevision`, `markCellCleanRevision`, `spillOwnerCoordinates`, `isSheetAlive` | None (no caller) | 0.6.0 |
| `@sheetwrite/wasm`, `@sheetwrite/formulas` | Removed `SourceSnapshot.byteLength` | None (no caller); `RangeSnapshot.byteLength` is unchanged | 0.6.0 |

### Document operations

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/document-operations/

`DocumentOp` is the exhaustive serializable mutation union used by Store/Grid transactions, persistence, sync, undo/redo, and document rebase. Operations address stable sheet IDs and explicit row/column coordinates; structural operations also rebase formula references and related metadata.

## Local transactions

`grid.applyTransaction({ patches })` participates in read-only/protection policy, undo/redo, and committed `change` events. Its `ApplyTransactionResult` is `applied`, `rejected`, `conflict`, or `noop`, with warnings/rejections where applicable. `store.applyTransaction` is the lower-level epoch boundary and intentionally bypasses Grid policy/history.

## Remote input

Apply sequenced host input through the remote operation path so events carry `source: "remote"` and are not re-enqueued as local output. Versions must be contiguous: gaps require reload or an explicit `SyncVersionGapRequest` recovery flow.

### Large restores

Undo can emit `restoreBlock` when the ordinary `setBlock` payload exceeds the transaction byte limit. This operation has `range`, `encoding: "deflate-json-v1"`, `decodedBytes`, and `data` fields. `data` is canonical base64 of a raw DEFLATE stream. Its decoded bytes contain UTF-8 JSON for a `PackedCellBlock`, not another operation or transaction.

Persist and replay the operation unchanged. Servers and peers must validate the encoding and decoded block before applying it. The encoded operation still uses the normal transaction and version payload limits. A block can expand to at most 64 MiB of JSON and 4,000,000 cells. Invalid streams or blocks are rejected before mutation. Snapshot schema version 1 remains unchanged because snapshots store the resulting cells, not restore streams.

The operation has the same range, formula, reference, style, protection, and conservative rebase behavior as `setBlock`. The Grid emits one change event and sync submits one version. Hosts that dispatch over the exhaustive `DocumentOp` union must add `restoreBlock` support before accepting new clients.

### Atomic multi-version batches

If a restore still cannot fit one version, the Grid splits packed blocks into smaller ranges. It applies those operations as one transaction and emits one `change` event. Ordinary host `applyTransaction` limits and result fields do not change.

The persistence adapter must implement `commitBatch`. Its request carries the usual commit fields plus `versionOperationCounts`. Each count selects the next consecutive operations for one version. Counts must be positive, cover all operations, and describe at least two versions. Every version must pass the normal operation and byte limits. A batch has at most 16 versions and 64 MiB of encoded operations.

The server must validate all versions and apply all operations in one database transaction. It must publish all versions or none. Versions run from `baseVersion + 1` to `baseVersion + versionOperationCounts.length`. Each published version carries `batch: { index, count }` with a zero-based index and the same mutation ID. The response acknowledges the last version. Retry uses the same mutation ID for the whole batch.

Peers hold batch members until all consecutive versions arrive. They validate and apply the combined operations once. A rejected member leaves the peer document and server-version cursor unchanged. Missing versions use the normal gap recovery path. Pending IndexedDB records retain `versionOperationCounts` across reload. Rebase preserves batch boundaries and rejects ambiguous range, formula, or reference changes with a typed conflict. Adapters without `commitBatch` reject an oversized local step before mutation.

Malformed pending batch counts raise `IndexedDbPendingCommitStorageError` with code `transaction`. The memory adapter reports rejected document application with `PersistenceError` code `commit-rejected`. Invalid remote batch metadata uses `SyncProtocolError` code `invalid-batch`; a batch ceiling uses `batch-limit`. A complete batch rejected by the Grid uses `remote-operations-rejected`.

XLSX export reads the restored document cells. It does not store restore streams or batch metadata.

## Snapshots and rebase

Validate untrusted JSON with the snapshot validator before hydration. `SnapshotValidationError` identifies the failing path. `rebaseDocumentOperations` accepts only cases it can establish as non-overlapping; conflicts preserve the original pending queue for host resolution.

- [`DocumentOp`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/document-op/)
- [`Grid.applyTransaction`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/grid/#applytransaction)
- [`ApplyTransactionResult`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/apply-transaction-result/)
- [`WorkbookSnapshot`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/workbook-snapshot/)
- [Persistence and recovery](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/persistence/)

### Events

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/events/

`grid.on(evt, fn)` subscribes to a grid event and returns an `off()` function. Call it to unsubscribe.

```ts
const off = grid.on("change", ({ transaction, source, commitReason }) => {
  if (source === "local") console.log(commitReason, transaction.patches.length);
});
// later
off();
```

After a user types a value and presses Enter, the log shows `edit-enter 1`.

## Event direction

`change` is the committed transaction stream. `ChangeEvent.source` is `local` for user or API output that a host may persist, and `remote` for already-persisted input that must not be enqueued again. Selection, search, renderer fallback, and other UI events remain observational.

Framework `onGridChange` / `grid-change` callbacks carry the same committed event. Adapter readiness is `{ grid, generation, reason }`; `reason` distinguishes `initial`, `input-reset`, and `renderer-reset`. The imperative ref, exposed handle, or binding is assigned before readiness and cleared on replacement.

## Grid events

| Event | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | `ChangeEvent`: `{ transaction; changes; commitReason; source: "local" \| "remote"; epoch? }` |
| `selection` | `{ selection: Selection \| null }` |
| `scroll` | `{ scrollTop; firstRow; lastRow; scrollLeft; firstVisibleColumn; lastVisibleColumn }`; the visible-column fields are `number \| null`. |
| `edit-begin` | `{ addr: CellAddress }` |
| `edit-commit` | `{ addr: CellAddress; value: CellValue }` |
| `search` | `SearchResult`: `{ query: string; matches: CellAddress[]; active: number }` |
| `command-state-change` | `{ states }`: every command's `GridCommandState`. See [Host-owned command state](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/toolbar-and-ribbon/#host-owned-command-state). |
| `mutation-rejected` | `{ issues: MutationIssue[] }` |
| `active-sheet` | `{ sheet: SheetId }`, after the visible sheet changes (direct call or cross-sheet scroll). |
| `hyperlink-activate` | `HyperlinkActivationEvent` |
| `theme-change` | `{ theme: Theme }`, after `setTheme` or `replaceTheme` changes the base theme. |
| `renderer-fallback` | `{ requested: "worker"; error: SheetwriteError }`, once, when the worker renderer could not be constructed. |
| `datasource-error` | `{ request; error: SheetwriteError }`; `request` is the `DataSourceRequest` without its `signal`. |
| `export-error` | `{ format: "csv" \| "xlsx"; error: SheetwriteError }`, when a built-in toolbar or context-menu export fails. |

`commitReason` is one of `edit-blur`, `edit-enter`, `edit-tab`, `edit-programmatic`, `paste`, `cut`, `clear`, `fill`, `structure`, `style`, `replace`, `undo`, `redo` or `api`.

## Sync coordinator events

`SyncCoordinator` has its own event stream. `sync.on(fn)` returns an unsubscribe function:

```ts
const sync = new SyncCoordinator(grid, adapter, {
  documentId: "products",
  serverVersion: loadedSnapshot.version ?? 0,
});
const off = sync.on((event) => {
  if (event.type === "conflict") showConflict(event.response);
  if (event.type === "reload-required") requestFreshSnapshot();
});

saveButton.onclick = () => void sync.sendNext();
// later
off();
sync.destroy();
```

| `event.type` | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | `state` |
| `restored` | `pending` |
| `persisting`, `pending`, `sending` | `mutation` |
| `acknowledged` | `clientMutationId`, `version`, `duplicate` |
| `conflict` | `mutation`, `response` |
| `remote-applied` | `operation` |
| `reload-required` | `expectedVersion`, `receivedVersion`, optional `snapshot` |
| `reloaded`, `recovered` | `serverVersion`, `pending` |
| `storage-error`, `error` | `error`, optional `clientMutationId` |

## Edge cases and limits

- Persist only `change` events with `source: "local"`. Remote input is observable but never belongs in outgoing local persistence.
- `changes` is empty for commits that only change metadata.
- Hydration from a snapshot and datasource pages emit no user change event.
