### Sheetwrite 0.5.0

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.5.0/

Sheetwrite 0.5.0 adds an optional full formula engine, makes collaboration
recover without a reload, lets an app give engine memory back to the browser,
and makes large documents faster to load, edit, and undo. All seven packages
release as 0.5.0. Read the [breaking changes](#breaking-changes) first: most
apps already call `initSheetwrite()` and need no change.

## Highlights

- **Full formula engine.** `@sheetwrite/formulas` adds grouping, pivots,
`LAMBDA`, statistics, regression, finance, regex, and reshaping functions.
- **Spill references and array constants** in both engines: `=SUM(A1#)` and
`={1,2;3,4}`.
- **Large undo works.** Undo of a very large clear is one history step, sent as
one compressed operation or one atomic batch.
- **Conflict recovery without a reload.** `SyncCoordinator.recoverConflict()`
recovers a cell-level conflict on the live Grid.
- **Engine memory goes back to the browser.** `releaseEngineMemory()` moves
the live stores to a fresh engine instance: after a million-row sheet is
cleared to ten rows, WebAssembly memory drops from 173 MiB to 38 MiB.
- **String storage stays bounded.** Text that edits overwrite or clear is
reclaimed and reused instead of piling up for the life of the document.
- **Faster.** Loading 100,000 to 1,000,000 rows is 26–35% faster, XLSX import
38% faster, and CSV import 52% faster.

## New

### Full formula engine

`@sheetwrite/formulas` is the same Rust engine as `@sheetwrite/wasm`, built with
the analysis families. It has the same API and loaders. Select it one time,
before you create a Grid:

```ts
import { initSheetwrite } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import * as formulas from "@sheetwrite/formulas";

await initSheetwrite(undefined, formulas);
```

It adds:

- grouping and pivot tables: `GROUPBY`, `PIVOTBY`, `PERCENTOF`;
- `LAMBDA` and its helpers: `MAP`, `REDUCE`, `SCAN`, `BYROW`, `BYCOL`,
`MAKEARRAY`, `ISOMITTED`;
- 36 statistical distribution functions, descriptive statistics, and ranking;
- regression: `LINEST`, `LOGEST`, `TREND`, `GROWTH`, `FORECAST.LINEAR`;
- finance and working-day functions, including `NETWORKDAYS.INTL`;
- text: `TEXTSPLIT`, `TEXTBEFORE`, `TEXTAFTER`, and `REGEXTEST`,
`REGEXEXTRACT`, `REGEXREPLACE`;
- reshaping: `VSTACK`, `HSTACK`, `WRAPROWS`, `TOCOL`, `EXPAND`, `SORTBY`;
- database functions and matrices: `MMULT`, `MINVERSE`, `MDETERM`, `MUNIT`.

The default engine does not change: its function set and binary stay the same,
and formula assist suggests only the functions of the selected engine.

- [Analysis formulas guide](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/analysis-formulas/): one worked task per family.
- [Formula function contract](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/reference/formula-functions/): every function and its build.
- [Formula analysis showcase](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/showcases/formulas/): thirteen panels recalculate live over 20,000 orders.

### Formulas in both engines

- **Spill references.** `=SUM(A1#)` refers to the current spill of `A1` and
follows it when it changes size. XLSX files store it as `_xlfn.ANCHORARRAY`.
See [Spill references](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/dynamic-arrays-and-spills/#spill-references).
- **Array constants.** `={1,2;3,4}` spills two rows and two columns, and array
constants work as function arguments. See
[Array constants](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/dynamic-arrays-and-spills/#array-constants).
- **Array arithmetic.** Operators apply to each array element. Scalars and
single rows or columns expand to match the other operand.

### Large undo and atomic batches

Undo of a very large clear now works and stays one history step. The Grid sends
the restore as one compressed `restoreBlock` operation. If that still needs more
than one server version, it uses an atomic batch through the new optional
`PersistenceAdapter.commitBatch`: the server applies all versions or none, and
peers apply the whole batch in one transaction. An undo above every limit
changes nothing and emits `mutation-rejected`, and older edits stay undoable.
See [Undo and redo](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/#undo-and-redo) and
[Large undo and atomic batches](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/#large-undo-and-atomic-batches).

### Conflict recovery without a reload

After a base-version conflict, call `sync.recoverConflict()`. When the pending
work and the server versions it did not see change different cells, and neither
side inserts, deletes, or moves rows or columns, it applies the missed versions
to the live Grid, moves the pending queue onto the server head, and keeps undo
history. In every other case it returns `reload-required` with the reason and
changes nothing, so the host reloads as before. See
[Conflict and snapshot reload](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/#conflict-and-snapshot-reload).

### Release engine memory

A WebAssembly instance never gives memory back, so after a large import or
clear the page used to keep its peak for its whole life. Call
`releaseEngineMemory()` when the app is idle. It waits for running
transactions and page loads, then moves every live store into a fresh engine
instance and lets the browser free the old one. Values, formulas and their
cached results, spills, loaded datasource pages, unsaved edits, and undo
history all move. If any store cannot move, nothing changes.

WebAssembly memory before and after release Shorter is less memory · shared scale

**Million-row sheet cleared to ten rows**Pause ≈ 50 ms
Before**173 MiB**
After**38 MiB**

**Same clear, undo history kept**Pause ≈ 270 ms
Before**173 MiB**
After**76 MiB**

**Paged store with unsaved edits**Pause ≈ 5 ms
Before**38 MiB**
After**1.2 MiB**

Release never makes memory larger, and the pause grows with the live data.
See [Release retained engine memory](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/performance/memory/#release-retained-engine-memory).

### Other new APIs

Choose the layer you use:

Core — themes, row bridges, recovery, and memory

- **Read the theme:** `grid.getTheme()` returns the base theme.
Listen to `theme-change` for `setTheme` or `replaceTheme`.
- **Bound row-bridge history:** `maxRecentTransactions` in `createRowBridge`
sets the recent transaction ID window (default 8,192).
- **Inspect conflict recovery:** `SyncConflictRecovery`,
`SyncConflictReloadReason`, and the `recovered` event describe the result
and reasons of in-place recovery.
- **Return engine memory:** `releaseEngineMemory()` returns an
`EngineMemoryReleaseReport`. See the memory comparison above.

Engine — independent instances, bulk data, and windowed reads

- **Create an independent instance:** `createEngine()` and `EngineInstance`
in `wasm` and `formulas` share compiled code.
- **Read and write bulk data:** `setBlockPacked`, `setColumnBlockPacked`,
`loadedSpans`, and `cellSnapshots` in `wasm` use packed data.
- **Load formula inputs:** `formulaReadBands` in `wasm` identifies the cells
that visible formulas read.
- **Track raw string IDs:** `stringPoolEpoch` in `wasm` identifies their
string-pool generation.

## Breaking changes

| Change | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Core needs `initSheetwrite()`. Core now owns its own engine instance, so calling only `load()` from `@sheetwrite/wasm` or `@sheetwrite/formulas` no longer lets you create a Grid or a `SheetwriteStore`; the error says so. | Call `await initSheetwrite()` before you create a Grid or store. Apps that already do need no change. |
| A Grid with `presentation: "data-grid"` no longer adds empty, unnamed columns to fill its width. A spreadsheet still does. | Set `minColumns` if you want empty columns in a data grid. |
| `CellStore.setBlock` is removed from `@sheetwrite/wasm`. | Use `setBlockPacked` (row-major) or `setColumnBlockPacked` (column-major). |
| Raw string IDs from `@sheetwrite/wasm` can change when the string pool is rebuilt. | Drop cached string IDs when `stringPoolEpoch` changes. |

## Changed

- **String storage is reclaimed.** Text that edits overwrite or clear was kept
for the life of the document. After a commit that leaves at least 256 KiB of
dead text, and more dead text than live text, the engine rebuilds its string
pool and reuses the freed space. History keeps its own text, so undo is not
affected. To shrink WebAssembly memory itself, use `releaseEngineMemory()`.
- **One owner for formula results.** The engine stores calculated values,
spill output, and calculated errors apart from the cells you write. A write
always wins over a calculated value, as before; spill reads and writes next
to a spill are faster.
- **Fill and Replace all send one operation.** They used to send one
operation per cell, so the `maxOperations` transaction limit (10,000 by
default) rejected a fill or replace over more than 10,000 cells. They now
send one range operation, as paste already did, and only the
`maxEncodedBytes` limit applies. Events, undo, and sync results are the
same.
- **Resize previews.** Row and column resize show a preview while you drag and
record one undoable change on release, instead of changing the document on
every step.
- **Pointer gestures end with their context.** A drag ends when the sheet, view,
structure, or read-only state changes, and a second pointer cannot take over
a drag.
- **Selection before edit.** Selection changes are reported before
`edit-begin`.
- **Negative currency.** The minus sign comes before a currency prefix
(`-$246`), as in Excel.
- **Smaller packages.** Published packages no longer include source maps, and
the React, Vue, and Svelte adapters declare only CSS files as side effects, so
bundlers can remove unused JavaScript.
- **New dependency.** `@sheetwrite/core` depends on `fflate` 0.8.3 for the
restore codec.

## Fixed

### Formulas

- A spill that reads another spill shows its current values. Spills that read
each other show `#CYCLE!`.
- With a windowed datasource, a visible formula that reads an off-screen column
no longer stays `#LOADING!`.
- With a windowed datasource, a visible formula that reads a frozen row or a
merged cell no longer shows a loading marker or a stale value, and the cells
visible formulas read stay loaded while they are on screen.
- Exports, `getRange`, and find no longer unload cells that are on screen.
- `FILTER` works in debug builds when its input is smaller than its size bound.
- Decoded lookup ranges are released when recalculation ends.

### Collaboration and undo

- `rebaseDocumentOperations` no longer puts an edit on the wrong row when
pending work holds more than one operation and one side inserted or deleted
rows. An edit to a row the server deleted now returns a conflict instead of
being written onto another row.
- Undo after a collaborator inserts or deletes rows or columns restores the
cell you edited, instead of writing the old value onto another row.
- An undo above the transaction limits now emits `mutation-rejected` and leaves
older edits undoable, instead of failing silently every time.
- `MemoryPersistenceAdapter` works before the engine is initialized, and a
failed commit, including one member of an atomic batch, leaves the document
unchanged.

### Editing and display

- In the Svelte adapter, a live option such as `readOnly` changed while the
Grid starts is applied before `ready` fires. In every adapter, a ref or
`onReady` callback that throws now retires the new Grid, as React already did.
- Every editor commits to the cell it opened on, through sorting and filtering.
- A rejected fill leaves the selection unchanged.
- Paste across hidden columns writes only the visible columns, and one undo
reverts it.
- The toolbar, find bar, and context menu follow a theme change, and the
toolbar colour swatches show the theme's real colours.
- Row numbers no longer paint into the header corner while you scroll.
- Sheet tabs no longer scroll the page, and the sheet menu stays open when an
unrelated part of the page scrolls.
- A search highlight or note on a partly visible top row is no longer dropped.

## Performance

These medians come from alternating runs on the same machine. Times vary by
device and workload. The [performance page](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/performance/)
has the full measurements and package sizes.

### Faster paths

Bars show the time saved compared with 0.4.0. A full bar is 100%.
The lighter end shows the reported range. The Memory group shows bytes saved.

Load and import

Load 100,000 to 1,000,000 rows26–35% faster
Load number-only columns56–59% faster
Write a 1,000,000-cell block60% faster1.36 s → 0.55 s
CSV import, 200,000 × 1052% faster493 ms → 239 ms
XLSX import, 1 MB workbook38% faster1.68 s → 1.04 s
Restore 4,000,000 cells39% faster2.21 s → 1.35 s

Formulas

Change one constant among 100,000 formulas1,167× faster35 ms → 0.03 ms
`LET(x, lookup, x+x+x)`87% faster
Write next to a spill61% faster
`SUMPRODUCT`, `COUNTIF`, `SUMIFS`, `PERCENTILE` over ranges27–59% faster
Read a sheet with a spill32% faster

Rows and data operations

Insert 10,000 rows into 1,000,000 with a row bridge6,940× faster34.7 s → 5 ms
Value-list filter, 1,000 picks over 1,000,000 rows104× faster2.9 s → 28 ms
Delete a 100,000-cell sheet85% faster
Fill 10,000 to 100,000 cells66–67% faster
Replace all, 10,000 to 100,000 matches49–50% faster
Multi-key sort34–38% faster
Distinct values25–85% faster

Editing and rendering

One-cell commit to a 110,000-cell `MemoryPersistenceAdapter` documentNo full rebuildwas about 450 ms
Toolbar state for a 4,096-cell selection52% faster
Scroll with wrapped text39% faster
Row resize34% faster0.218 ms → 0.144 ms
Undo a 1,000,000-cell clear28% faster2.54 s → 1.83 s
Framework adapter mount and reset16–38% faster
Scroll with number formats14% faster

Memory

String-pool storage after 100,000 unique overwrites (not WebAssembly heap size)99.6% less84.3 MB → 0.35 MB
XLSX import peak memory34% less476 MiB → 312 MiB

### Slower paths

These paths took longer in 0.5.0. The bars show measured times, not speed ratios.

OperationLog scale · each tick is 10×Median time
0.1110100 ms

Column sum · 100,000 rows
0.4.0**0.21 ms**
0.5.0**0.44 ms**

Column sum · 1,000,000 rows
0.4.0**1.9 ms**
0.5.0**4.2 ms**

Create a 100,000-cell spill
0.4.0**10.6 ms**
0.5.0**11.2–13.5 ms**

The lighter end of the spill bar shows its reported range, not p95.

Column sums use `aggregate`. They were about 2× slower in 0.5.0.
[0.5.1](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.5.1/) made them about 2× faster again, but the
100,000-row case can still be slower than 0.4.0. See [#110](https://github.com/chh-ay/sheetwrite/issues/110).
The spill case was 6–27% slower. See [#109](https://github.com/chh-ay/sheetwrite/issues/109).

## Upgrade checklist

EveryoneRequired
Initialize the engine, then update every package together
Make sure you `await initSheetwrite()` before you create a Grid or store. Install 0.5.0 for each `@sheetwrite/*` package that you use.

If you call `CellStore.setBlock` from `@sheetwrite/wasm`Breaking
Use the packed block writers
Use `setBlockPacked` (row-major) or `setColumnBlockPacked` (column-major). They take all string cells as one UTF-8 buffer plus byte offsets.

If you run a persistence or collaboration serverRequired
Accept `restoreBlock` before 0.5.0 clients connect
Optional: implement `commitBatch` for undo that needs more than one version. See Large undo and atomic batches (https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/#large-undo-and-atomic-batches).

If you cache raw string IDs from `@sheetwrite/wasm`Required
Drop the cache when the string pool changes
Clear cached IDs when `stringPoolEpoch` changes.

If you use `presentation: "data-grid"` with filler columnsBehavior change
Set `minColumns`
Data-grid presentation no longer adds filler columns by itself.

If you want the analysis functionsOptional
Install the full formula engine
Install `@sheetwrite/formulas` and select it before you create a Grid.

If you hold large documents for a long timeOptional
Release engine memory when idle
Call `releaseEngineMemory()` after a large clear or import.

If you recover from sync conflictsOptional
Recover in place before you reload
Call `sync.recoverConflict()` before your reload path. See Conflict and snapshot reload (https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/#conflict-and-snapshot-reload).

If you check dependency licenses or lockfilesFor information
Expect `fflate` 0.8.3
`@sheetwrite/core` now depends on `fflate`. Your package manager installs it; you do not add it yourself.

The full list of changes is in each package's `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Concepts

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/

These pages explain the model under the API: which part owns each piece of
state, how the engine recalculates, how a document changes through operations,
and how failures reach your code. Read them before you design persistence or
collaboration.

- [Runtime ownership](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/runtime-ownership/): Understand Sheetwrite runtime, renderer, store, virtualization, and document ownership boundaries.
- [Calculation engine](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/calculation-engine/): Understand engine builds, incremental recalculation, spills, paged data, formula errors, volatility, and iteration.
- [Documents and operations](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/documents-and-operations/): Understand authoritative workbook snapshots, document operations, storage transactions, and cell inputs.
- [Error handling](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/error-handling/): Typed failures, stable codes, recovery paths, event direction, validation, and incomplete-data behavior.

### Import and export

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/

Sheetwrite reads and writes XLSX through the optional `@sheetwrite/xlsx`
package, and CSV and TSV through core. Each page says what a format keeps and
what it reports as a fidelity warning.

- [XLSX import](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-import/): Import workbook snapshots or rectangular tables with explicit fidelity warnings.
- [XLSX export](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/): Download an active-sheet table or save a workbook with formulas and supported formatting.
- [CSV and TSV](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/csv-and-tsv/): Exchange plain table values without installing the optional XLSX package.
- [Kept parts and round trips](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/): Keep eligible unmodelled XLSX parts as original compressed bytes and surface losses after edits.
- [Large files and streaming](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/): Read seekable files and write bounded chunks while retaining explicit XLSX resource limits.
- [LibreOffice compatibility](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/libreoffice-compatibility/): Understand the checked LibreOffice round trips, display fixes and known producer differences.

### Getting started

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/

New to Sheetwrite? Install it, then build your first grid. Choose an engine
when your workbook needs analysis formulas, and read the upgrade guide before
you move to a new release.

- [Installation](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/installation/): Install Sheetwrite for Vanilla, React, Vue, or Svelte and initialize its WebAssembly runtime.
- [First grid](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/first-grid/): Initialize Sheetwrite, create a workbook, and observe committed changes.
- [Choose an engine](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/choose-an-engine/): Use the default engine for standard formulas or select the full engine for analysis functions.
- [Upgrade to 0.6.0](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/upgrade-to-0-6-0/): Review formula recalculation, document protocol, XLSX fidelity, and optional UI changes before upgrading.

### Tutorials

Source: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/

Each tutorial builds one working result from an empty project, step by step.
Pick the one for your framework, or for Node.js on the server.

- [Excel in JavaScript](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-javascript/): Open an XLSX table, edit it in a browser Grid, and download a workbook without a framework.
- [Excel in React](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-react/): Open an XLSX table, edit it in React, and download the current workbook.
- [Excel in Vue](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-vue/): Open an XLSX table, edit it in Vue, and download the current workbook.
- [Excel in Svelte](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-svelte/): Open an XLSX table, edit it in Svelte, and download the current workbook.
- [Excel in Node.js](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-nodejs/): Read real XLSX file bytes and save a workbook snapshot on the server without a DOM.
- [Spreadsheet app with the ribbon](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/spreadsheet-app-with-ribbon/): Build a disposable spreadsheet shell with a ribbon, formula bar, sheet tabs and XLSX file controls.

## Public API declarations

Every symbol below is compiler-verified from the declaration files the packages ship. Entry-point classification, signatures, and source JSDoc are the complete public surface; anything absent is not public API.

### `@sheetwrite/charts`

#### `@sheetwrite/charts` — supported

Declaration target: `./dist/index.d.ts`
Source entry: `src/index.ts`
Page: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/charts/

##### `ChartAnchor` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartAnchor { row: number; col: number; offsetX: number; offsetY: number; width: number; height: number; }
```

Position in worksheet coordinates; dimensions and offsets use CSS pixels.

Members:
- `col` — 0-based column of the cell that holds the top-left corner.
- `row` — 0-based row of the cell that holds the top-left corner.

##### `ChartChangeEvent` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartChangeEvent { readonly epoch: number | undefined; readonly charts: readonly ChartRef[]; }
```

Charts whose `ChartView` may differ after one store commit. Emitted at most
once per commit, only when `charts` is not empty; each chart appears once.
A chart that no longer exists resolves to `null`.

Members:
- `charts` — Charts to resolve again, in commit order of the edits that touched them.
- `epoch` — Store epoch after the commit. `undefined` when the store sent its change
event without an epoch, which a custom `Store` can do.

##### `ChartDefinition` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartDefinition { id: string; kind: ChartKind; title?: string; axes?: { xTitle?: string; yTitle?: string; }; legend?: "none" | "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"; anchor: ChartAnchor; series: ChartSeries[]; }
```

Persisted chart definition; IDs are unique within the owning sheet.

Members:
- `axes` — Axis titles; `undefined` shows no axis titles.
- `legend` — Legend position; `undefined` lets the renderer use its default position.
- `title` — Text above the chart; `undefined` shows no title.

##### `ChartKind` — type

```ts
export type ChartKind = "column" | "bar" | "line" | "area" | "pie" | "doughnut" | "scatter";
```

Chart families that the document model supports.

##### `ChartRange` — type

```ts
export type ChartRange = Range | "#REF!";
```

A deleted source remains explicit instead of silently reading another cell.

##### `ChartRef` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartRef { readonly sheet: SheetId; readonly id: string; }
```

Stable identity of one chart: the sheet that owns it and its ID on that sheet.

##### `ChartRenderer` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartRenderer { mount(host: HTMLElement, chart: ChartRef, size: { width: number; height: number; }): MountedChart; dispose(): void; }
```

Draws charts into host elements that the grid's object layer owns.

Members:
- `mount` — `host` is an empty element that core owns, positions and clips.

##### `ChartSeries` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartSeries { name?: string; nameRange?: ChartRange; values: ChartRange; categories?: ChartRange; }
```

Sources are read in row-major order.

##### `ChartSeriesView` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartSeriesView { name: string; values: Array<number | null>; categories: Array<string | number | boolean | null>; numberFormats: Array<string | null>; categoryFormats: Array<string | null>; numberLocale: string | null; truncated: boolean; referenceError: boolean; }
```

Resolved plain data; the renderer does not read cells. Arrays follow source cells in row-major order.

Members:
- `categoryFormats` — Format code per category; date categories are serial numbers and need it to show as dates.
- `numberFormats` — Excel format code per value, as the grid paints it: cell style, then column style, then column format.
- `numberLocale` — BCP 47 locale of the first value column, for separators; `null` keeps the default.
- `referenceError` — A source was deleted; that source reads as empty.
- `truncated` — A source had more than `MAX_CHART_POINTS` cells and its tail was dropped.
- `values` — Numeric cells; text, booleans, errors and empty cells are `null` (a gap).

##### `ChartSize` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartSize { width: number; height: number; }
```

Box size in CSS pixels.

##### `ChartSvgOptions` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartSvgOptions { document?: Document; }
```

Options for `renderChartSvg`.

Members:
- `document` — Document that owns the new elements; the global `document` by default.

##### `ChartView` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartView { chart: ChartDefinition; series: ChartSeriesView[]; }
```

One immutable-by-convention rendering input, refreshed on chart-change events.

##### `ChartViewCache` — type

```ts
export type ChartViewCache = ChartViewProvider;
```

Resolved chart views for one store, refreshed only by chart-change events.

Listeners run after the changed charts are invalidated, so `get` inside a
listener always resolves the committed cell data.

##### `createChartRenderer` — function

```ts
(store: Store): ChartRenderer
```

Creates the SVG chart renderer for one store. All mounted charts share one
view cache. A chart redraws after a chart-change event names it, or after a
resize, at most once per animation frame. Scrolling never redraws a chart.
@example
```ts
import { createChartRenderer } from "@sheetwrite/charts";
import type { ChartRef, Store } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function showChart(store: Store, host: HTMLElement, chart: ChartRef) {
 const renderer = createChartRenderer(store);
 const mounted = renderer.mount(host, chart, { width: 320, height: 200 });
 return () => {
 mounted.dispose();
 renderer.dispose();
 };
}
```

##### `createChartViewCache` — function

```ts
(store: Store): ChartViewCache
```

Creates the per-store chart view cache a chart renderer reads from.

Views resolve lazily on first `get` and stay cached until a chart-change
event names that chart, so repeated frames never reread cells.
@example
```ts
import { createChartViewCache, type ChartView } from "@sheetwrite/charts";
import type { SheetId, Store } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function watchChart(
 store: Store,
 sheet: SheetId,
 id: string,
 render: (view: ChartView | null) => void,
) {
 const charts = createChartViewCache(store);
 render(charts.get({ sheet, id }));
 const unsubscribe = charts.subscribe((event) => {
 if (event.charts.some((chart) => chart.sheet === sheet && chart.id === id)) {
 render(charts.get({ sheet, id }));
 }
 });
 return () => {
 unsubscribe();
 charts.dispose();
 };
}
```

##### `MountedChart` — interface

```ts
export interface MountedChart { resize(width: number, height: number): void; dispose(): void; }
```

Draws one chart into a box that core places and sizes.

Members:
- `resize` — Core calls this after it changes the box size in CSS pixels.

##### `registerChartsBackend` — function

```ts
(): void
```

Register the chart view cache as the core chart view provider, so
`openChartViews(store)` returns live chart views, and the SVG chart renderer,
so grids created after this call draw their charts.
@example
```ts
import { registerChartsBackend } from "@sheetwrite/charts";
import { openChartViews, type Store } from "@sheetwrite/core";

registerChartsBackend();

function salesChartValues(store: Store) {
 const charts = openChartViews(store);
 const values = charts.get({ sheet: "s", id: "sales" })?.series[0]?.values ?? [];
 charts.dispose();
 return values;
}
```

##### `renderChartSvg` — function

```ts
(view: ChartView, size: ChartSize, options?: ChartSvgOptions): SVGSVGElement
```

Draws a chart view as a standalone SVG element of `size` CSS pixels.

Series colors read `--sheetwrite-chart-1` to `--sheetwrite-chart-8`, and text
reads the grid theme variables, so the chart follows the host theme. The
function reads no cells and keeps no state.
@example
```ts
import { renderChartSvg, type ChartView } from "@sheetwrite/charts";

function showChart(host: HTMLElement, view: ChartView) {
 host.replaceChildren(renderChartSvg(view, { width: 320, height: 200 }));
}
```

#### `@sheetwrite/charts/register` — supported

Declaration target: `./dist/register.d.ts`
Source entry: `src/register.ts`
Page: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/charts-register/

##### `registerChartsBackend` — function

```ts
(): void
```

Register the chart view cache as the core chart view provider, so
`openChartViews(store)` returns live chart views, and the SVG chart renderer,
so grids created after this call draw their charts.
@example
```ts
import { registerChartsBackend } from "@sheetwrite/charts";
import { openChartViews, type Store } from "@sheetwrite/core";

registerChartsBackend();

function salesChartValues(store: Store) {
 const charts = openChartViews(store);
 const values = charts.get({ sheet: "s", id: "sales" })?.series[0]?.values ?? [];
 charts.dispose();
 return values;
}
```

### `@sheetwrite/core`

#### `@sheetwrite/core` — supported

Declaration target: `./dist/index.d.ts`
Source entry: `src/index.ts`
Page: https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/

##### `AggregateOp` — type

```ts
export type AggregateOp = "sum" | "avg" | "min" | "max" | "count";
```

Column aggregate operation for `Grid.aggregate` / `Store` data ops.

##### `ApplyTransactionResult` — type

```ts
export type ApplyTransactionResult = | { status: "applied"; epoch: number; transaction: Transaction; warnings?: MutationIssue[]; rejections?: MutationIssue[]; } | { status: "conflict"; expectedEpoch: number; actualEpoch: number } | { status: "rejected"; epoch: number; issues: MutationIssue[]; } | { status: "noop"; epoch: number; reason: "empty" | "out-of-bounds" | "incomplete-data" | "read-only"; };
```

Outcome of applying a document transaction, including conflict, rejection, and no-op states.

##### `assertRuntimeResourceSnapshot` — function

```ts
(snapshot: RuntimeResourceSnapshot): void
```

Reject overlap, negative values, and attempts to fold runtime observations into owner totals.

##### `assertWorkbookTables` — function

```ts
(sheets: readonly Sheet[], limits?: Readonly<WorkbookTableResourceLimits>, reservedNames?: readonly string[]): void
```

Reject an invalid or oversized live workbook before table arrays are copied to WASM.

##### `BoundaryDirection` — type

```ts
export type BoundaryDirection = "js-to-wasm" | "wasm-to-js";
```

Direction of a measured JS/WASM boundary crossing.

##### `BoundaryOperationStats` — interface

```ts
export interface BoundaryOperationStats { readonly operation: RuntimeResourceOperation; readonly ffiCalls: number; readonly jsToWasmBytes: number; readonly wasmToJsBytes: number; readonly largestTransferBytes: number; readonly bulkCalls: number; readonly scalarCalls: number; }
```

Fixed-cardinality boundary crossing counters for one operation.

##### `BoundaryTransferKind` — type

```ts
export type BoundaryTransferKind = "bulk" | "scalar";
```

Whether a measured boundary crossing transfers one scalar or a packed batch.

##### `CalculationSettings` — interface

```ts
export interface CalculationSettings { iterate: boolean; maxIterations: number; maxChange: number; }
```

Workbook calculation options, mirroring Excel's "Enable iterative calculation".
A workbook without this record uses the defaults.

Members:
- `iterate` — Recalculate circular references iteratively instead of showing `#CYCLE!`; Excel default `false`.
- `maxChange` — Iteration stops once no value changes by more than this; finite and >= 0, Excel default 0.001.
- `maxIterations` — Most passes over each circular reference; an integer from 1 to 32,767, Excel default 100.

##### `cellA1` — function

```ts
(row: number, col: number): string
```

0-based (row, col) → A1 cell reference (0, 0 → "A1").

##### `CellAddress` — interface

```ts
export interface CellAddress { sheet: SheetId; row: number; col: number; }
```

Zero-based address of one cell on a stable sheet ID.

##### `CellAlign` — type

```ts
export type CellAlign = "left" | "center" | "right";
```

Horizontal text alignment supported by cell styles.

##### `CellBlock` — interface

```ts
export interface CellBlock { startRow: number; startCol: number; rowCount: number; colCount: number; cells: SnapshotCell[]; }
```

Sparse row-major cells bounded by one rectangular block.

##### `CellBorder` — interface

```ts
export interface CellBorder { color?: string; width?: number; style?: "solid" | "dashed" | "dotted"; }
```

Visual border applied to one or more sides of a cell.

Members:
- `color` — hex color, e.g. "#111111"

##### `CellBorders` — interface

```ts
export interface CellBorders { all?: CellBorder; top?: CellBorder; right?: CellBorder; bottom?: CellBorder; left?: CellBorder; }
```

Per-side borders; `all` applies to any side not given its own border.

##### `CellChange` — interface

```ts
export interface CellChange { addr: CellAddress; oldValue: CellValue; newValue: CellValue; oldStyle?: CellStyle; newStyle?: CellStyle; }
```

One committed cell edit, carrying enough to roll back.

##### `CellEditor` — interface

```ts
export interface CellEditor { mount(host: HTMLElement, context: CellEditorContext): CellEditorInstance; }
```

Framework-neutral named editor definition registered through GridOptions.editors.

##### `CellEditorContext` — interface

```ts
export interface CellEditorContext { readonly grid: Grid; readonly address: Readonly<CellAddress>; readonly viewAddress: Readonly<CellAddress>; readonly column: Readonly<Column>; readonly value: CellScalar; readonly text: string; readonly initialInput: string | undefined; readonly selectAll: boolean; readonly label: string; readonly signal: AbortSignal; commit(value: string, navigation?: CellEditorNavigation): void; cancel(): void; }
```

Immutable state and guarded completion callbacks for one mounted editor.

##### `CellEditorInstance` — interface

```ts
export interface CellEditorInstance { update(context: CellEditorContext): void; reposition(rect: CellEditorRect): void; commit(navigation: CellEditorNavigation): string | undefined | Promise<string | undefined>; cancel(): void; destroy(): void; }
```

Retained lifecycle returned by a custom editor's mount method.

##### `CellEditorNavigation` — type

```ts
export type CellEditorNavigation = "down" | "right" | "left" | "none";
```

Selection movement applied after a successful editor commit.

##### `CellEditorRect` — interface

```ts
export interface CellEditorRect { readonly x: number; readonly y: number; readonly width: number; readonly height: number; }
```

Viewport-relative geometry of the cell currently owned by an editor.

##### `CellFormat` — type

```ts
export type CellFormat = "text" | "number" | "date" | "currency";
```

How a column's cells are typed, parsed, and rendered: `text` verbatim, `number`
via its `numberFormat`, `date` as an Excel-style serial (see `date-serial.ts`)
rendered by a date `numberFormat`, and `currency` as a plain number rendered by
a currency `numberFormat` (e.g. `$#,##0.00`).

##### `CellHyperlink` — interface

```ts
export interface CellHyperlink { id: string; range: Range; target: HyperlinkTarget; display?: string; style?: CellStyle; }
```

Bounded serializable hyperlink metadata applied to one cell or range.

Members:
- `display` — Optional accessible/OOXML display label; cell values remain authoritative.
- `id` — Stable identity used by operations, history, and collaboration rebase.
- `style` — Optional override merged over the deterministic blue/underline link style.

##### `CellInputSnapshot` — interface

```ts
export interface CellInputSnapshot { readonly address: CellAddress; readonly text: string; readonly format: CellFormat; }
```

View-aware editable snapshot of one cell, for hosts building a detached
formula bar or cell inspector. `address` is the translated *data* address —
the correct target for `Grid.applyTransaction` even under an active
sort/filter view — while the `(row, col)` inputs of
{@link Grid.getCellInput} are active-sheet view coordinates.

Members:
- `address` — Underlying data address, suitable for a `set` patch.
- `format` — Column input format, for `parseCellInput`.
- `text` — Formula source when the cell is a formula, else the literal display text.

##### `CellLoadState` — type

```ts
export type CellLoadState = "unloaded" | "loaded-empty" | "loaded-value" | "local-edit";
```

Datasource loading state for a resolved cell.

##### `CellNote` — interface

```ts
export interface CellNote { addr: CellAddress; text: string; }
```

Serializable plain-text note anchored to a cell.

##### `CellPaintContext` — interface

```ts
export interface CellPaintContext { value: CellScalar; x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number; theme: Theme; style: CellStyle; }
```

Read-only cell value and screen geometry supplied to a custom renderer.

##### `CellRenderer` — interface

```ts
export interface CellRenderer { canvas?(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, c: CellPaintContext): void; dom?(c: CellPaintContext): HTMLElement; update?(element: HTMLElement, c: CellPaintContext): void; destroy?(element: HTMLElement): void; }
```

Custom cell renderer hooks for the main-thread canvas or retained DOM overlay.

Members:
- `destroy` — Runs immediately before a retained element is removed or replaced.
- `dom` — Creates a fresh, detached element uniquely owned by one retained DOM cell.
- `update` — Updates a retained element after its value, style, theme, or geometry changes.

##### `CellScalar` — type

```ts
export type CellScalar = string | number | boolean | null;
```

A scalar that can be displayed directly.

##### `cellScalarToText` — function

```ts
(value: CellScalar): string
```

Spreadsheet display text for a resolved scalar.

##### `CellStyle` — interface

```ts
export interface CellStyle { bold?: boolean; italic?: boolean; underline?: boolean; strikethrough?: boolean; fontSize?: number; fontFamily?: string; color?: string; backgroundColor?: string; align?: CellAlign; verticalAlign?: CellVerticalAlign; numberFormat?: string; wrap?: boolean; border?: CellBorders; }
```

Serializable formatting applied to a cell or used as a column default.

Members:
- `align` — Horizontal placement of cell text within its column.
- `backgroundColor` — hex color, e.g. "#ffffff"
- `bold` — Uses the bold variant of the theme font.
- `border` — Border overrides for the cell's individual sides.
- `color` — hex color, e.g. "#111111"
- `fontFamily` — Font family name, e.g. "Calibri". The theme font family stays the fallback,
so a font the browser lacks renders in the theme font. Letters, digits,
spaces, `.`, `_` and `-` only; at most 128 characters.
- `fontSize` — Font size in unzoomed CSS pixels; zoom is applied during painting.
- `italic` — Uses the italic variant of the theme font.
- `numberFormat` — Excel number-format code for this cell, e.g. "0.00%". Overrides the
column's `numberFormat`; at most 255 characters.
- `strikethrough` — Draws a line through each rendered text run.
- `underline` — Draws a line beneath each rendered text run.
- `verticalAlign` — Vertical placement of cell text; omitted keeps text centered.
- `wrap` — Wraps text within the cell width; row auto-fit accounts for the resulting line count.

##### `CellValue` — type

```ts
export type CellValue = | { kind: "literal"; value: CellScalar } | { kind: "ref"; target: CellAddress } | { kind: "formula"; src: string };
```

A cell's persisted input: a literal, a cross-reference, or a formula.
References resolve through the store's reference graph; formulas resolve in
the WASM calculation engine.

##### `CellVerticalAlign` — type

```ts
export type CellVerticalAlign = "top" | "middle" | "bottom";
```

Vertical text placement within a cell's height.

##### `ChangeEvent` — interface

```ts
export interface ChangeEvent { transaction: Transaction; changes: CellChange[]; commitReason: CommitReason; source: OperationSource; epoch?: number; }
```

Payload of the `change` event; flows OUT for API submission/reconcile.

Members:
- `changes` — Cell-level before/after effects; empty for commits that only change metadata.
- `commitReason` — What produced this commit — see {@link CommitReason}.
- `epoch` — Store epoch after the commit; emitted store and grid changes include it.
- `source` — Remote input is observable but never belongs in outgoing local persistence.
- `transaction` — Operations that actually committed after policy and bounds filtering.

##### `ChartAnchor` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartAnchor { row: number; col: number; offsetX: number; offsetY: number; width: number; height: number; }
```

Position in worksheet coordinates; dimensions and offsets use CSS pixels.

Members:
- `col` — 0-based column of the cell that holds the top-left corner.
- `row` — 0-based row of the cell that holds the top-left corner.

##### `ChartChangeEvent` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartChangeEvent { readonly epoch: number | undefined; readonly charts: readonly ChartRef[]; }
```

Charts whose `ChartView` may differ after one store commit. Emitted at most
once per commit, only when `charts` is not empty; each chart appears once.
A chart that no longer exists resolves to `null`.

Members:
- `charts` — Charts to resolve again, in commit order of the edits that touched them.
- `epoch` — Store epoch after the commit. `undefined` when the store sent its change
event without an epoch, which a custom `Store` can do.

##### `ChartChangeListener` — type

```ts
export type ChartChangeListener = (event: ChartChangeEvent) => void;
```

Listener for `subscribeChartChanges` and `ChartViewProvider.subscribe`.

##### `ChartDefinition` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartDefinition { id: string; kind: ChartKind; title?: string; axes?: { xTitle?: string; yTitle?: string }; legend?: "none" | "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"; anchor: ChartAnchor; series: ChartSeries[]; }
```

Persisted chart definition; IDs are unique within the owning sheet.

Members:
- `axes` — Axis titles; `undefined` shows no axis titles.
- `legend` — Legend position; `undefined` lets the renderer use its default position.
- `title` — Text above the chart; `undefined` shows no title.

##### `ChartKind` — type

```ts
export type ChartKind = "column" | "bar" | "line" | "area" | "pie" | "doughnut" | "scatter";
```

Chart families that the document model supports.

##### `ChartRange` — type

```ts
export type ChartRange = Range | "#REF!";
```

A deleted source remains explicit instead of silently reading another cell.

##### `ChartRef` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartRef { readonly sheet: SheetId; readonly id: string; }
```

Stable identity of one chart: the sheet that owns it and its ID on that sheet.

##### `ChartRenderer` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartRenderer { mount(host: HTMLElement, chart: ChartRef, size: { width: number; height: number }): MountedChart; dispose(): void; }
```

Draws charts into host elements that the grid's object layer owns.

Members:
- `mount` — `host` is an empty element that core owns, positions and clips.

##### `ChartRendererFactory` — type

```ts
export type ChartRendererFactory = (store: Store) => ChartRenderer;
```

Creates the chart renderer of one grid. The grid disposes it. It lives next
to `ChartViewProviderFactory` because the chart type domain cannot read `Store`.

##### `ChartSeries` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartSeries { name?: string; nameRange?: ChartRange; values: ChartRange; categories?: ChartRange; }
```

Sources are read in row-major order.

##### `ChartSeriesView` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartSeriesView { name: string; values: Array<number | null>; categories: Array<string | number | boolean | null>; numberFormats: Array<string | null>; categoryFormats: Array<string | null>; numberLocale: string | null; truncated: boolean; referenceError: boolean; }
```

Resolved plain data; the renderer does not read cells. Arrays follow source cells in row-major order.

Members:
- `categoryFormats` — Format code per category; date categories are serial numbers and need it to show as dates.
- `numberFormats` — Excel format code per value, as the grid paints it: cell style, then column style, then column format.
- `numberLocale` — BCP 47 locale of the first value column, for separators; `null` keeps the default.
- `referenceError` — A source was deleted; that source reads as empty.
- `truncated` — A source had more than `MAX_CHART_POINTS` cells and its tail was dropped.
- `values` — Numeric cells; text, booleans, errors and empty cells are `null` (a gap).

##### `ChartView` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartView { chart: ChartDefinition; series: ChartSeriesView[]; }
```

One immutable-by-convention rendering input, refreshed on chart-change events.

##### `ChartViewProvider` — interface

```ts
export interface ChartViewProvider { get(chart: ChartRef): ChartView | null; subscribe(listener: ChartChangeListener): () => void; dispose(): void; }
```

Cached chart views supplied by the optional charts package; renderers do not read cells.

Members:
- `dispose` — Stop observing the store and release cached views.
- `get` — Resolve on first access; later accesses use the cached committed view.
- `subscribe` — Observe invalidation after cached views have been removed.

##### `ChartViewProviderFactory` — type

```ts
export type ChartViewProviderFactory = (store: Store) => ChartViewProvider;
```

Creates a chart provider owned and disposed by one renderer or host.

##### `colToA1` — function

```ts
(col: number): string
```

Column index (0-based) → A1 column label (0 → "A", 26 → "AA").

##### `Column` — interface

```ts
export interface Column { key: string; header: string; width: number; type: CellFormat; numberFormat?: string; numberLocale?: string; headerStyle?: CellStyle; cellStyle?: CellStyle; visible?: boolean; renderer?: string; editor?: string; }
```

Schema and default presentation for one workbook column.

Members:
- `cellStyle` — Base style merged beneath each cell's own style.
- `editor` — Name of a registered custom editor (see `GridOptions.editors`).
- `header` — Schema label used by table exports and data-grid presentation headers.
- `headerStyle` — Overrides theme styling for the painted column header.
- `key` — Non-empty key, unique within the sheet, used to map input and datasource values.
- `numberFormat` — Excel number-format code, e.g. "#,##0.00"
- `numberLocale` — Explicit BCP 47 locale for separators; omitted keeps the deterministic default.
- `renderer` — Name of a registered custom cell renderer (see `Grid.defineCellRenderer`).
- `type` — Controls cell input parsing and default value formatting for this column.
- `visible` — Set to `false` to exclude the column from the live view and table exports.
- `width` — Unzoomed column width in CSS pixels.

##### `ColumnarData` — interface

```ts
export interface ColumnarData { rowCount: number; columns: Record<string, ArrayLike<CellScalar | CellValue>>; }
```

Eager column-oriented values used to initialize a sheet.

##### `ColumnFilter` — type

```ts
export type ColumnFilter = | { kind: "values"; values: readonly CellScalar[] } | { kind: "contains"; text: string; matchCase?: boolean } | { kind: "compare"; op: "gt" | "gte" | "lt" | "lte" | "eq" | "neq"; value: number } | { kind: "empty" } | { kind: "nonEmpty" };
```

One column's filter predicate. All active column filters AND together;
matching is against the cell's resolved value (text or number).

##### `CommentAdapter` — interface

```ts
export interface CommentAdapter { listComments(documentId: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<CommentListResult>; mutateComment(request: CommentMutationRequest): Promise<CommentMutationResponse>; subscribeComments?( documentId: string, listener: (event: VersionedCommentEvent) => void, signal?: AbortSignal, ): undefined | (() => void); }
```

Host persistence contract for versioned comment threads.

##### `CommentAnchor` — type

```ts
export type CommentAnchor = | { kind: "cell"; address: { sheet: string; row: number; col: number } } | { kind: "range"; range: Range };
```

Document location to which a comment thread is attached.

##### `CommentAuthorRef` — interface

```ts
export interface CommentAuthorRef { id: string; displayName?: string; avatarUrl?: string; }
```

Stable host-provided identity displayed on a comment message.

##### `CommentCoordinator` — class

```ts
class CommentCoordinator { constructor(adapter: CommentAdapter, options: CommentCoordinatorOptions); commentThreads: () => readonly CommentThread[]; create: (threadId: string, messageId: string, anchor: CommentAnchor, body: string, clientMutationId: string) => Promise<CommentMutationResponse>; destroy: () => void; load: () => Promise<readonly CommentThread[]>; mutate: (mutation: CommentMutation, clientMutationId: string) => Promise<CommentMutationResponse>; on: (listener: CommentListener) => () => void; reply: (threadId: string, messageId: string, body: string, clientMutationId: string) => Promise<CommentMutationResponse>; resolve: (threadId: string, resolved: boolean, clientMutationId: string) => Promise<CommentMutationResponse>; serverVersion: number }
```

Transport/auth-neutral comment state with server-owned author and timestamp fields.

##### `CommentCoordinatorEvent` — type

```ts
export type CommentCoordinatorEvent = | { type: "loaded"; version: number; threads: readonly CommentThread[] } | { type: "changed"; version: number; thread: CommentThread } | { type: "conflict"; currentVersion: number } | { type: "gap"; expectedVersion: number; receivedVersion: number } | { type: "error"; error: SheetwriteError };
```

State transition emitted by the comment coordinator.

##### `CommentCoordinatorOptions` — interface

##### `CommentMessage` — interface

One immutable author message in a comment thread.

##### `CommentMutation` — type

```ts
export type CommentMutation = | { kind: "create"; threadId: string; messageId: string; anchor: CommentAnchor; body: string; } | { kind: "reply"; threadId: string; messageId: string; body: string } | { kind: "resolve"; threadId: string; resolved: boolean };
```


Applied, duplicate, or conflict acknowledgement for a comment mutation.

##### `CommentThread` — interface

```ts
export interface CommentThread { id: string; documentId: string; anchor: CommentAnchor; version: number; messages: readonly CommentMessage[]; resolved: boolean; resolvedBy?: CommentAuthorRef; resolvedAt?: string; }
```

Versioned discussion anchored to a document location.

##### `CommitReason` — type

```ts
export type CommitReason = | "edit-blur" | "edit-enter" | "edit-tab" | "edit-programmatic" | "paste" | "cut" | "clear" | "fill" | "structure" | "style" | "replace" | "undo" | "redo" | "api";
```

The gesture/operation that produced a committed transaction. Consumers
switching on reasons MUST keep a default branch — the union grows with new
mutation features.

##### `ConditionalFormatPredicate` — type

```ts
export type ConditionalFormatPredicate = | { kind: "greaterThan"; value: number } | { kind: "lessThan"; value: number } | { kind: "equal"; value: CellScalar } | { kind: "contains"; text: string; matchCase?: boolean } | { kind: "formula"; source: string };
```

Predicate used to decide whether a conditional format applies.

##### `ConditionalFormatRule` — interface

```ts
export interface ConditionalFormatRule { range: Range; when: ConditionalFormatPredicate; style: CellStyle; stopIfTrue?: boolean; }
```

Ordered condition and style applied to a cell range.

Members:
- `stopIfTrue` — Stop evaluating lower-precedence rules for a cell when this rule matches.

##### `ContextMenuActionName` — type

```ts
export type ContextMenuActionName = | "cut" | "copy" | "paste" | "clearContents" | "merge" | "unmerge" | "insertRowAbove" | "insertRowBelow" | "deleteRow" | "insertColumnLeft" | "insertColumnRight" | "deleteColumn" | "hideRow" | "showAllRows" | "autoFitRow" | "hideColumn" | "showAllColumns" | "autoFitColumn" | "clearFilter" | "exportCsv" | "exportXlsx" | "editNote" | "deleteNote" | "pivotFields" | "separator";
```

Built-in action names accepted by custom context-menu rows.

##### `ContextMenuContext` — interface

```ts
export interface ContextMenuContext { readonly cell: CellAddress | null; readonly clientX: number; readonly clientY: number; }
```

Cell and viewport coordinates resolved for one bundled context-menu opening.

Members:
- `cell` — Right-clicked cell, or null when the pointer is outside the cell body.
- `clientX` — Viewport-relative browser pointer coordinate.
- `clientY` — Viewport-relative browser pointer coordinate.

##### `ContextMenuItem` — interface

```ts
export interface ContextMenuItem { id?: string; action?: ContextMenuActionName; onClick?: (grid: Grid, cell: CellAddress | null) => void; label?: string; shortcut?: KeyboardAction | KeyShortcut; visible?: boolean | ((context: ContextMenuContext) => boolean); disabled?: boolean | ((context: ContextMenuContext) => boolean); icon?: IconName; items?: readonly ContextMenuItem[]; }
```

Built-in, separator, or custom callback row in the right-click menu.
@example
```ts
import type { ContextMenuItem, GridConfig } from "@sheetwrite/core";

const total: ContextMenuItem = {
 id: "total",
 label: "Show total",
 onClick(grid) { window.alert(String(grid.aggregate(0, "sum"))); },
};
const config: GridConfig = { contextMenu: [total, { action: "separator" }, { action: "copy" }] };
```
@see
ContextMenuItems
@see
GridConfig.contextMenu

Members:
- `action` — Built-in action to bind (or "separator"). Omit when supplying `onClick`.
- `disabled` — Static or context-aware disabled state.
- `icon` — Glyph shown before the label. Built-in actions have one by default; `config.icons` overrides apply.
- `id` — Stable host identifier, exposed as `data-context-menu-item`.
- `items` — Rows of a submenu. The row opens it on click, hover or the Right Arrow key and runs nothing itself.
- `label` — Menu row text. Defaults per action.
- `onClick` — Custom click handler; receives the grid and the right-clicked cell (null if none).
- `shortcut` — A bound action name or a custom key combination. An explicit combination
registers `onClick` as a keyboard command; action names only reference the
existing built-in binding. Both forms display platform-aware labels.
For example, `shortcut: "copy"` follows the configured Copy binding, while
`shortcut: "Mod+Shift+K"` binds this item's `onClick` callback.
See {@link KeyboardOptions} for built-in action overrides.
- `visible` — Static or request-aware visibility. Hidden separators are normalized.

##### `ContextMenuItems` — type

```ts
export type ContextMenuItems = | readonly ContextMenuItem[] | ((context: ContextMenuContext) => readonly ContextMenuItem[]);
```

Static rows or a context-aware factory evaluated each time the menu opens.

##### `createGrid` — function

```ts
(host: HTMLElement, opts: GridOptions): Grid
```

Creates and mounts an imperative Grid in the supplied host element.
@example
```ts
import { createGrid, initSheetwrite } from "@sheetwrite/core";

await initSheetwrite();
const host = document.createElement("div");
host.style.height = "400px";
document.body.append(host);
const grid = createGrid(host, {
 workbook: {
 activeSheet: "sales",
 sheets: [{ id: "sales", name: "Sales", rowCount: 2,
 columns: [{ key: "amount", header: "Amount", type: "number", width: 120 }] }],
 },
 data: { rowCount: 2, columns: { amount: [12, 18] } },
});
grid.scrollToCell({ sheet: "sales", row: 1, col: 0 });
// Call when the host view is removed.
grid.destroy();
```
@see
Grid
@see
GridOptions

##### `createGridFromSnapshot` — function

```ts
(host: HTMLElement, snapshot: unknown, options?: SnapshotGridOptions): Grid
```

Mount a grid over a validated, non-dirty snapshot. The grid owns and disposes
the hydrated store just like one created through `createGrid`.

##### `createRowBridge` — function

```ts
<Row extends Record<string, CellScalar>, Id extends RowBridgeId = RowBridgeId>(options: RowBridgeOptions<Row, Id>): RowBridge<Id>
```

Create a typed bridge while preserving row and identity inference.
@example
```ts
import { createRowBridge } from "@sheetwrite/core";

const bridge = createRowBridge({
 columns: [{ key: "amount" }],
 defaultRows: [{ id: "order-1", amount: 12 }],
 getRowId: (row) => row.id,
});
```
@see
RowBridgeOptions
@see

##### `createRuntimeResourceSnapshot` — function

```ts
(input: { operation: RuntimeResourceOperation; phase: RuntimeResourcePhase; wasm: StoreMemoryBreakdown; jsOwners?: readonly ResourceOwnerBytes[]; boundary?: readonly BoundaryOperationStats[]; runtime?: RuntimeMemoryObservation; }): RuntimeResourceSnapshot
```

##### `DataCell` — type

```ts
export type DataCell = CellScalar | CellValue | { value: CellValue; style?: CellStyle };
```

Datasource cell value with optional cell-specific styling.

##### `DataSource` — interface

```ts
export interface DataSource { readonly capabilities: DataSourceCapabilities; getRows(request: DataSourceRequest): Promise<DataSourcePage>; }
```

Host callback that asynchronously loads cancellable rectangular pages.
@example
```ts
import type { DataSource, RowData } from "@sheetwrite/core";

const rows: RowData[] = [{ amount: 12 }, { amount: 18 }];
const datasource: DataSource = {
 capabilities: { protocol: 2, columns: "windowed" },
 async getRows(request) {
 request.signal.throwIfAborted();
 return {
 protocol: 2, start: request.start, columns: request.columns,
 rows: rows.slice(request.start, request.end).map((row) =>
 Object.fromEntries(request.columns.flatMap((band) =>
 band.keys.map((key) => [key, row[key] ?? null])))),
 };
 },
};
```
@see
GridOptions.datasource
@see
DataSourceRequest

Members:
- `getRows` — Loads the requested rows and columns; implementations should stop work when its signal aborts.

##### `DataSourceCapabilities` — interface

```ts
export interface DataSourceCapabilities { protocol: 2; columns: "windowed" | "full-width"; }
```

Declares whether a source can load only the requested column runs.

##### `DataSourceColumnBand` — interface

```ts
export interface DataSourceColumnBand { start: number; end: number; keys: readonly string[]; }
```

One half-open run of workbook columns, in stable sheet order.

Members:
- `end` — Exclusive workbook column index after the last key.
- `keys` — Stable workbook column keys for every index in `[start, end)`.
- `start` — Zero-based workbook column index of the first key.

##### `DataSourcePage` — interface

```ts
export interface DataSourcePage { protocol: 2; start: number; columns: readonly DataSourceColumnBand[]; rows: RowData[]; revision?: string | number; }
```

One resolved rectangular page returned by a DataSource.

Members:
- `columns` — Exact column runs represented by every returned row.
- `protocol` — Paging contract version.
- `start` — Inclusive row index of the first returned row.

##### `DataSourceRequest` — interface

```ts
export interface DataSourceRequest { protocol: 2; sheet: SheetId; start: number; end: number; columns: readonly DataSourceColumnBand[]; signal: AbortSignal; revision: number; }
```

Cancellable sheet rectangle requested from a DataSource.

Members:
- `columns` — Exact visible, frozen, or prefetched column runs required by the Grid.
- `end` — Exclusive row index.
- `protocol` — Paging contract version.
- `start` — Inclusive row index.

##### `DataSourceStorageOptions` — interface

```ts
export interface DataSourceStorageOptions { mode?: "dense" | "paged"; chunkRows?: number; cacheBytes?: number; dirtyCellLimit?: number; }
```

Dense or allocation-lazy paged storage policy for datasource cells.

Members:
- `cacheBytes` — Per-sheet clean-chunk cache budget; defaults to 32 MiB. Sparse local edits are accounted separately; dirty and visible chunks may exceed it.
- `chunkRows` — Paged row chunk size; defaults to 4,096 and is normalized to a power of two.
- `dirtyCellLimit` — Maximum sparse local edits retained outside the clean page cache. Defaults to 1,000,000.
- `mode` — Storage engine. Dense is the default.

##### `DataValidationComparison` — type

```ts
export type DataValidationComparison = | { operator: "between" | "notBetween"; min: number; max: number } | { operator: | "equal" | "notEqual" | "greaterThan" | "lessThan" | "greaterThanOrEqual" | "lessThanOrEqual"; value: number; };
```

Native comparison semantics for numeric, date-serial, and text-length validation.
Interval operands are inclusive; `notBetween` accepts values outside that interval.

##### `DataValidationCondition` — type

```ts
export type DataValidationCondition = | { kind: "list"; values: readonly CellScalar[]; allowCustom?: boolean } | { kind: "number"; min?: number; max?: number; integer?: boolean; comparison?: DataValidationComparison; } | { kind: "date"; min?: number; max?: number; comparison?: DataValidationComparison } | { kind: "textLength"; min?: number; max?: number; comparison?: DataValidationComparison } | { kind: "checkbox"; checkedValue?: CellScalar; uncheckedValue?: CellScalar; };
```

Serializable condition enforced by a data-validation rule.

`min` and `max` remain inclusive legacy bounds. Use `comparison` when the
operator itself is significant; comparison and legacy bounds are mutually exclusive.

##### `DataValidationRule` — interface

```ts
export interface DataValidationRule { id: string; range: Range; condition: DataValidationCondition; policy: ValidationPolicy; allowBlank?: boolean; helpText?: string; }
```

One stable, range-scoped data-entry rule. Blank cells are allowed unless disabled.

##### `dateToSerial` — function

```ts
(date: Date): number
```

Convert a real UTC `Date` to the Excel 1900-system serial. It is the inverse
of {@link serialToDate} except for synthetic serial 60, which JavaScript
cannot represent as a Date. Construct calendar dates with `Date.UTC(...)`
(or via {@link parseDateInput}) to avoid host-timezone shifts.

##### `decodeStoreMemoryStats` — function

```ts
(encoded: ArrayLike<number>, wasmCommittedBytes: number | null): StoreMemoryBreakdown
```

Decode the flat Rust protocol and fail closed on version/order/total drift.

##### `DEFAULT_DELIMITED_TEXT_RESOURCE_LIMITS` — variable

```ts
Readonly<DelimitedTextResourceLimits>
```

Synchronous operations return one in-memory string, so byte/cell ceilings
bound allocation while sheet-compatible dimensions remain independently valid.

##### `DEFAULT_MAX_CHANGE` — variable

```ts
0.001
```

Excel's convergence threshold for a new workbook.

##### `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` — variable

```ts
100
```

Excel's iteration count for a new workbook.

##### `DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_RESOURCE_LIMITS` — variable

```ts
Readonly<SnapshotResourceLimits>
```

Conservative defaults that retain the million-row paged-sheet contract.

##### `DEFAULT_SYNC_COORDINATOR_LIMITS` — variable

```ts
Readonly<SyncCoordinatorLimits>
```

Security and durability defaults bound hostile remote versions, recovery
buffers, acknowledgement memory, and the offline pending queue independently.

##### `DEFAULT_THEME` — variable

```ts
Theme
```

Default canvas theme used before CSS and explicit theme overrides.

##### `DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_RESOURCE_LIMITS` — variable

```ts
Readonly<TransactionResourceLimits>
```

Inclusive defaults for every atomic document transaction accepted by a
Store or Grid. The count bounds object-heavy validation and dispatch; the
exact UTF-8 JSON size bounds hostile or accidentally oversized payloads.

##### `DEFAULT_WORKBOOK_TABLE_RESOURCE_LIMITS` — variable

```ts
Readonly<WorkbookTableResourceLimits>
```

Independent metadata ceilings enforced before table arrays cross the WASM boundary.

##### `DEFAULT_XLSX_RESOURCE_LIMITS` — variable

```ts
Readonly<XlsxResourceLimits>
```

Codec defaults combine SpreadsheetML worksheet dimensions with independent
ZIP/XML and aggregate-work ceilings for untrusted in-memory conversion.

##### `DelimitedTextOperation` — type

```ts
export type DelimitedTextOperation = "parse" | "import" | "encode" | "export";
```

Phase reported by a typed delimited-text resource failure.

##### `DelimitedTextOptions` — interface

```ts
export interface DelimitedTextOptions { resourceLimits?: Partial<DelimitedTextResourceLimits>; signal?: AbortSignal; }
```

Optional resource ceilings for an in-memory delimited-text operation.

Members:
- `resourceLimits` — Positive safe-integer overrides merged over `DEFAULT_DELIMITED_TEXT_RESOURCE_LIMITS`.
- `signal` — Abort between bounded encode chunks or store windows.

##### `DelimitedTextOptionsError` — class

```ts
class DelimitedTextOptionsError extends SheetwriteError { constructor(resource: keyof DelimitedTextResourceLimits, value: unknown); name: "DelimitedTextOptionsError"; resource: keyof DelimitedTextResourceLimits; value: unknown }
```

Stable invalid-option failure for a delimited-text resource ceiling.

##### `DelimitedTextResourceError` — class

```ts
class DelimitedTextResourceError extends SheetwriteError { constructor(resource: keyof DelimitedTextResourceLimits, limit: number, actual: number, operation: DelimitedTextOperation); actual: number; limit: number; name: "DelimitedTextResourceError"; resource: keyof DelimitedTextResourceLimits }
```

Stable resource-limit failure raised before the next oversized parse or encode allocation.

##### `DelimitedTextResourceLimits` — interface

```ts
export interface DelimitedTextResourceLimits { maxInputBytes: number; maxOutputBytes: number; maxRows: number; maxColumns: number; maxCells: number; maxFieldBytes: number; maxWriterWindowRows: number; }
```

Resource ceilings shared by synchronous CSV and TSV parsing and encoding.

Members:
- `maxCells` — Aggregate fields across all records; defaults to 1,000,000.
- `maxColumns` — Fields in any one record; defaults to 16,384.
- `maxFieldBytes` — Decoded UTF-8 bytes in one field; defaults to 1 MiB.
- `maxInputBytes` — Input string size in UTF-8 bytes; defaults to 32 MiB.
- `maxOutputBytes` — Output string size in UTF-8 bytes, including a BOM; defaults to 64 MiB.
- `maxRows` — Syntactically present records; defaults to 1,000,000.
- `maxWriterWindowRows` — Rows fetched by an export writer in one packed store read; defaults to 4,096.

##### `diffRuntimeResourcePhases` — function

```ts
(before: RuntimeResourceSnapshot, after: RuntimeResourceSnapshot): RuntimeResourcePhaseDelta
```

Diff two validated phases of the same operation by exclusive resource owner.

##### `DocumentOp` — type

```ts
export type DocumentOp = | { op: "set"; addr: CellAddress; value: CellValue; style?: CellStyle } | { op: "setRange"; range: Range; cells: SnapshotCell[] } | { op: "setBlock"; range: Range; block: PackedCellBlock } | { op: "restoreBlock"; range: Range; encoding: "deflate-json-v1"; decodedBytes: number; data: string; } | { op: "setRangeStyle"; range: Range; style: Partial<CellStyle> | null } | { op: "clearRange"; range: Range; contents?: boolean; style?: boolean } | { op: "addRows"; sheet: SheetId; at: number; count: number } | { op: "removeRows"; sheet: SheetId; at: number; count: number } | { op: "moveRows"; sheet: SheetId; from: number; count: number; to: number } | { op: "addColumns"; sheet: SheetId; at: number; columns: Column[] } | { op: "removeColumns"; sheet: SheetId; at: number; count: number } | { op: "moveColumns"; sheet: SheetId; from: number; count: number; to: number } | { op: "setColumn"; sheet: SheetId; col: number; patch: Partial<Column> } | { op: "setRowMeta"; sheet: SheetId; row: number; meta: RowMetadata | null } | { op: "addMerge"; sheet: SheetId; merge: MergeRange } | { op: "removeMerge"; sheet: SheetId; merge: MergeRange } | { op: "addSheet"; sheet: SheetSnapshot } | { op: "removeSheet"; sheet: SheetId } | { op: "renameSheet"; sheet: SheetId; name: string } | { op: "moveSheet"; sheet: SheetId; to: number } | { op: "setSheetVisibility"; sheet: SheetId; visibility: SheetVisibility } | { op: "addTable"; table: WorkbookTable } | { op: "updateTable"; sheet: SheetId; tableId: string; patch: WorkbookTablePatch } | { op: "removeTable"; sheet: SheetId; tableId: string } | { op: "setSheetMeta"; sheet: SheetId; patch: { frozenRows?: number; frozenCols?: number; conditionalFormats?: ConditionalFormatRule[]; rowGroups?: RowGroup[]; sortKeys?: SortKey[]; filters?: Array<[col: number, filter: ColumnFilter]>; }; } | { op: "setValidationRule"; sheet: SheetId; rule: DataValidationRule } | { op: "removeValidationRule"; sheet: SheetId; id: string } | { op: "setHyperlink"; sheet: SheetId; hyperlink: CellHyperlink } | { op: "removeHyperlink"; sheet: SheetId; id: string } | { op: "setProtectedRange"; sheet: SheetId; protectedRange: ProtectedRange } | { op: "removeProtectedRange"; sheet: SheetId; id: string } | { op: "setNote"; addr: CellAddress; text: string | null } | { op: "setNamedRange"; namedRange: NamedRangeSnapshot } | { op: "removeNamedRange"; name: string; scope?: SheetId } | { op: "setCalculation"; calculation: CalculationSettings } | { op: "setChart"; sheet: SheetId; chart: ChartDefinition } | { op: "removeChart"; sheet: SheetId; id: string } | { op: "setPivot"; sheet: SheetId; pivot: PivotDefinition } | { op: "removePivot"; sheet: SheetId; id: string };
```

Exhaustive serializable operation union for workbook mutations.

##### `documentOpTarget` — function

```ts
(operation: DocumentOp): string
```

Exhaustive stable target identity used by persistence/logging layers.

##### `DocumentRebaseResult` — type

```ts
export type DocumentRebaseResult = | { status: "rebased"; operations: readonly DocumentOp[] } | { status: "conflict"; conflict: RebaseConflict };
```

Successful rebased operations or a conservative rebase conflict.

##### `DocumentValidationError` — interface

```ts
export interface DocumentValidationError { path: string; code: | "unsupported-schema" | "invalid-value" | "duplicate-id" | "missing-reference" | "out-of-bounds" | "overlapping-merge" | "non-serializable" | "resource-limit"; message: string; }
```

Path-qualified validation failure for a document operation.
