Success or structured errors returned by document validation.

##### `downloadBytes` — function

```ts
(bytes: Uint8Array | string, filename: string, mime: string): void
```

Trigger a browser download from in-memory bytes. The temporary anchor is
removed and its object URL is scheduled for revocation even when DOM append or
click throws.

##### `emptyStoreMemoryStats` — function

```ts
(wasmCommittedBytes: number | null): StoreMemoryBreakdown
```

Construct a zero-owner store report when no WASM store is available.

##### `EngineMemoryReleaseReport` — interface

```ts
export interface EngineMemoryReleaseReport { readonly stores: number; readonly wasmBytesBefore: number; readonly wasmBytesAfter: number; readonly pauseMs: number; }
```

Result of an explicit, all-store engine memory release.

Members:
- `pauseMs` — Main-thread migration pause, excluding the wait for active work.
- `stores` — Stores migrated together; disposed stores are excluded.
- `wasmBytesAfter` — Committed linear memory of its replacement, including migration scratch.
- `wasmBytesBefore` — Committed linear memory of the retired engine.

##### `formatNumber` — function

```ts
(value: number | string, format?: string, locale?: string): string
```

Deterministic Excel-style number/date formatter. Supports explicit locale
separators, percent/scientific notation, UTC date/time tokens, four-section
positive/negative/zero/text codes, quoted literals, and backslash escapes.
`General` formats exactly like an omitted code.

##### `fromCsv` — function

```ts
(text: string, columns: readonly Column[], options?: DelimitedTextOptions): ColumnarData
```

Parse CSV into `ColumnarData`. The first record is consumed as a positional
header. Input fields project onto declared visible columns; hidden declared
columns are initialized to `null`, matching the visible-column CSV export.
Extra fields are ignored and missing fields become `null`. The returned
columnar table is fully materialized in memory.

##### `fromXlsxTable` — function

```ts
(data: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array, options?: XlsxWorkbookOptions): Promise<ColumnarData>
```

Parse the first sheet of `.xlsx` bytes into `ColumnarData`. The first parsed
row is treated as the header and its cell text becomes each column's key.
Numbers stay numbers, date cells use the date-serial convention, strings are
verbatim, and empty cells become `null`.
@example
```ts
import { registerXlsxBackends } from "@sheetwrite/xlsx";
import { fromXlsxTable } from "@sheetwrite/core";

registerXlsxBackends();
async function openTable(file: File) {
 return fromXlsxTable(await file.arrayBuffer());
}
```
@see
toXlsxTable

##### `fromXlsxWorkbook` — function

```ts
(data: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array, options?: XlsxWorkbookOptions): Promise<WorkbookSnapshot>
```

Formula-preserving, multi-sheet workbook import through the optional XLSX backend.
@example
```ts
import { registerXlsxBackends } from "@sheetwrite/xlsx";
import { fromXlsxWorkbook, createGridFromSnapshot, initSheetwrite } from "@sheetwrite/core";

registerXlsxBackends();
async function openWorkbook(host: HTMLElement, file: File) {
 await initSheetwrite();
 const snapshot = await fromXlsxWorkbook(await file.arrayBuffer());
 return createGridFromSnapshot(host, snapshot);
}
```
@see
toXlsxWorkbook

##### `fromXlsxWorkbookFile` — function

```ts
(file: Blob, options?: XlsxWorkbookOptions): Promise<WorkbookSnapshot>
```

Import a seekable File/Blob without first buffering the compressed workbook.

##### `Grid` — interface

```ts
export interface Grid { readonly store: Store; readonly actions: GridActions; getRuntimeResourceSnapshot( operation: RuntimeResourceOperation, phase: RuntimeResourcePhase, runtime?: RuntimeMemoryObservation, ): RuntimeResourceSnapshot; getCommandState(command: GridCommandName): GridCommandState; getFocusCellStyle(): CellStyle; summarizeSelection(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SelectionSummary | null>; setActiveSheet(id: SheetId): void; scrollToCell(addr: CellAddress): void; getCellAtPoint(clientX: number, clientY: number): CellAddress | null; getActiveSheet(): SheetId; getCellInput(row: number, col: number): CellInputSnapshot | null; getSelection(): Selection | null; setSelection(sel: Selection | null): void; getTheme(): Theme; getShortcutLabel(action: KeyboardAction): string; setTheme(theme: Partial<Theme>): void; replaceTheme(theme: Partial<Theme> | undefined): void; getEffectiveTheme(): Theme; setReadOnly(readOnly: boolean): void; setConfig(config: GridConfig | undefined): void; applyTransaction(transaction: GridTransaction): ApplyTransactionResult; exportSnapshot(): WorkbookSnapshot; applyRemoteOperations( operations: readonly DocumentOp[], options?: RemoteOperationOptions, ): ApplyTransactionResult; defineCellRenderer(name: string, renderer: CellRenderer): void; aggregate(col: number, op: AggregateOp): number; sortBy(col: number, ascending?: boolean): void; sortByMulti(keys: readonly SortKey[]): void; filterBy(col: number, needle: string): void; setColumnFilter(col: number, filter: ColumnFilter | null): void; setSort(keys: readonly SortKey[]): ApplyTransactionResult; getColumnFilters(): ReadonlyMap<number, ColumnFilter>; distinctValues(col: number, limit?: number): CellScalar[]; hideRows(rows: readonly number[]): void; showRows(rows?: readonly number[]): void; hiddenRows(): readonly number[]; hideColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void; showColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void; hiddenColumns(): readonly number[]; groupRows(start: number, end: number): void; ungroupRows(start: number, end: number): void; setGroupCollapsed(start: number, collapsed: boolean): void; rowGroups(): readonly RowGroup[]; clearView(): void; undo(): void; redo(): void; exportCsv(filename: string): void; exportXlsx(filename: string): Promise<void>; search(query: string, opts?: SearchOptions): SearchResult; findNext(): SearchResult; findPrev(): SearchResult; clearSearch(): void; replaceCurrent(replacement: string): SearchResult; replaceAll(replacement: string): ReplaceResult; insertRows(at: number, count?: number): void; removeRows(at: number, count?: number): void; insertColumns(at: number, count?: number): void; removeColumns(at: number, count?: number): void; addSheet(input: AddSheetInput): SheetLifecycleResult; removeSheet(id: SheetId): SheetLifecycleResult; renameSheet(id: SheetId, name: string): SheetLifecycleResult; moveSheet(id: SheetId, toIndex: number): SheetLifecycleResult; setSheetVisibility(id: SheetId, visibility: SheetVisibility): SheetLifecycleResult; setConditionalFormats(rules: readonly ConditionalFormatRule[]): void; setHyperlink(hyperlink: CellHyperlink): ApplyTransactionResult; removeHyperlink(id: string): ApplyTransactionResult; getHyperlink(addr: CellAddress): CellHyperlink | null; activateHyperlink(addr: CellAddress): boolean; setValidationRule(rule: DataValidationRule): ApplyTransactionResult; removeValidationRule(id: string): ApplyTransactionResult; setProtectedRange(protectedRange: ProtectedRange): ApplyTransactionResult; removeProtectedRange(id: string): ApplyTransactionResult; getPivots(sheet?: SheetId): PivotDefinition[]; setPivot(pivot: PivotDefinition, sheet?: SheetId): ApplyTransactionResult; removePivot(id: string, sheet?: SheetId): ApplyTransactionResult; getPivotFields(sheet: SheetId, id: string): PivotSourceField[]; getPivotResult(sheet: SheetId, id: string): PivotResultView | null; getCharts(sheet?: SheetId): readonly ChartDefinition[]; setChart(chart: ChartDefinition, sheet?: SheetId): ApplyTransactionResult; removeChart(id: string, sheet?: SheetId): ApplyTransactionResult; selectChart(id: string | null, sheet?: SheetId): void; openPanel(panel: GridPanel | null): void; setProtectionResolver(resolver: ProtectionResolver | undefined, mode?: MutationPolicyMode): void; setNote(addr: CellAddress, text: string | null): ApplyTransactionResult; getNote(addr: CellAddress): string | null; setOverscan(overscan?: number): void; setMinColumns(minColumns?: number): void; highlightCells(ranges: readonly HighlightRange[] | null, color?: string): void; setPresenceOverlays(overlays: readonly PresenceOverlay[] | null): void; styleRange(range: Range, style: Partial<CellStyle> | null): void; beginEdit(row: number, col: number, initial?: string, selectAll?: boolean): void; dataEdge(row: number, col: number, dRow: number, dCol: number): number | null; setRowHeight(row: number, height: number): void; setColumnWidth(col: number, width: number): void; autoFitRows(range?: Range): void; autoFitColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void; setFrozen(rows: number, cols?: number): void; setZoom(zoom: number): void; getZoom(): number; rendererKind(): "canvas" | "worker"; on<E extends keyof GridEvents>(evt: E, fn: (e: GridEvents[E]) => void): () => void; refresh(): void; destroy(): void; }
```

Imperative grid handle for document commands, events, rendering, and teardown.
@example
```ts
import type { Grid } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function updateTotal(grid: Grid) {
 const sheet = grid.getActiveSheet();
 const result = grid.applyTransaction({
 patches: [{ op: "set", addr: { sheet, row: 0, col: 0 }, value: { kind: "literal", value: 42 } }],
 });
 if (result.status === "applied") grid.scrollToCell({ sheet, row: 0, col: 0 });
 return grid.aggregate(0, "sum");
}
```
@see
createGrid
@see
Grid.applyTransaction

Members:
- `actions` — Imperative action surface for binding custom toolbars/menus.
- `activateHyperlink` — Validate and emit a host-owned activation event. External targets are never
opened by Sheetwrite; internal navigation occurs only under the explicit policy.
- `addSheet` — Add a sheet with a stable ID and return its actionable transaction outcome.
- `aggregate` — Column aggregate over the active sheet's data.
@example
```ts
import type { Grid } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function total(grid: Grid) {
 return grid.aggregate(1, "sum");
}
```
@see
SheetwriteStore.aggregate
- `applyRemoteOperations` — Apply host-supplied operations without undo history or outgoing dirty state.
The resulting change event has `source: "remote"`.
- `applyTransaction` — Apply arbitrary patches as one undoable Grid commit. No-op when read-only.
Use `Store.applyTransaction` only for low-level writes that intentionally
bypass Grid history and policy.
@example
```ts
import type { Grid } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function setFirstCell(grid: Grid) {
 return grid.applyTransaction({ patches: [
 { op: "set", addr: { sheet: grid.getActiveSheet(), row: 0, col: 0 },
 value: { kind: "literal", value: 42 } },
 ] });
}
```
@see
Transaction
- `autoFitColumns` — Explicitly resize columns from a bulk worksheet read.
- `autoFitRows` — Explicitly resize rows to fit wrapped content; never runs during paint.
- `beginEdit` — Open the cell editor at a view cell, optionally seeding text / selecting all.
- `clearSearch` — Clear the current search and its highlights.
- `clearView` — Clear any active sort/filter view.
- `dataEdge` — Ctrl+Arrow-style jump target: the data-run edge from (row, col) on the
moved axis (row for vertical moves, col for horizontal), or null when the
store is not columnar. Under an active sort/filter view, `row` is a view
position and vertical moves return view positions. For hosts building
their own keymaps (`config.keyboard`).
- `distinctValues` — Distinct resolved values of a column in first-seen order. Defaults to
1,000 values for bounded filter menus; pass 0 to request an uncapped scan.
- `exportCsv` — Download the active sheet as CSV.
@example
```ts
import type { Grid } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function downloadCsv(grid: Grid) {
 grid.exportCsv("sales.csv");
}
```
- `exportSnapshot` — Deterministically export the complete authoritative workbook document.
- `exportXlsx` — Download the active sheet through the registered XLSX backend.
@example
```ts
import type { Grid } from "@sheetwrite/core";
import { registerXlsxBackends } from "@sheetwrite/xlsx";

async function downloadXlsx(grid: Grid) {
 await registerXlsxBackends();
 await grid.exportXlsx("sales.xlsx");
}
```
@see
toXlsxWorkbook
- `filterBy` — Filter the displayed rows to those whose column text contains `needle`.
@example
```ts
import type { Grid } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function showOpenRows(grid: Grid) {
 grid.filterBy(0, "Open");
}
```
@see
Grid.clearView
- `findNext` — Move the active match to the next match and scroll it into view.
- `findPrev` — Move the active match to the previous match and scroll it into view.
- `getActiveSheet` — Id of the currently visible sheet.
- `getCellAtPoint` — Resolve browser viewport coordinates to an active-sheet cell for host-owned
menus and interactions. Returns null outside the cell body.
- `getCellInput` — Editable snapshot of the cell at a view position on the active sheet, or
null when out of bounds. See {@link CellInputSnapshot}.
- `getCharts` — Clones of the chart definitions on `sheet` (default: the active sheet).
- `getColumnFilters` — Active column filters on the active sheet, keyed by column index.
- `getCommandState` — Query undo/redo availability and formatting active/mixed/disabled state.
- `getEffectiveTheme` — The effective (post-zoom) theme the renderer is currently painting with.
- `getFocusCellStyle` — Effective style of the focus cell: its own style over its column's
`cellStyle`. Empty when nothing is selected.
- `getPivotFields` — Source fields for the field list; empty on the default engine.
- `getPivotResult` — Plain-JSON output of one pivot. The default engine reports the saved
output (`saved`), or `unavailable` without one. Null when `sheet` holds
no pivot with `id`.
- `getPivots` — Clones of the pivot definitions on `sheet`, or on every sheet; no engine is needed.
- `getRuntimeResourceSnapshot` — Versioned coarse runtime ownership snapshot, including datasource state.
- `getShortcutLabel` — Platform-aware label for a bound action, or an empty string when disabled.
- `getTheme` — Resolved base theme, before zoom scaling. The returned object is a copy.
- `groupRows` — Define a collapsible row group over a data-row range (end-inclusive).
- `hiddenColumns` — Currently hidden columns on the active sheet.
- `hiddenRows` — Currently hidden data rows on the active sheet.
- `hideColumns` — Hide columns through one bulk-safe metadata transaction.
- `hideRows` — Hide the given data rows (composes with filters/sort).
- `highlightCells` — Draw temporary highlights outside document history. Pass `null` to clear all
highlights: `grid.highlightCells(null)`. Per-range `color` wins over the call color.
Undo does not clear highlights; use `styleRange` for persistent cell fills.
- `openPanel` — Show `panel` on the grid's right edge and shrink the cells to make room;
`null` closes the open panel. One panel shows at a time: opening a panel
closes the previous one. Escape and the close button close it and return
focus to the grid.
- `redo` — Redo the last undone cell edit.
- `removeChart` — Remove a chart from `sheet` (default: the first sheet that holds it) as one undo entry.
- `removePivot` — Remove a pivot from `sheet` (default: the sheet that holds it) as one undo entry.
- `removeSheet` — Remove a sheet while preserving at least one visible worksheet.
- `rendererKind` — Which renderer is actually active: `"worker"` when the OffscreenCanvas
worker constructed successfully, `"canvas"` otherwise (including after a
`renderer-fallback`).
- `replaceAll` — Replace every current match in a single undoable transaction (one
`undo()` restores them all), then re-scan. Formula/ref cells are skipped
and not counted. No-op when read-only.
- `replaceCurrent` — Replace the active match with `replacement`, then advance to the next match
(re-scanning against the new data). Only literal text/number cells are
eligible; formula and ref cells are skipped (formula source is never
rewritten). Honors the active {@link SearchOptions} (matchCase; `wholeCell`
swaps the entire cell). The write flows through the grid's commit path as
one undoable step. No-op when read-only or when there is no active match.
- `replaceTheme` — Option-level replacement: re-run construction-time resolution
(`DEFAULT_THEME < CSS custom properties < theme`) with the new partial.
`undefined` restores the CSS-variable/default resolution. Adapters call
this for their declarative `theme` prop; imperative patching stays on
{@link setTheme}.
- `rowGroups` — Row groups on the active sheet.
- `search` — Find cells matching `query`; highlights matches, emits `search`, returns the result.
- `selectChart` — Select the chart object `id` on `sheet` (default: the active sheet), or
deselect with `null`. Selecting a chart on another sheet activates that
sheet first. Emits `chart-select`.
- `setChart` — Insert or replace the chart with `chart.id` as one undo entry. `sheet`
defaults to the active sheet; chart IDs are unique only within a sheet.
- `setColumnFilter` — Set or clear (null) one column's filter. All column filters AND together
and compose with the active sort and hidden rows.
- `setColumnWidth` — Set one column's width via an undoable `setColumn` patch.
- `setConfig` — Reconfigure built-in chrome and keyboard handling without replacing the
Grid or clearing selection/history. Construction-bound GridOptions are not
accepted here.
- `setFrozen` — Pin the first `rows` view rows and `cols` columns; they stay visible while
the body scrolls (0 = unfreeze that axis). Persisted on the active sheet.
- `setGroupCollapsed` — Collapse/expand a row group; collapsing hides its rows.
- `setMinColumns` — Live-update the minimum rendered column count. Increasing the minimum
silently extends presentation padding; `undefined` restores the default.
- `setOverscan` — Live-update the render window overscan (row/column positions painted past
each edge); `undefined` restores the default of 6.
- `setPivot` — Insert or replace a pivot as one undo entry. `sheet` defaults to the sheet
that holds the pivot's ID, then to the active sheet. The pivot's
`savedOutput` is removed, because it does not match a changed definition.
- `setPresenceOverlays` — Replace ephemeral remote-presence overlays; null clears every collaborator.
- `setReadOnly` — Update editability without replacing the Grid or clearing session state.
- `setRowHeight` — Set one row's persistent display height through document history.
- `setSheetVisibility` — Set host-visible worksheet state; stock UI never offers `veryHidden`.
- `setSort` — Persisted multi-key sort of the active sheet.
- `setTheme` — Imperative patch: merge `theme` into the accumulated base theme.
- `setZoom` — Content zoom factor (0.5–2): scales row/column geometry and fonts.
- `showColumns` — Show columns through one bulk-safe metadata transaction.
- `showRows` — Show the given data rows again, or every hidden row when omitted.
- `sortBy` — Sort the displayed rows by a column (does not mutate stored data).
@example
```ts
import type { Grid } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function showLargestFirst(grid: Grid) {
 grid.sortBy(1, false);
}
```
@see
Grid.clearView
- `sortByMulti` — Multi-key sort of the displayed rows (first key primary; stable).
- `styleRange` — Merge `style` into every cell of `range` (null clears cell styles) as one
undoable transaction. Styles land in the store and paint in the canvas —
unlike {@link highlightCells}, which draws a translucent overlay above it.
- `summarizeSelection` — Totals for the current selection, for a status bar. Large selections are
read in chunks between frames, so the page stays responsive; abort
`signal` to stop early, which rejects with the signal's reason. Resolves
null when nothing is selected.
- `undo` — Undo the last recorded cell edit. If the restored data is above the
transaction resource limits, nothing changes: the Grid emits
`mutation-rejected` and removes that entry, so older edits stay undoable.
@example
```ts
import type { Grid } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function undoAndRestore(grid: Grid) {
 grid.undo();
 grid.redo();
}
```
@see
Grid.redo
- `ungroupRows` — Remove a row group (rows become visible if the group was collapsed).

##### `GridActions` — interface

```ts
export interface GridActions { toggleBold(): void; toggleItalic(): void; toggleUnderline(): void; toggleStrikethrough(): void; setAlign(align: CellAlign): void; setTextColor(color: string | null): void; setFillColor(color: string | null): void; toggleBorder(): void; setBorders(preset: BorderPreset): void; setFontFamily(family: string | null): void; setFontSize(size: number | null): void; stepFontSize(direction: 1 | -1): void; setVerticalAlign(align: CellVerticalAlign): void; toggleWrap(): void; setNumberFormat(code: string | null): void; stepDecimals(direction: 1 | -1): void; mergeAndCenter(): void; clearAll(): void; autoSum(): void; find(): void; freezePanes(): void; clearFormat(): void; merge(): void; unmerge(): void; sort(ascending: boolean): void; insertRowAbove(): void; insertRowBelow(): void; deleteRow(): void; insertColumnLeft(): void; insertColumnRight(): void; deleteColumn(): void; hideRows(rows?: readonly number[]): void; showRows(rows?: readonly number[]): void; autoFitRows(): void; hideColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void; showColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void; autoFitColumns(cols?: readonly number[]): void; clearFilter(col?: number): void; copy(): Promise<ClipboardOutcome>; cut(): Promise<ClipboardOutcome>; paste(): Promise<ClipboardOutcome>; pasteValues(): Promise<ClipboardOutcome>; clearContents(): void; exportCsv(filename?: string): void; exportXlsx(filename?: string): Promise<void>; editNote(): void; deleteNote(): void; showPivotFields(): void; undo(): void; redo(): void; }
```

Imperative operations the toolbar and context menu bind to; also exposed as `Grid.actions`.

Members:
- `autoSum` — Put `=SUM(...)` in the focus cell over the contiguous numbers directly
above it, or to its left when there are none above.
- `clearAll` — Clear the selection's contents and formatting, as one undoable step.
- `copy` — Copy the focused rectangle to the system clipboard. Never rejects.
- `cut` — Copy + clear the source (after the clipboard accepted). Never rejects.
- `deleteNote` — Remove the focus cell's note as one undoable step. Does nothing when it has
none. Does nothing on a read-only grid.
- `editNote` — Open the note editor on the focus cell, with its note or empty for a new
one. Ctrl or Cmd+Enter and leaving the editor save; Escape cancels. Does
nothing on a read-only grid.
- `exportCsv` — Download the active sheet as CSV. Never throws; a failure emits `export-error`.
- `exportXlsx` — Download the active sheet as XLSX. Resolves when the download starts and never
rejects; a failure emits `export-error`.
- `find` — Open the built-in find bar when it is enabled.
- `freezePanes` — Freeze rows above and columns left of the focus cell in view coordinates.
Does nothing without a selection; focusing A1 unfreezes both axes.
- `mergeAndCenter` — Merge the selection and center its text, as one undoable step.
- `paste` — Paste at the focus cell. Never rejects.
- `pasteValues` — Paste keeping only resolved values — no formulas, no styles (Ctrl+Shift+V). Never rejects.
- `setBorders` — Apply an Excel border preset to the selection. Edge presets (`top`,
`bottom`, `left`, `right`, `outside`, `thickOutside`) touch only the
selection's outer cells and keep each cell's other sides.
- `setFillColor` — Set the selection's fill; null removes it (Excel's "No Fill").
- `setFontFamily` — Set the selection's font family; null returns it to the column/theme font.
- `setFontSize` — Set the selection's font size in CSS pixels; null returns it to the default.
- `setNumberFormat` — Set the selection's number format; null returns it to the column's format.
- `setTextColor` — Set the selection's text color; null returns it to automatic (the theme color).
- `showPivotFields` — Open the field list of the pivot table whose output holds the focus cell.
Does nothing when the focus cell is outside every pivot. Does nothing on a
read-only grid.
- `stepDecimals` — Show one more (1) or one fewer (-1) decimal place than the focus cell does.
- `stepFontSize` — Step the focus cell's font size to the next larger (1) or smaller (-1) standard size.

##### `GridCommandName` — type

```ts
export type GridCommandName = Exclude<ToolbarActionName, "separator">;
```

Built-in command names accepted by state queries and change events.

##### `GridCommandState` — interface

```ts
export interface GridCommandState { readonly disabled: boolean; readonly activity: "inactive" | "active" | "mixed"; }
```

Observable availability and selection-derived activity for one command.

##### `GridCommandStateChangeEvent` — interface

```ts
export interface GridCommandStateChangeEvent { readonly states: Readonly<Record<GridCommandName, GridCommandState>>; }
```

Complete command-state snapshot emitted whenever availability or activity can change.

##### `GridConfig` — interface

```ts
export interface GridConfig { toolbar?: boolean | ToolbarItem[]; bold?: boolean; italic?: boolean; align?: boolean; textColor?: boolean; fillColor?: boolean; border?: boolean; clearFormat?: boolean; merge?: boolean; sort?: boolean; export?: boolean; ribbon?: boolean; icons?: IconOverrides; contextMenu?: boolean | ContextMenuItems; undo?: boolean; find?: boolean; tabs?: boolean; keyboard?: boolean | KeyboardOptions | ((e: KeyboardEvent, grid: Grid) => boolean); }
```

Toolbar / feature configuration. When `config` is set the built-in toolbar is
shown; control flags default to `true` except the opt-in `export` flag.
@example
```ts
import type { GridConfig } from "@sheetwrite/core";

const config: GridConfig = {
 toolbar: true,
 contextMenu: [{ action: "copy" }, { action: "paste" }],
 keyboard(event, grid) {
 if (event.altKey && event.key === "b") {
 grid.actions.toggleBold();
 return true;
 }
 return false;
 },
};
```
@see
Grid.setConfig
@see
ContextMenuItem

Members:
- `align` — Show left, center, and right alignment controls (default true).
- `bold` — Show the bold control in the default toolbar (default true).
- `border` — Show the border control in the default toolbar (default true).
- `clearFormat` — Show the clear-format control in the default toolbar (default true).
- `contextMenu` — Built-in menu, disabled menu, static rows, or a request-aware row factory.
- `export` — Show CSV/XLSX export controls in the default toolbar (default false).
- `fillColor` — Show the fill-color control in the default toolbar (default true).
- `find` — Built-in Ctrl+F find widget: enabled (true, default) or disabled (false).
- `icons` — Replace built-in command icons by glyph name, in the toolbar, ribbon, ribbon menus and context menu. See {@link IconOverrides}.
- `italic` — Show the italic control in the default toolbar (default true).
- `keyboard` — Built-in keyboard handling. `true` (default) keeps the stock Sheets-style
bindings. An object replaces individual action bindings; omitted actions
keep their defaults, and `null` disables an action's keys.
For example: `{ bindings: { copy: { key: "c", mod: true, shift: true } } }`.
Menu hints and toolbar titles use these same bindings. `false` disables
all built-in keys. A function intercepts each keydown before the defaults;
return true to consume it, false to let the built-in handler continue.
- `merge` — Show merge and unmerge controls in the default toolbar (default true).
- `ribbon` — Replace the built-in toolbar with an Excel-style ribbon (Home, Insert,
Data and View tabs) that narrows its groups as the grid gets narrower.
A custom `toolbar` item list still renders the flat toolbar instead.
- `sort` — Show ascending and descending sort controls in the default toolbar (default true).
- `tabs` — Bottom sheet-tab bar for multi-sheet workbooks (default true).
- `textColor` — Show the text-color control in the default toolbar (default true).
- `toolbar` — Show the built-in toolbar (true), hide it (false), or supply a custom item list.
- `undo` — Show undo/redo controls in the built-in toolbar (default true).

##### `GridEvents` — interface

```ts
export interface GridEvents { change: ChangeEvent; selection: { selection: Selection | null }; scroll: { scrollTop: number; firstRow: number; lastRow: number; scrollLeft: number; firstVisibleColumn: number | null; lastVisibleColumn: number | null; }; "edit-begin": { addr: CellAddress }; "edit-commit": { addr: CellAddress; value: CellValue }; search: SearchResult; "command-state-change": GridCommandStateChangeEvent; "mutation-rejected": { issues: MutationIssue[] }; "active-sheet": { sheet: SheetId }; "hyperlink-activate": HyperlinkActivationEvent; "theme-change": { theme: Theme }; "renderer-fallback": { requested: "worker"; error: SheetwriteError }; "datasource-error": { request: Omit<DataSourceRequest, "signal">; error: SheetwriteError; }; "export-error": { format: "csv" | "xlsx"; error: SheetwriteError }; "chart-select": ChartRef | null; "chart-activate": ChartRef; }
```

Payload map for events emitted by a Grid.

Members:
- `active-sheet` — Emitted after the visible sheet changes (direct call or cross-sheet scroll).
- `chart-activate` — The user pressed Enter on a selected chart, for example to open its editor.
- `chart-select` — A chart object on the active sheet was selected; `null` when no object is selected.
- `command-state-change` — Command availability or formatting activity changed.
- `export-error` — Built-in toolbar/context-menu export failed after its action was dispatched.
- `renderer-fallback` — Emitted once when the worker renderer could not be constructed and the
grid fell back to the main-thread canvas renderer.
- `theme-change` — Emitted after `setTheme` or `replaceTheme` changes the base theme. Holds a copy.

##### `GridOptions` — interface

```ts
export interface GridOptions { workbook: Workbook; data?: ColumnarData; datasource?: DataSource; datasourceStorage?: DataSourceStorageOptions; renderer?: "canvas" | "worker"; workerUrl?: string | URL; presentation?: GridPresentation; theme?: Partial<Theme>; readOnly?: boolean; hyperlinkActivation?: "event-only" | "internal-navigation" | "disabled"; protectionResolver?: ProtectionResolver; mutationPolicy?: MutationPolicyMode; transactionResourceLimits?: Partial<TransactionResourceLimits>; renderers?: Record<string, CellRenderer>; editors?: Record<string, CellEditor>; overscan?: number; minColumns?: number; config?: GridConfig; }
```

Workbook, data, rendering, policy, and built-in UI options used to create a Grid.
@example
```ts
import type { GridOptions } from "@sheetwrite/core";

const options: GridOptions = {
 workbook: { activeSheet: "sheet1", sheets: [
 { id: "sheet1", name: "Sheet 1", rowCount: 1,
 columns: [{ key: "name", header: "Name", type: "text", width: 120 }] },
 ] },
 data: { rowCount: 1, columns: { name: ["Ada"] } },
 config: { toolbar: true, contextMenu: true, keyboard: true },
};
```
@see
createGrid
@see
GridConfig

Members:
- `config` — Built-in UI controls; providing an object enables the toolbar unless `toolbar` is false.
- `data` — Eager column-major values loaded into `workbook.activeSheet`; use instead of `datasource`.
- `datasource` — Lazy row provider requested for visible windows; use instead of eager `data`.
- `datasourceStorage` — Allocation and cache policy for datasource-backed cell storage.
- `editors` — Named custom editors resolved from each column's `editor` field.
- `hyperlinkActivation` — Hyperlink activation never opens a browser URL. `event-only` (default)
emits a safe resolved target; `internal-navigation` additionally moves to
stable internal destinations; `disabled` rejects every activation request.
- `minColumns` — Render at least this many columns, adding empty columns past the data. A
spreadsheet also adds empty columns to fill the host width; a data grid
adds them only through this option.
- `mutationPolicy` — Atomic rejects the transaction; partial skips denied operation objects.
- `overscan` — Extra row and visible-column positions painted on each viewport edge.
Defaults to 6; use 0 to disable the buffer.
- `presentation` — Header presentation. Spreadsheet mode (default) paints positional A/B/C
labels; data-grid mode paints each column's semantic `header`. Cell
addressing, row indices, clipboard values, formulas, and exports are
unchanged in both modes.
- `protectionResolver` — Host-owned client UX permission check. Servers must independently authorize
every submitted operation; this resolver is not an authentication boundary.
- `readOnly` — Disables mutating interactions while preserving navigation and selection.
- `renderer` — Paint backend; defaults to main-thread `canvas` and falls back there if a worker fails.
- `renderers` — Custom cell renderers registered up front; also see `Grid.defineCellRenderer`.
- `theme` — Overrides merged over the default theme and host CSS custom properties.
- `transactionResourceLimits` — Overrides inclusive operation-count and encoded-byte ceilings for every atomic mutation.
- `workbook` — Live workbook schema adopted by the store and updated by document operations.
- `workerUrl` — URL of the worker renderer module (`renderer: "worker"`), as served to the
BROWSER. Usually not needed: by default the grid creates its worker as
`new Worker(new URL("./worker.js", import.meta.url))`, which bundlers such
as Vite build together with the worker's imports. Pass a URL when there
is no bundler, or when yours copies the file instead of building it, for
example a copy of `@sheetwrite/core/dist/` in your public assets (see
`/docs/features/worker-rendering/`). A bare specifier like
`new URL("@sheetwrite/core/worker", import.meta.url)` is NOT reliable: the
platform `Worker` constructor does not consult package exports. If the
worker can't be constructed or fails to load, the grid falls back to the
main-thread canvas renderer and emits `renderer-fallback` once.

##### `GridPanel` — interface

```ts
export interface GridPanel { title: string; render(body: HTMLElement): () => void; focus?: boolean; }
```

One side panel that `Grid.openPanel` shows on the grid's right edge.

Members:
- `focus` — Move keyboard focus into the panel when it opens. Default `true`. Use
`false` for a panel that opens on cell selection, so arrow keys keep moving
the cell cursor.
- `render` — Fill `body`, then return a function that releases what `render` set up.
- `title` — Text in the panel header; it also names the panel for assistive technology.

##### `GridPresentation` — type

```ts
export type GridPresentation = "spreadsheet" | "data-grid";
```

Header semantics used by the retained canvas and accessibility mirror.

##### `GridTransaction` — interface

```ts
export interface GridTransaction { patches: DocumentOp[]; }
```

An undoable transaction submitted through a Grid.

Grid transactions deliberately have no epoch: optimistic reconciliation is
a low-level Store concern, while Grid commits are normal host-driven edits
that participate in read-only policy and undo/redo history.

##### `ICON_NAMES` — variable

```ts
readonly ["undo", "redo", "paste", "cut", "copy", "find", "zoomIn", "zoomOut", "autoSum", "clear", "bold", "italic", "underline", "strikethrough", "textColor", "fillColor", "fontGrow", "fontShrink", "clearFormat", "separator", "alignLeft", "alignCenter", "alignRight", "alignTop", "alignMiddle", "alignBottom", "wrap", "merge", "unmerge", "mergeAndCenter", "border", "borderAll", "borderOutside", "borderThickOutside", "borderTop", "borderBottom", "borderLeft", "borderRight", "borderNone", "currency", "percent", "comma", "decimalIncrease", "decimalDecrease", "hyperlink", "note", "exportCsv", "exportXlsx", "insert", "delete", "format", "hideRows", "unhideRows", "hideColumns", "unhideColumns", "freeze", "groupRows", "ungroupRows", "sortAsc", "sortDesc", "sortFilter", "clearFilter", "chart", "chartColumn", "chartBar", "chartLine", "chartArea", "chartPie", "chartDoughnut", "chartScatter", "pivotTable"]
```

##### `IconOverrides` — type

##### `KeyShortcut` — type

```ts
export type KeyShortcut = | `${"Mod" | "Ctrl" | "Meta" | "Alt" | "Shift"}+${string}` | { key: string; mod?: boolean; ctrl?: boolean; meta?: boolean; shift?: boolean; alt?: boolean; };
```

A compact modified key combination or a key object. Modifiers may appear in
any order before the final key, for example "Mod+Shift+K" or "Ctrl+Alt+Delete".
`Mod`/`mod` means Command on macOS and Control elsewhere; Ctrl and Meta are literal.
The parser rejects unknown/repeated modifiers and missing keys.

##### `MemoryPersistenceAdapter` — class

##### `parseCellInput` — function

```ts
(raw: string, type: CellFormat): CellValue
```

Coerce raw text input into a {@link CellValue}, following spreadsheet
input-bar conventions:

- blank (after trimming) clears the cell to a `null` literal;
- text longer than one character beginning with `=` becomes a formula;
- in a `number` column a finite numeric string becomes a number literal;
- in a `date` column a recognized date string ({@link parseDateInput}) becomes
 its serial-number literal;
- in a `currency` column a currency string ({@link parseCurrencyInput}) becomes
 a plain number literal;
- anything else is stored verbatim as a text literal (the untrimmed `raw`).

Shared by the grid's inline editor and any host-built formula bar, so input
parsing is identical everywhere instead of re-derived per consumer.

##### `parseCellLiteralInput` — function

```ts
(raw: string, type: CellFormat): CellScalar
```

Parse imported text as a literal using the same boolean, number, date, and
currency rules as {@link parseCellInput}. Unlike interactive entry, a leading
`=` remains inert text. Declared date columns also accept an existing finite
date serial so delimited export/import preserves numeric dates.

##### `parseCsv` — function

```ts
(text: string, options?: DelimitedTextOptions): string[][]
```

Parse the fixed comma dialect: quoted delimiters/newlines, doubled quotes,
bare CR, LF, or CRLF records, Unicode, trailing empty fields, and one optional
leading UTF-8 BOM. The synchronous API consumes an existing in-memory string
and returns an in-memory grid; it does not claim streaming. Scanning enforces
resource ceilings before materializing the next oversized field or record.

##### `parseCurrencyInput` — function

```ts
(raw: string): number | null
```

Parse a currency-formatted string into a plain number, or `null` when the
remaining text is not numeric. Strips currency symbols (`$ € £ ¥ ¤`), thousands
grouping (`,`), and whitespace, and reads accounting-style parentheses
(`(1,234.50)`) as a negative amount. Grouping/decimals follow the US locale the
renderer uses.

##### `parseDateInput` — function

```ts
(raw: string): number | null
```

Parse a user-typed date string into a serial, or `null` when it is not a date.
Accepted forms:

- ISO `yyyy-mm-dd` (e.g. `2026-07-06`);
- ISO date-time `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm` or `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss` (a `T` separator is
 also accepted); the fractional serial carries the time;
- slash `dd/mm/yyyy` and `mm/dd/yyyy`, disambiguated **conservatively**: if one
 component exceeds 12 it must be the day and the layout is unambiguous; when
 both are ≤ 12 the value is ambiguous (e.g. `04/05/2026`) and is read as
 **mm/dd** — Google Sheets' default (US) locale. Both > 12 is rejected.

Anything else (bare numbers, free text) returns `null` so callers can fall back
to a text literal.

##### `PendingCommit` — interface

```ts
export interface PendingCommit { documentId: string; baseVersion: number; clientMutationId: string; readonly operations: readonly DocumentOp[]; readonly versionOperationCounts?: readonly number[]; }
```

Immutable local operation batch awaiting a host acknowledgement.

Members:
- `versionOperationCounts` — Present only when the operations are too large for one server version.
Each entry is the operation count of one consecutive version of an atomic
batch, in order; the counts add up to `operations.length`. A server
applies and publishes all of these versions, or none of them.

##### `PendingCommitLoadOptions` — interface

```ts
export interface PendingCommitLoadOptions { signal?: AbortSignal; maxRecords: number; maxOperations: number; maxBytes: number; }
```

Mandatory bounds for one durable pending-commit restore.

Members:
- `maxBytes` — Maximum aggregate UTF-8 bytes of the JSON-encoded operation arrays.
- `maxOperations` — Maximum aggregate operation count returned for one document queue.
- `maxRecords` — Maximum records returned for one document queue.

##### `PendingCommitStorage` — interface

```ts
export interface PendingCommitStorage { load(documentId: string, options: PendingCommitLoadOptions): Promise<readonly PendingCommit[]>; put(commit: PendingCommit, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>; remove(documentId: string, clientMutationId: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>; replace( documentId: string, expectedClientMutationIds: readonly string[], commits: readonly PendingCommit[], signal?: AbortSignal, ): Promise<void>; }
```

Host-owned durable queue. Browser storage lives in the optional `./browser` entrypoint.

Members:
- `replace` — Atomically replaces one document queue only if its ordered IDs still match
the caller's expected view.

##### `PersistenceAdapter` — interface

```ts
export interface PersistenceAdapter { load(documentId: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<WorkbookSnapshot>; commit(request: PersistenceCommitRequest): Promise<PersistenceCommitResponse>; commitBatch?(request: PersistenceBatchCommitRequest): Promise<PersistenceCommitResponse>; }
```

Host load and commit contract for versioned workbook persistence.
@example
```ts
import { MemoryPersistenceAdapter, type PersistenceAdapter, type WorkbookSnapshot } from "@sheetwrite/core";

async function loadLocal(snapshot: WorkbookSnapshot) {
 if (!snapshot.documentId) throw new Error("A document ID is required");
 const adapter: PersistenceAdapter = new MemoryPersistenceAdapter(snapshot);
 return adapter.load(snapshot.documentId);
}
```
@see
MemoryPersistenceAdapter
@see
SyncCoordinator

Members:
- `commitBatch` — Commit an atomic batch at versions `baseVersion + 1` through
`baseVersion + versionOperationCounts.length`. Apply every member or none,
publish every member with its `batch` position, and acknowledge with the
last version. `SyncCoordinator` rejects a local transaction that needs more
than one version when the adapter does not implement this method.

##### `PersistenceBatchCommitRequest` — interface

```ts
export interface PersistenceBatchCommitRequest { readonly versionOperationCounts: readonly number[]; documentId: string; baseVersion: number; clientMutationId: string; readonly operations: readonly DocumentOp[]; signal?: AbortSignal; }
```

Cancellable commit of one atomic batch that spans several server versions.

Members:
- `versionOperationCounts` — Present only when the operations are too large for one server version.
Each entry is the operation count of one consecutive version of an atomic
batch, in order; the counts add up to `operations.length`. A server
applies and publishes all of these versions, or none of them.

##### `PersistenceCommitRequest` — interface

```ts
export interface PersistenceCommitRequest { signal?: AbortSignal; documentId: string; baseVersion: number; clientMutationId: string; readonly operations: readonly DocumentOp[]; readonly versionOperationCounts?: readonly number[]; }
```

Cancellable pending commit submitted to a persistence adapter.

Members:
- `versionOperationCounts` — Present only when the operations are too large for one server version.
Each entry is the operation count of one consecutive version of an atomic
batch, in order; the counts add up to `operations.length`. A server
applies and publishes all of these versions, or none of them.

##### `PersistenceCommitResponse` — type

```ts
export type PersistenceCommitResponse = | { status: "applied"; version: number; clientMutationId: string } | { status: "duplicate"; version: number; clientMutationId: string } | { status: "conflict"; currentVersion: number; operationsSinceBase?: readonly VersionedOperation[]; snapshot?: WorkbookSnapshot; };
```

Applied, duplicate, or conflict acknowledgement from persistence. `applied`
confirms the submitted operations unchanged; normalization must conflict.

##### `PersistenceError` — class

```ts
class PersistenceError extends SheetwriteError { constructor(code: PersistenceErrorCode, message: string, options?: ErrorOptions); name: "PersistenceError" }
```

Typed failure raised by persistence and synchronization flows.

##### `PersistenceErrorCode` — type

```ts
export type PersistenceErrorCode = | "aborted" | "invalid-snapshot" | "resource-limit" | "not-found" | "commit-rejected";
```

Stable category for a persistence failure.

##### `PivotAggregation` — type

```ts
export type PivotAggregation = | "SUM" | "COUNT" | "AVERAGE" | "MIN" | "MAX" | "COUNTA" | "DISTINCTCOUNT";
```

Aggregation applied to one value field. Semantics match PIVOTBY's aggregations.

##### `PivotDefinition` — interface

```ts
export interface PivotDefinition { id: string; name: string; source: PivotSource; anchor: { row: number; col: number }; rows: number[]; columns: number[]; values: PivotValueField[]; filters?: PivotFilter[]; sort?: PivotSort[]; rowTotals?: boolean; columnTotals?: boolean; subtotals?: boolean; layout?: PivotLayout; savedOutput?: { rows: number; cols: number; cells: CellScalar[] }; }
```

Serializable pivot-table definition, owned by the sheet that holds its
anchor. The output starts at `anchor` and spills right and down.

Members:
- `anchor` — Top-left output cell on the owning sheet. Deleting the anchor's row or
column keeps the pivot and moves the anchor to the first surviving cell
at the deletion position.
- `columns` — Source field indices that group the output columns, outermost first.
- `columnTotals` — Grand-total column at the right (PIVOTBY `col_total_depth`; OOXML
`rowGrandTotals`). Default `true`.
- `filters` — Keep-lists that limit which source rows contribute; at most one per field.
- `id` — Stable identity, unique in the workbook.
- `layout` — Default `"compact"`.
- `name` — User-facing caption.
- `rows` — Source field indices that group the output rows, outermost first.
- `rowTotals` — Grand-total row at the bottom (PIVOTBY `row_total_depth`; OOXML
`colGrandTotals`). Default `true`.
- `savedOutput` — Output cells a file saved for this pivot, row-major from `anchor`: for
example the cells Excel rendered. At most 1,000,000 cells, and
`cells.length` is `rows * cols`.

- The default engine computes no pivots, so it shows these values from
 the anchor. Formulas read them, and local writes into them are refused.
 A source cell, formula or spill in the rectangle shows `#SPILL!` at
 the anchor until it is cleared.
- The full engine ignores these values and recalculates the output.
- `setPivot` on the Grid or store removes them, because the saved
 values no longer match a changed definition. A row or column edit
 keeps them only when the output rectangle moves without a change;
 an edit inside the rectangle removes them.
- Snapshots, sync and XLSX export keep them on every engine.
- `sort` — Label order of grouped fields; each key names a field that groups its axis.
- `source` — Data the pivot summarizes.
- `subtotals` — Subtotal rows and columns for each outer group of a multi-field axis. Default `true`.
- `values` — Aggregated fields, in output order.

##### `PivotFieldType` — type

```ts
export type PivotFieldType = "number" | "text" | "boolean" | "mixed" | "blank";
```

Inferred type of one source field from its data rows.

##### `PivotFilter` — interface

```ts
export interface PivotFilter { field: number; values: CellScalar[]; }
```

Keep-list filter: only source rows whose `field` value is in `values` contribute.

##### `PivotLayout` — type

```ts
export type PivotLayout = "compact" | "tabular";
```

Layout of row labels: one indented label column, or one label column per row field.

##### `PivotResultView` — interface

```ts
export interface PivotResultView { status: "ok" | "error" | "unavailable" | "saved"; error?: string; anchor: CellAddress; rows: number; cols: number; headerRows: number; labelCols: number; cells: CellScalar[]; }
```

Plain-JSON view of one pivot's output, for the field list and other UI.

- `ok`: the output occupies `rows` x `cols` cells from `anchor`; `cells`
 holds their values row-major. The first `headerRows` rows hold column
 labels and the first `labelCols` columns hold row labels.
- `error`: the anchor shows `error` (for example `#SPILL!` or `#REF!`)
 and `cells` is empty.
- `unavailable`: the loaded engine computes no pivots (the default
 engine) and the pivot has no saved output. The definition is still
 kept, saved and synchronized.
- `saved`: the default engine shows `savedOutput`, which a file saved;
 `cells` holds those values and `headerRows`/`labelCols` are 0.

##### `PivotSort` — interface

```ts
export interface PivotSort { axis: "rows" | "columns"; field: number; descending: boolean; }
```

Sort of one axis field by its labels. Fields without a sort key sort ascending.

##### `PivotSource` — type

```ts
export type PivotSource = | { range: Range; invalid?: true } | { table: WorkbookTableId; invalid?: true };
```

Data a pivot summarizes.

- A range source includes its header row: the first range row names the
 fields, and field `i` is the column `range.start.col + i`.
- A table source names a workbook table by its stable `WorkbookTable.id`.
 Field `i` is table column `i`; header and totals rows are excluded.

When the source disappears (its sheet, its table, or every source row or
column is deleted), core sets `invalid: true` and keeps the reference
unchanged. The engine then shows `#REF!` at the anchor.

##### `PivotSourceField` — interface

```ts
export interface PivotSourceField { index: number; header: string; type: PivotFieldType; }
```

One source field offered by the field list.

Members:
- `header` — Field name, from the source header row or table column.
- `index` — Source field index, as used by `rows`, `columns`, `values` and `filters`.
- `type` — Type inferred from the field's data rows.

##### `PivotValueField` — interface

```ts
export interface PivotValueField { field: number; aggregation: PivotAggregation; name?: string; }
```

One aggregated value field. `name` replaces the default caption.

Members:
- `aggregation` — How the field's values in each output cell combine.
- `field` — Source field index that the value aggregates.
- `name` — Custom caption; without it the output shows the default caption.

##### `PresenceCoordinatorOptions` — interface

```ts

```

Identity, privacy, and timing options for presence coordination.

Members:
- `heartbeatMs` — Publish/prune interval in milliseconds; defaults to 15,000. Use 0 to disable the timer.
- `maxActors` — Remote actors retained at once; defaults to 32 and is clamped to at least 1.
- `maxRangesPerActor` — Selection ranges sent or accepted per actor; defaults to 8 and is clamped to at least 1.
- `timeoutMs` — Idle receipt time before a remote actor expires; defaults to 45,000 milliseconds.

##### `RebaseConflict` — interface


Reason and affected operations for an unsafe document rebase.

##### `RebaseConflictCode` — type

```ts
export type RebaseConflictCode = | "overlapping-edit" | "sheet-removed" | "sheet-lifecycle" | "formula-structural" | "structural-overlap" | "unsupported-structural";
```

Stable conservative-rebase conflict category.

##### `rebaseDocumentOperations` — function

```ts
(localOperations: readonly DocumentOp[], remoteOperations: readonly DocumentOp[]): DocumentRebaseResult
```

Conservative server-ordered rebase for pending offline work. Non-overlapping
literal edits are shifted across row/column insertion and deletion. Ambiguous
formula, overlapping, sheet-lifecycle, and move cases become explicit
conflicts instead of lossy guesses. This is the collaboration design gate;
no CRDT dependency is required for the supported cases.

Each local operation is written after the local operations before it, and
each remote operation after the remote operations before it. A remote
operation is therefore carried forward through the local sequence: before it
is compared with local operation k, it is moved past local operations 0..k-1.

##### `REF_CYCLE` — variable

```ts
"#CYCLE!"
```

Sentinel shown for a reference that participates in a cycle.

##### `releaseEngineMemory` — function

```ts
(): Promise<EngineMemoryReleaseReport>
```

Move all live stores into a fresh WASM instance. Call explicitly while idle;
the main-thread pause scales with resident data and compact undo history.
Preparation failures leave every live store and the selected instance unchanged.
A larger replacement is discarded; the report then has zero migrated stores.
@example
```ts
import { initSheetwrite, releaseEngineMemory } from "@sheetwrite/core";

await initSheetwrite();
// Run between user actions, not in an input or render callback.
const report = await releaseEngineMemory();
document.body.dataset.engineBytes = String(report.wasmBytesAfter);
```
@see
EngineMemoryReleaseReport

Members:

##### `resolveChartView` — function

```ts
(store: Store, sheet: SheetId, id: string): ChartView | null
```

Resolve one chart to plain data the renderer draws without reading cells.
Values that are not numbers (text, booleans, errors, empty cells) become
`null`. Each series range costs one bulk window read of at most
`MAX_CHART_POINTS` cells. Returns `null` when the chart does not exist.

Call it after a {@link subscribeChartChanges} event names the chart, not per frame.

##### `RowBridge` — class

```ts
class RowBridge { constructor<Id extends RowBridgeId = RowBridgeId, Row extends Record<string, CellScalar> = Record<string, CellScalar>>(options: RowBridgeOptions<Row, Id>); columnKeys: (sheet?: SheetId) => readonly string[]; project: (event: ChangeEvent, requestedOperations?: readonly DocumentOp[], transactionId?: string) => RowBridgeProjection<Id>; reconcile: (input: RowBridgeReconciliationInput<Id>) => RowBridgeProjection<Id>; rowIds: (sheet?: SheetId) => readonly (Id | null)[] }
```

Projects canonical document transactions into host-owned row changes.

The bridge only owns compact data-space identity arrays. It never writes to
`defaultRows`, never renders, and never creates a second document store.

Members:
- `columnKeys` — Current semantic column keys in canonical column order.
- `project` — Project an applied Grid change as an accepted, transformed, or remote result.
- `reconcile` — Reconcile a canonical transaction response without synchronizing host rows implicitly.
- `rowIds` — Current data-space row identities; visual sort and filters do not affect this order.

##### `RowBridgeCell` — interface


A cell effect with semantic column and host row identity.

##### `RuntimeResourcePhaseDelta` — interface

##### `SearchOptions` — interface

```ts
export interface SearchOptions { matchCase?: boolean; wholeCell?: boolean; sheet?: SheetId; columns?: number[]; }
```

Case, whole-cell, sheet, and column constraints for grid search.

Members:
- `columns` — Restrict to these column indices (defaults to all columns).
- `matchCase` — Case-sensitive match (default false).
- `sheet` — Restrict to a sheet (defaults to the active sheet).
- `wholeCell` — Match only when the whole cell text equals the query (default false: substring).

##### `SearchResult` — interface


Ordered matches and active index produced by a grid search.

Members:
- `active` — Index of the active match within `matches`, or -1 when there are none.
- `matches` — Matching cells in row-major order.
- `query` — Query string retained for navigation and subsequent replacement.

calendar fields are stable regardless of the host time zone.

##### `Sheet` — interface

```ts
export interface Sheet { id: SheetId; name: string; visibility?: SheetVisibility; columns: Column[]; rowCount: number; rowHeights?: Map<number, number>; hiddenRows?: Set<number>; rowGroups?: RowGroup[]; conditionalFormats?: ConditionalFormatRule[]; hyperlinks?: CellHyperlink[]; validationRules?: DataValidationRule[]; protectedRanges?: ProtectedRange[]; notes?: CellNote[]; sortKeys?: SortKey[]; filters?: Array<[col: number, filter: ColumnFilter]>; merges?: MergeRange[]; frozenRows?: number; frozenCols?: number; tables?: WorkbookTable[]; charts?: ChartDefinition[]; pivots?: PivotDefinition[]; }
```

Workbook sheet schema used when creating a live grid.

Members:
- `charts` — Charts anchored to this sheet; series sources use stable sheet IDs.
- `columns` — Ordered schema; array positions are the zero-based column coordinates.
- `conditionalFormats` — Conditional styles folded into the bulk render-window style dictionary.
- `filters` — Persisted column filters as JSON-safe index/value tuples.
- `frozenCols` — Leading columns pinned left of the scrolling body (0/undefined = none).
- `frozenRows` — Leading view rows pinned above the scrolling body (0/undefined = none).
- `hiddenRows` — Persisted hidden data rows; runtime form is sparse and non-JSON.
- `hyperlinks` — Stable, serializable range hyperlinks; external URLs pass the shared safety policy.
- `id` — Stable identifier, unique within the workbook and used by every cell address.
- `merges` — Persisted merged-cell regions; covered cells render/export from the anchor.
- `name` — User-facing sheet name shown in tabs and workbook exports.
- `notes` — Simple cell notes. Discussion threads live outside the document model.
- `pivots` — Pivot tables anchored on this sheet; IDs are unique in the workbook.
- `protectedRanges` — Client-side protected-range policy metadata; never server authorization.
- `rowCount` — Row count for both in-memory and datasource-backed sheets.
- `rowGroups` — Persisted collapsible row groups.
- `rowHeights` — Sparse per-row height overrides; default comes from the theme.
- `sortKeys` — Persisted sort keys for the sheet's view.
- `tables` — Native workbook tables anchored to this stable worksheet identity.
- `validationRules` — Serializable data-entry rules evaluated at the local mutation barrier.
- `visibility` — Hidden worksheets remain addressable but are omitted from the tab strip.

```ts

```

Stable identifier used to address a workbook sheet.

##### `SheetwriteStore` — class

```ts
class SheetwriteStore implements Store { constructor(workbook: Workbook, data?: ColumnarData, options?: SheetwriteStoreOptions); acknowledgeOperations: (operations: readonly DocumentOp[], storageRevision?: bigint) => void; aggregate: (sheet: SheetId, col: number, op: AggregateOp) => number; applyTransaction: (tx: Transaction, reasonOrOptions?: CommitReason | TransactionApplicationOptions) => ApplyTransactionResult; areColumnsFullyLoaded: (sheet: SheetId, startRow: number, endRow: number, columns: readonly number[]) => boolean; canApplyLocally: (patch: DocumentOp) => boolean; captureRangeHistory: (input: Range) => CompactRangeHistory | null; clearView: (sheet: SheetId) => void; columnFilters: (sheet: SheetId) => ReadonlyMap<number, ColumnFilter>; dataEdge: (sheet: SheetId, row: number, col: number, dRow: number, dCol: number) => number; dataRowAt: (sheet: SheetId, viewRow: number) => number; dispose: () => void; distinctValues: (sheet: SheetId, col: number, limit?: number) => CellScalar[]; ensureColumns: (sheet: SheetId, columns: readonly Column[]) => void; exportSnapshot: () => WorkbookSnapshot; filterBy: (sheet: SheetId, col: number, needle: string) => void; getCell: (addr: CellAddress) => ResolvedCell; getCellLoadState: (addr: CellAddress) => CellLoadState; getClipboardWindow: (sheet: SheetId, viewRows: { start: number; end: number; }, cols: readonly number[]) => ClipboardWindowView; getDataWindow: (sheet: SheetId, rows: { start: number; end: number; }, cols: readonly number[]) => VisibleWindowView; getFormula: (addr: CellAddress) => string | null; getFormulaMatrixResourcePeak: () => TransientResourcePeak; getPagedStats: (sheet: SheetId) => PagedStoreStats; getPivotFields: (sheet: SheetId, id: string) => PivotSourceField[]; getPivotResult: (sheet: SheetId, id: string) => PivotResultView | null; getPivots: (sheet?: SheetId) => PivotDefinition[]; getRangeMutationAllocationStats: () => RangeMutationAllocationStats; getRefTarget: (addr: CellAddress) => CellAddress | null; getRuntimeResourceSnapshot: (operation: RuntimeResourceOperation, phase: RuntimeResourcePhase, runtime?: RuntimeMemoryObservation) => RuntimeResourceSnapshot; getSpillAnchor: (addr: CellAddress) => CellAddress | null; getVisibleWindow: (sheet: SheetId, rows: { start: number; end: number; }, cols: readonly number[]) => VisibleWindowView; getWorkbook: () => Workbook; groupRows: (sheet: SheetId, start: number, end: number) => void; hasView: (sheet: SheetId) => boolean; hiddenRows: (sheet: SheetId) => number[]; hideRows: (sheet: SheetId, rows: readonly number[]) => void; isPaged: (sheet: SheetId) => boolean; isRangeFullyLoaded: (input: Range) => boolean; loadPage: (sheet: SheetId, start: number, columns: readonly DataSourceColumnBand[], rows: readonly RowData[], protect?: (addr: CellAddress) => boolean) => void; on: (_evt: "change", fn: ChangeListener) => () => void; queryCapability: (sheet: SheetId) => QueryCapability; recalculateVolatile: (now?: Date) => void; removePivot: (id: string, sheet?: SheetId) => ApplyTransactionResult; removeSheetFormulaIdentity: (sheet: SheetId) => boolean; renameSheetFormulaIdentity: (sheet: SheetId, name: string) => boolean; resetFormulaMatrixResourcePeak: () => void; resetRangeMutationAllocationStats: () => void; resetRuntimeResourceAccounting: () => void; rowGroups: (sheet: SheetId) => readonly RowGroup[]; searchCells: (sheet: SheetId, query: string, opts?: { matchCase?: boolean; wholeCell?: boolean; columns?: number[]; }) => CellAddress[]; searchCellsFlat: (sheet: SheetId, query: string, opts?: { matchCase?: boolean; wholeCell?: boolean; columns?: number[]; }) => Uint32Array; setColumnFilter: (sheet: SheetId, col: number, filter: ColumnFilter | null) => void; setDetailedChangeCapture: (enabled: boolean) => void; setGroupCollapsed: (sheet: SheetId, start: number, collapsed: boolean) => void; setPivot: (pivot: PivotDefinition, sheet?: SheetId) => ApplyTransactionResult; setProtectionResolver: (resolver: ProtectionResolver | undefined, mode?: MutationPolicyMode) => void; showRows: (sheet: SheetId, rows?: readonly number[]) => void; sortBy: (sheet: SheetId, col: number, ascending: boolean) => void; sortByMulti: (sheet: SheetId, keys: readonly SortKey[]) => void; ungroupRows: (sheet: SheetId, start: number, end: number) => void; viewRowCount: (sheet: SheetId) => number; viewRowOf: (sheet: SheetId, dataRow: number) => number | null; withResourceOperation: <T>(operation: RuntimeResourceOperation, run: () => T) => T; static fromSnapshot: (input: unknown, options?: SheetwriteStoreOptions) => SheetwriteStore }
```

Stable public facade and the sole transaction, epoch, policy, and event barrier.
@example
```ts
import { initSheetwrite, SheetwriteStore, type Workbook } from "@sheetwrite/core";

async function total(workbook: Workbook) {
 await initSheetwrite();
 const store = new SheetwriteStore(workbook);
 try {
 return store.aggregate(workbook.activeSheet, 0, "sum");
 } finally {
 store.dispose();
 }
}
```
@see
Store.aggregate
@see
createGrid

Members:
- `acknowledgeOperations` — Release sparse paged edits after server acknowledgement.
- `aggregate` — Aggregate one column. Datasource-backed sheets must be fully loaded.
@example
```ts
import type { SheetwriteStore, SheetId } from "@sheetwrite/core";

function totals(store: SheetwriteStore, sheet: SheetId) {
 return { total: store.aggregate(sheet, 0, "sum"), average: store.aggregate(sheet, 0, "avg") };
}
```
@see
AggregateOp
- `applyTransaction` — Apply a low-level storage transaction.

This bypasses Grid read-only checks and Grid undo/redo history. Use
`Grid.applyTransaction` for normal host-driven edits.
Queued and flushed at a barrier — never reentrant.
- `ensureColumns` — Ensure a sheet can address at least `columns.length` columns without
producing user changes or dirty patches. Used for presentation padding.
- `exportSnapshot` — Deterministic, JSON-safe authoritative runtime document.
- `getCell` — Single-cell read for interactions, API reads, and tests.
NOT for the render hot path — renderers use `getVisibleWindow`.
- `getCellLoadState` — Loaded/empty/local state; dense stores always return a loaded state.
- `getClipboardWindow` — Optional packed clipboard read. Custom stores may omit it; the controller
preserves the per-cell Store fallback contract.
- `getDataWindow` — Optional packed canonical data-row window used by file export. Unlike
`getVisibleWindow`, sort/filter state never remaps `rows`.
- `getFormula` — Formula source at `addr`, or null when the cell is not a formula.
- `getPivotFields` — Source fields of one pivot; empty on the default engine or for an unknown pivot.
- `getPivotResult` — Plain-JSON output of one pivot. The default engine reports the saved
output (`saved`), or `unavailable` without one. Null when `sheet` holds
no pivot with `id`.
- `getPivots` — Clones of the pivot definitions on `sheet`, or on every sheet; readable without the engine.
- `getRefTarget` — Plain-reference target at `addr`, or null when the cell is not a ref.
- `getSpillAnchor` — Owning dynamic-array formula cell, or null when `addr` is not spilled.
- `getVisibleWindow` — Bulk read of a visible window; the only read a renderer should use per frame.
- `queryCapability` — Explicit partial-data state for paged datasource stores.
- `recalculateVolatile` — Recompute volatile formulas (`TODAY`, `NOW`, `RAND`, `RANDBETWEEN`, `OFFSET`,
`INDIRECT`) from one captured instant. The supplied Date is interpreted as an absolute UTC instant.
Edits already recompute volatile formulas and read the clock once per
recalculation; this call uses `now` instead, until the next edit.
- `removePivot` — Remove a pivot; `sheet` defaults to the sheet that holds it.
- `setDetailedChangeCapture` — Opt in to per-cell before/after capture for packed and clear operations.
- `setPivot` — Insert or replace a pivot. `sheet` defaults to the sheet that holds the
pivot's ID, then to the active sheet. The pivot's `savedOutput` is
removed: saved values do not match a definition the caller changed.
- `setProtectionResolver` — Configure host-owned protected-range permissions. The resolver is synchronous
so every local mutation ingress shares one atomic commit barrier.
- `viewRowCount` — Displayed row count after any active sort/filter view.

##### `SheetwriteStoreOptions` — interface

```ts
export interface SheetwriteStoreOptions { snapshotResourceLimits?: Partial<SnapshotResourceLimits>; transactionResourceLimits?: Partial<TransactionResourceLimits>; storage?: "dense" | "paged"; chunkRows?: number; cacheBytes?: number; dirtyCellLimit?: number; referenceSimulationLimit?: number; protectionResolver?: ProtectionResolver; mutationPolicy?: MutationPolicyMode; }
```

Storage layout plus snapshot and transaction resource ceilings for one store.

Members:
- `cacheBytes` — Per-sheet clean-chunk budget; defaults to 32 MiB. Dirty and pinned chunks may exceed it.
- `chunkRows` — Paged row chunk size; defaults to 4,096 and is normalized to a power of two.
- `dirtyCellLimit` — Maximum sparse local edits retained outside the clean page cache. Defaults to 1,000,000 cells; further edits reject atomically.
- `referenceSimulationLimit` — Maximum clean references retained for exact multi-operation remove-sheet simulation.
- `snapshotResourceLimits` — Overrides canonical snapshot/workbook allocation ceilings before construction.
- `storage` — Storage engine; defaults to eager `dense` allocation.
- `transactionResourceLimits` — Overrides inclusive operation-count and encoded-byte ceilings for every transaction.

##### `shiftA1Refs` — function

```ts
(src: string, dRow: number, dCol: number): string
```

Shift relative A1 references in a formula by (dRow, dCol) — used when a
formula is filled into other cells. Absolute parts ($A, A$1) stay fixed, and
tokens preceded by an alphanumeric (function names, identifiers) are skipped.

##### `SnapshotResourceLimits` — interface

```ts
export interface SnapshotResourceLimits { maxSheets: number; maxRowsPerSheet: number; maxColumnsPerSheet: number; maxMetadataEntries: number; maxSerializedBytes: number; maxLogicalCellsPerSheet: number; maxDenseCells: number; }
```

Resource ceilings applied before snapshot normalization or store allocation.

Members:
- `maxColumnsPerSheet` — Columns in any sheet; defaults to 16,384.
- `maxDenseCells` — Aggregate cells allocated by dense storage; defaults to 5,000,000.
- `maxLogicalCellsPerSheet` — Logical row-by-column cells in any sheet; defaults to 4,294,967,295.
- `maxMetadataEntries` — Aggregate workbook/sheet metadata array entries; defaults to 1,000,000.
- `maxRowsPerSheet` — Rows in any sheet; defaults to 1,000,000.
- `maxSerializedBytes` — UTF-8 JSON bytes inspected while validating a snapshot; defaults to 64 MiB.
- `maxSheets` — Workbook sheets; defaults to 256.
